title.zh: 卷二十五 魏書二十五 辛毗楊阜高堂隆傳
title.en: Volume 25: Book of Wei 25 - Biographies of Xin Pi, Yang Fu, and Gaotang Long
title.raw: 卷二十五 魏書二十五 辛毗楊阜高堂隆傳 Volume 25: Book of Wei 25 - Biographies of Xin Pi, Yang Fu, and Gaotang Long

sentences.zh: 辛毗 楊阜 高堂隆

translations.literal: Xin Pi Yang Fu Gaotang Long.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Pi, Yang Fu, and Gaotang Long.

sentences.zh: 辛毗字佐治，潁川陽翟人也。

translations.literal: Xin Pi, courtesy name Zuozhi, was a man of Yangdi in Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Pi, whose courtesy name was Zuozhi, came from Yangdi in Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 其先建武中，自隴西東遷。

translations.literal: His ancestors in the Jianwu era moved east from Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jianwu reign, his forebears had migrated eastward out of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 毗隨兄評從袁紹。

translations.literal: Xin Pi followed elder brother Xin Ping in following Yuan Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Pi followed his elder brother Xin Ping into Yuan Shao's service.

sentences.zh: 太祖爲司空，辟毗，毗不得應命。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor being Minister of Works summoned Xin Pi; Xin Pi could not answer the summons.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao held the post of Minister of Works, he called Xin Pi to office, but Xin Pi was unable to accept the appointment.

sentences.zh: 及袁尚攻兄譚於平原，譚使毗詣太祖求和。

translations.literal: When Yuan Shang attacked elder brother Yuan Tan at Pingyuan, Tan sent Xin Pi to go to the Grand Progenitor to seek peace.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Shang besieged his older brother Yuan Tan at Pingyuan, Tan dispatched Xin Pi to Cao Cao to sue for peace.

sentences.zh: 〈《英雄記》曰：譚、尚戰於外門，譚軍敗奔北。

translations.literal: The Yingxiong ji says: Tan and Shang fought at the outer gate; Tan's army was defeated and fled north.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Heroes relates that Yuan Tan and Yuan Shang fought at the outer gate, Tan's force was routed, and he fled north.

sentences.zh: 郭圖說譚曰：「今將軍國小兵少，糧匱勢弱，顯甫之來，久則不敵。

translations.literal: Guo Tu persuaded Tan saying: "Now the general's state is small and troops few; provisions are exhausted and the situation weak; when Xianfu comes, if it is prolonged then you will not be a match."
translations.idiomatic: Guo Tu urged Yuan Tan: "Your domain is small, your soldiers few, your grain is running out, and your position is weak. When Shang arrives in force, a drawn-out fight will not favor you."

sentences.zh: 愚以爲可呼曹公來擊顯甫。

translations.literal: I foolishly think it is possible to call Lord Cao to come strike Xianfu.
translations.idiomatic: I would call Lord Cao in to strike Shang while you still can."

sentences.zh: 曹公至，必先攻鄴，顯甫還救。

translations.literal: When Lord Cao arrives, he will surely first attack Ye; Xianfu will return to save it.
translations.idiomatic: Once Cao Cao arrives, he will move on Ye first, and Shang will have to double back to relieve the city."

sentences.zh: 將軍引兵而西，自鄴以北皆可虜得。

translations.literal: The general leads troops west; from Ye northward all can be taken captive.
translations.idiomatic: You march west with your army, and everything north of Ye falls within your grasp."

sentences.zh: 若顯甫軍破，其兵奔亡，又可斂取以拒曹公。

translations.literal: If Xianfu's army is broken, his troops will flee in disorder, and again you can gather them in to resist Lord Cao.
translations.idiomatic: If Shang's host is shattered, his men will scatter, and you can round them up and turn them against Cao Cao."

sentences.zh: 曹公遠僑而來，糧餉不繼，必自逃去。

translations.literal: Lord Cao comes from afar as a sojourner; provisions will not continue; he will surely flee on his own.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao is campaigning far from home; his supply lines will not hold, and he will withdraw of his own accord."

sentences.zh: 比此之際，趙國以北皆我之有，亦足與曹公爲對矣。

translations.literal: At the time of this comparison, north of Zhao all will be ours; also sufficient to stand as match to Lord Cao.
translations.idiomatic: When that moment comes, everything north of Zhao will be yours, and you will be strong enough to face Cao Cao on even terms."

sentences.zh: 不然，不諧。

translations.literal: If not, not harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise the plan will not work."

sentences.zh: 」譚始不納，後遂從之。

translations.literal: " Tan at first did not accept; afterward then followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Tan refused at first, but in the end he adopted the advice.

sentences.zh: 問圖：「誰可使？

translations.literal: He asked Tu: "Who can be sent?
translations.idiomatic: He asked Guo Tu, "Whom can we send?

sentences.zh: 」圖荅：「辛佐治可。

translations.literal: " Tu answered: "Xin Zuozhi can."
translations.idiomatic: Guo Tu replied, "Xin Zuozhi is the man for it."

sentences.zh: 」譚遂遣毗詣太祖。〉

translations.literal: " Tan then sent Xin Pi to go to the Grand Progenitor.〉
translations.idiomatic: Tan thereupon sent Xin Pi to Cao Cao."

sentences.zh: 太祖將征荊州，次于西平。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor was about to campaign against Jingzhou and halted at Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao was on the point of marching against Jingzhou and had encamped at Xiping.

sentences.zh: 毗見太祖致譚意，太祖大恱。

translations.literal: Xin Pi saw the Grand Progenitor and conveyed Tan's intent; the Grand Progenitor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When Xin Pi laid out Tan's proposal before Cao Cao, Cao Cao was delighted.

sentences.zh: 後數日，更欲先平荊州，使譚、尚自相弊。

translations.literal: After several days, he again wished first to pacify Jingzhou, causing Tan and Shang mutually to exhaust each other.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later he again favored striking Jingzhou first and letting Tan and Shang wear one another down.

sentences.zh: 他日置酒，毗望太祖色，知有變，以語郭嘉。

translations.literal: Another day when wine was set out, Xin Pi observed the Grand Progenitor's expression, knew there was a change, and told Guo Jia.
translations.idiomatic: At a later banquet Xin Pi read a shift in Cao Cao's mood, sensed that the plan was changing, and spoke of it to Guo Jia.

sentences.zh: 嘉白太祖，太祖謂毗曰：「譚可信？

translations.literal: Jia reported to the Grand Progenitor; the Grand Progenitor said to Xin Pi: "Can Tan be trusted?
translations.idiomatic: Guo Jia relayed this to Cao Cao, who asked Xin Pi, "Can we trust Tan?

sentences.zh: 尚必可克不？

translations.literal: Shang surely can be overcome or not?
translations.idiomatic: And can Shang really be defeated?"

sentences.zh: 」毗對曰：「明公無問信與詐也，直當論其勢耳。

translations.literal: " Xin Pi replied: "The enlightened lord need not ask about trust and deceit; directly ought to discuss their situation only."
translations.idiomatic: Xin Pi answered, "You need not trouble yourself with whether he is sincere. Consider only how the balance of power lies."

sentences.zh: 袁氏本兄弟相伐，非謂他人能閒其間，乃謂天下可定於己也。

translations.literal: The Yuan clan fundamentally brothers attacking each other; it is not that others can put space between them; rather they say the realm can be settled in themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuans are tearing one another apart as brothers; they do not imagine outsiders can drive a wedge between them—they imagine they can settle the empire on their own."

sentences.zh: 今一旦求救於明公，此可知也。

translations.literal: Now in one morning seeking rescue from the enlightened lord, this can be known.
translations.idiomatic: That they should now beg you for help in a single day tells you all you need to know."

sentences.zh: 顯甫見顯思困而不能取，此力竭也。

translations.literal: Xianfu sees Xiansi trapped yet cannot take him; this is strength exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Shang has Tan cornered yet cannot finish him—that is exhaustion of military strength."

sentences.zh: 兵革敗於外，謀臣誅於內，兄弟讒鬩，國分爲二；

translations.literal: Weapons defeated abroad, counsellors executed within, brothers slanderously quarreling, the state split in two;
translations.idiomatic: Their armies have met defeat in the field, their strategists have been put to death at court, the brothers turn on each other, and the domain is cut in two;

sentences.zh: 連年戰伐，而介冑生蟣蝨，加以旱蝗，饑饉並臻，國無囷倉，行無裹糧，天災應於上，人事困於下，民無愚智，皆知土崩瓦解，此乃天亡尚之時也。

translations.literal: Years linked in warfare, yet between armor and helmet lice are born; added to drought and locusts, famine both arrive together; the state has no granary, marching has no wrapped grain; heaven's disasters respond above, human affairs are trapped below; the people without foolish and wise, all know earth collapse tile disintegration; this then is the time of heaven destroying Shang.
translations.idiomatic: Year after year of campaigning has left lice breeding in the soldiers' mail; drought and locusts have piled on, and famine stalks the land. Granaries stand empty, and men march without rations in their packs. Portents of calamity gather above while human affairs founder below. High and low alike see the edifice crumbling—this is the moment Heaven has marked for Shang's fall."

sentences.zh: 兵法稱有石城湯池帶甲百萬而無粟者，不能守也。

translations.literal: The art of war states: having stone walls moat like boiling water belt armor a million yet without grain, cannot defend.
translations.idiomatic: The military classics say that stone ramparts and moats like seething cauldrons, even with a million armored men, cannot be held if there is no grain."

sentences.zh: 今往攻鄴，尚不還救，即不能自守。

translations.literal: Now going to attack Ye, if Shang does not return to save, then cannot defend himself.
translations.idiomatic: Strike Ye now: if Shang does not turn back to relieve it, he cannot hold the city on his own."

sentences.zh: 還救，即譚踵其後。

translations.literal: If he returns to save, then Tan follows at his heels.
translations.idiomatic: If he does turn back, Tan will be on his heels."

sentences.zh: 以明公之威，應困窮之敵，擊疲弊之寇，無異迅風之振秋葉矣。

translations.literal: By the enlightened lord's might, responding to trapped exhausted enemy, striking weary worn-out bandits, no different from swift wind's shaking autumn leaves.
translations.idiomatic: With your prestige, falling on an enemy already cornered and a host already spent, you will scatter them like a gale stripping the autumn woods."

sentences.zh: 天以袁尚與明公，明公不取而伐荊州。

translations.literal: Heaven takes Yuan Shang and gives him to the enlightened lord; the enlightened lord does not take him but campaigns against Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has handed you Yuan Shang on favorable terms, yet you would ignore him and march on Jingzhou instead."

sentences.zh: 荊州豐樂，國未有釁。

translations.literal: Jingzhou abundant happy; the state has not yet quarrel.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhou is rich and at peace, and you have no quarrel with its lords."

sentences.zh: 仲虺有言：『取亂侮亡。

translations.literal: Zhonghui had words: 'Take chaos despise perishing.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui put it thus: 'Seize the moment when a rival is in turmoil; press the attack when he is on the verge of collapse.'

sentences.zh: 』方今二袁不務遠略而內相圖，可謂亂矣；

translations.literal: ' Now the two Yuans do not pursue far strategy but internally plot against each other; can be called chaos;
translations.idiomatic: The two Yuans neglect long-range strategy and scheme against each other at home—that is what 'chaos' means;

sentences.zh: 居者無食，行者無糧，可謂亡矣。

translations.literal: Dwellers have no food, walkers have no grain; can be called perishing.
translations.idiomatic: those who stay starve, and those who march have no grain—that is what 'perishing' means.

sentences.zh: 朝不謀夕，民命靡繼，而不綏之，欲待他年；

translations.literal: Morning does not plan evening; people's lives without continuation; yet not comforting them, wishing to wait other years;
translations.idiomatic: They cannot plan from dawn to dusk; the people's lives hang by a thread. If you do not rescue them now and put off action for some later year,

sentences.zh: 他年或登，又自知亡而改脩厥德，失所以用兵之要矣。

translations.literal: Other years perhaps ascend, again themselves knowing perishing and changing cultivating their virtue; loses what uses troops' essentials.
translations.idiomatic: they may rally, realize their peril, and mend their rule—then you will have missed the whole point of wielding an army."

sentences.zh: 今因其請救而撫之，利莫大焉。

translations.literal: Now because they request rescue and you comfort them, benefit none greater.
translations.idiomatic: To answer their plea for aid and bring them under your wing now is the greatest opportunity you could ask for."

sentences.zh: 且四方之寇，莫大於河北；

translations.literal: Moreover of enemies in the four quarters, none greater than north of the River;
translations.idiomatic: Among the powers that threaten you from every side, none outweighs what lies north of the Yellow River;

sentences.zh: 河北平，則六軍盛而天下震。

translations.literal: When north of the River is pacified, then the six armies flourish and the realm trembles.
translations.idiomatic: pacify the north, and the imperial host will stand at full strength while the realm trembles at your approach."

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「善。

translations.literal: " The Grand Progenitor said: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao said, "Well said."

sentences.zh: 」乃許譚平，次于黎陽。

translations.literal: " Then granted Tan peace and halted at Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: He agreed to make peace with Tan and moved his camp to Liyang.

sentences.zh: 明年攻鄴，克之，表毗爲議郎。

translations.literal: The next year attacked Ye, overcame it, memorialized Xin Pi as Gentleman Consultant.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he took Ye by storm and recommended Xin Pi for appointment as a Gentleman Consultant.

sentences.zh: 乆之，太祖遣都護曹洪平下辯，使毗與曹休參之，令曰：「昔高祖貪財好色，而良、平匡其過失。

translations.literal: After a long time, the Grand Progenitor sent Chief Protector Cao Hong to pacify Xiabian, had Xin Pi and Cao Xiu join in it, order saying: "Of old the High Ancestor was greedy for wealth fond of women, yet Liang and Ping corrected his faults.
translations.idiomatic: Some time later Cao Cao sent Chief Protector Cao Hong to reduce Xiabian and attached Xin Pi and Cao Xiu to the expedition with these instructions: "The Han founder loved wealth and women, yet Zhang Liang and Chen Ping set his missteps right.

sentences.zh: 今佐治、文烈憂不輕矣。

translations.literal: Now Zuozhi and Wenlie's worries are not light."
translations.idiomatic: Zuozhi and Wenlie now bear a heavy burden of care."

sentences.zh: 」軍還，爲丞相長史。

translations.literal: " When the army returned, he became Chief Clerk of the Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: When the force returned, Xin Pi was appointed chief clerk of the chancellery.

sentences.zh: 文帝踐阼，遷侍中，賜爵關內侯。

translations.literal: Wendi ascended the throne, was promoted Palace Attendant, granted title secondary marquis within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen took the throne, Xin Pi rose to palace attendant and received the rank of secondary marquis within the passes.

sentences.zh: 時議改正朔。

translations.literal: At the time discussed changing the calendar's first month.
translations.idiomatic: The court was debating a change to the calendar's inaugural month.

sentences.zh: 毗以魏氏遵舜、禹之統，應天順民；

translations.literal: Xin Pi held that the Wei house followed Shun and Yu's line, responded to Heaven obeyed the people;
translations.idiomatic: Xin Pi argued that the Wei house had inherited the legitimate line of Shun and Yu and had answered both Heaven and the people;

sentences.zh: 至於湯、武，以戰伐定天下，乃改正朔。

translations.literal: As for Tang and Wu, by warfare settled the realm, then changed the calendar's first month.
translations.idiomatic: Tang of Shang and King Wu won the realm by arms and only then altered the calendar.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰「行夏之時」，左氏傳曰「夏數爲得天正」，何必期於相反。

translations.literal: Confucius said 'practice Xia's seasons'; Zuo's Commentary says 'Xia's reckoning is obtaining Heaven's correct'; why must expect mutually opposite.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, 'I would follow the calendar of the Xia,' and the Zuo commentary calls the Xia reckoning 'the count that accords with Heaven's true month'—there is no need to insist on reversing it.

sentences.zh: 帝善而從之。

translations.literal: The emperor deemed good and followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the argument and dropped the proposal.

sentences.zh: 帝欲徙冀州士家十萬戶實河南。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to move Ji Province garrison families hundred thousand households to fill Henan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor proposed resettling a hundred thousand garrison households from Ji Province south into the Henan heartland.

sentences.zh: 時連蝗民饑，群司以爲不可，而帝意甚盛。

translations.literal: At the time successive locusts people hungry; all offices thought not possible, yet the emperor's intent very strong.
translations.idiomatic: Locusts had come in waves and the people were starving; every ministry advised against the move, but the emperor's resolve only hardened.

sentences.zh: 毗與朝臣俱求見，帝知其欲諫，作色以見之，皆莫敢言。

translations.literal: Xin Pi with court ministers together requested audience; the emperor knew they wished to remonstrate, put on color to receive them, all none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Pi went in with the senior ministers to seek an audience. Foreseeing a remonstrance, the emperor received them with a dark countenance, and no one dared speak.

sentences.zh: 毗曰：「陛下欲徙士家，其計安出：」帝曰：「卿謂我徙之非邪？

translations.literal: Xin Pi said: "Your Majesty wishes to move garrison families; from where does this plan emerge:" The emperor said: "You think my moving them is wrong?"
translations.idiomatic: Xin Pi said, "If you mean to uproot the garrison families, what is the rationale?" The emperor shot back, "You think the resettlement is a mistake?"

sentences.zh: 」毗曰：「誠以爲非也。

translations.literal: " Xin Pi said: "Truly I think it is wrong."
translations.idiomatic: Xin Pi replied, "I believe it is."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「吾不與卿共議也。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "I will not with you jointly discuss."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Then I have nothing further to discuss with you."

sentences.zh: 」毗曰：「陛下不以臣不肖，置之左右，廁之謀議之官，安得不與臣議邪！

translations.literal: " Xin Pi said: "Your Majesty not because I am unworthy, placed me left right, placed me among counsel-discussion officials, how can not discuss with me!"
translations.idiomatic: Xin Pi answered, "You appointed me to your side despite my mediocrity and gave me a seat among your advisers—how can you refuse to hear me out?"

sentences.zh: 臣所言非私，乃社稷之慮也，安得怒臣！

translations.literal: What your servant speaks is not private; is altars of soil and grain's concern; how can be angry at your servant!
translations.idiomatic: I speak not for myself but for the altars of state—surely that is no cause for anger!"

sentences.zh: 」帝不荅，起入內；

translations.literal: " The emperor did not answer, rose and entered within;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made no reply, rose, and withdrew to the inner chambers;

sentences.zh: 毗隨而引其裾，帝遂奮衣不還，良乆乃出，曰：「佐治，卿持我何太急邪？

translations.literal: Xin Pi followed and pulled his robe skirt; the emperor then flung garment not returning; long time then came out, saying: "Zuozhi, you hold me how too urgent?"
translations.idiomatic: Xin Pi followed, seized the hem of his robe, and the emperor shook him off and stayed away a long while before reappearing. "Zuozhi," he said, "why are you tugging at me so fiercely?"

sentences.zh: 」毗曰：「今徙，旣失民心，又無以食也。

translations.literal: " Xin Pi said: "Now moving, already lose people's hearts, again have nothing by which to eat."
translations.idiomatic: Xin Pi said, "If you press the move now, you forfeit the people's trust and leave them nothing to eat."

sentences.zh: 」帝遂徙其半。

translations.literal: " The emperor then moved half of them.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the emperor relocated only half the households he had first intended.

sentences.zh: 嘗從帝射雉，帝曰：「射雉樂哉！

translations.literal: Once followed the emperor shooting pheasants; the emperor said: "Shooting pheasants joyful!"
translations.idiomatic: On an outing when he accompanied the emperor pheasant hunting, the emperor exclaimed, "There is real sport in this!"

sentences.zh: 」毗曰：「於陛下甚樂，而於羣下甚苦。

translations.literal: " Xin Pi said: "For your Majesty very joyful; yet for the host of subordinates very bitter."
translations.idiomatic: Xin Pi replied, "It is pleasure for Your Majesty, but torment for your ministers."

sentences.zh: 」帝默然，後遂爲之稀出。

translations.literal: " The emperor was silent; afterward then for this rarely went out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fell silent, and afterward he seldom went out on such hunts again.

sentences.zh: 上軍大將軍曹真征朱然于江陵，毗行軍師。

translations.literal: Senior General Cao Zhen campaigned against Zhu Ran at Jiangling; Xin Pi acted Army Adviser.
translations.idiomatic: When Senior General Cao Zhen led a punitive expedition against Zhu Ran at Jiangling, Xin Pi served as army adviser on the campaign.

sentences.zh: 還，封廣平亭侯。

translations.literal: Returned, enfeoffed Broad Peace village marquis.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was enfeoffed as village marquis of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 帝欲大興軍征吳，毗諫曰：「吳、楚之民，險而難禦，道隆後服，道洿先叛，自古患之，非徒今也。

translations.literal: The emperor wished greatly to raise army campaign Wu; Xin Pi remonstrated saying: "Wu and Chu people, treacherous and hard to control; when the Way is elevated late submit, when the Way is muddy first rebel; from antiquity troubled by this, not only now.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor planned a major mobilization against Wu, Xin Pi remonstrated: "The peoples of Wu and Chu are stubborn and hard to govern: when the moral tone of government is high they are slow to submit, and when it falters they are the first to rebel. That has been the worry of every age, not ours alone."

sentences.zh: 今陛下祚有海內，夫不賔者，其能乆乎？

translations.literal: Now your Majesty's throne possesses within the seas; those not guesting, can they long?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty now holds the realm entire—how long can any who withhold allegiance hold out?"

sentences.zh: 昔尉佗稱帝，子陽僭號，歷年未幾，或臣或誅。

translations.literal: Of old Wei Tuo declared emperor, Ziyang usurped title; years passed not many, some became subjects some were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Tuo once declared himself emperor, Gongsun Shu styled himself a sovereign, yet within a few years both had been brought to heel or destroyed."

sentences.zh: 何則，違逆之道不乆全，而大德無所不服也。

translations.literal: What then; the way of rebellion-disobedience not long whole; yet great virtue nothing not submits.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellion cannot long endure, and where true great virtue holds sway nothing remains unsubdued."

sentences.zh: 方今天下新定，土廣民稀。

translations.literal: Just now the realm newly settled, land broad people sparse.
translations.idiomatic: The empire is only lately pacified; territory is vast and population thin.

sentences.zh: 夫廟筭而後出軍，猶臨事而懼，況今廟筭有闕而欲用之，臣誠未見其利也。

translations.literal: Now temple calculation then afterward send out army, still facing affairs and fearing; moreover now temple calculation has gaps yet wishes to use it; your servant truly has not seen its benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Even when every detail has been weighed in council before troops march, a wise commander still meets each turn of events with caution—and now the plan itself is incomplete. I frankly see no advantage in pressing ahead."

sentences.zh: 先帝屢起銳師，臨江而旋。

translations.literal: The late emperor repeatedly raised sharp armies, reached the river and turned back.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor more than once led picked hosts to the Yangzi only to wheel about without forcing a crossing."

sentences.zh: 今六軍不增於故，而復循之，此未易也。

translations.literal: Now the six armies do not increase from before; yet again follow it; this is not easy.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial army is no stronger than it was then; to repeat the same attempt will not be easy."

sentences.zh: 今日之計，莫若脩范蠡之養民，法管仲之寄政，則充國之屯田，明仲尼之懷遠；

translations.literal: Today's plan, none like cultivate Fan Li's nurturing people, model Guan Zhong's lodged governance, then Chongguo's garrison fields, clarify Zhongni's cherishing the distant;
translations.idiomatic: The better course today is to nurture the people as Fan Li did, to administer border counties as Guan Zhong advised, to open garrison farms after Zhao Chongguo's example, and to win distant peoples as Confucius taught;

sentences.zh: 十年之中，彊壯未老，童齓勝戰，兆民知義，將士思奮，然後用之，則役不再舉矣。

translations.literal: Within ten years, strong adult not yet old, children shedding teeth surpass battle, myriad people know righteousness, generals soldiers think exertion; then use them, then service not again raised.
translations.idiomatic: within ten years your prime cohorts will still be in their prime, your youths will have come of fighting age, the common people will understand where duty lies, and officers and men will burn to prove themselves. Then you may commit them to war and need not repeat the mobilization."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「如卿意，更當以虜遺子孫邪？

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "As your meaning, moreover ought to leave the enemy captives for descendants?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "By your reasoning, am I to leave the foe for my sons and grandsons to deal with?"

sentences.zh: 」毗對曰：「昔周文王以紂遺武王，惟知時也。

translations.literal: " Xin Pi replied: "Of old King Wen of Zhou left Zhou of Shang for King Wu; only knew the time."
translations.idiomatic: Xin Pi answered, "King Wen of Zhou left King Zhou of Shang for King Wu to overthrow—because he knew the hour had not yet come."

sentences.zh: 苟時未可，容得已乎！

translations.literal: If the time not yet permissible, how can allow stopping!
translations.idiomatic: When the times forbid action, what choice have you but to wait?"

sentences.zh: 」帝竟伐吳，至江而還。

translations.literal: " The emperor in the end campaigned against Wu, reached the river and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went ahead with the campaign against Wu in any case, marched to the river, and turned back.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，進封潁鄉侯，邑三百戶。

translations.literal: Mingdi ascended the throne, advanced enfeoffment Ying village marquis, fief three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming came to the throne, Xin Pi was promoted to village marquis of Ying with a fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 時中書監劉放、令孫資見信於主，制斷時政，大臣莫不交好，而毗不與往來。

translations.literal: At the time Central Documents Supervisor Liu Fang and Director Sun Zi were seen trusted by the ruler, controlled and decided current government; great ministers none not befriended, yet Xin Pi did not with them go and come.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fang, the supervisor of the secretariat, and Sun Zi, its director, enjoyed the sovereign's full confidence and shaped every decision of the day, so that every senior minister courted their favor—everyone except Xin Pi, who kept his distance.

sentences.zh: 毗子敞諫曰：「今劉、孫用事，衆皆影附，大人宜小降意，和光同塵；

translations.literal: Xin Pi's son Xin Chang remonstrated saying: "Now Liu and Sun handle affairs; the host all shadow attach; the great man ought slightly lower intent, harmonize light same dust;
translations.idiomatic: His son Xin Chang urged him, "Liu and Sun now hold the levers of power, and the whole court shadows their every step. You should bend your pride a little and blend your light with the dust of the world;

sentences.zh: 不然必有謗言。

translations.literal: If not, surely there will be slanderous words."
translations.idiomatic: otherwise slander will find you."

sentences.zh: 」毗正色曰：「主上雖未稱聦明，不爲闇劣。

translations.literal: " Xin Pi with straight color said: "The lord above although not yet called intelligent bright, is not dim inferior."
translations.idiomatic: Xin Pi answered sternly, "The sovereign may not yet be accounted a sage, but he is no fool."

sentences.zh: 吾之立身，自有本未。

translations.literal: My establishing body, naturally has root and tip.
translations.idiomatic: I have my own principles in how I comport myself.

sentences.zh: 就與劉、孫不平，不過令吾不作三公而已，何危害之有？

translations.literal: Even if with Liu and Sun not level, no more than cause me not to become Three Dukes only; what harm danger is there?
translations.idiomatic: Even if Liu and Sun take against me, the worst they can do is keep me from the rank of one of the Three Dukes—what real harm is that?

sentences.zh: 焉有大丈夫欲爲公而毀其高節者邪？

translations.literal: How has great husband wishing to be duke yet destroying his high integrity?
translations.idiomatic: What sort of man would sell his integrity for a minister's chair?"

sentences.zh: 」宂從僕射畢軌表言：「尚書僕射王思精勤舊吏，忠亮計略不如辛毗，毗宜代思。

translations.literal: Concurrent Deputy Director (pushe) Bi Gui submitted a memorial stating that Vice Director of the Secretariat Wang Si is a diligent veteran official, that in loyalty and planning he does not match Xin Pi, and that Xin Pi ought to replace Si.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Gui, who held the concurrent post of Deputy Director (pushe), submitted a memorial saying that Wang Si, vice director of the secretariat, is a scrupulous veteran and utterly loyal, yet cannot match Xin Pi in counsel, and that Xin Pi should succeed him.

sentences.zh: 」帝以訪放、資，放、資對曰：「陛下用思者，誠欲取其効力，不貴虛名也。

translations.literal: " The emperor used to consult Fang and Zi; Fang and Zi replied saying: "Your Majesty's employing Si, truly wishes to take his effective strength, not value empty name."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor consulted Liu Fang and Sun Zi, who replied, "Your Majesty appointed Wang Si because you wanted practical service from him, not a hollow reputation."

sentences.zh: 毗實亮直，然性剛而專，聖慮所當深察也。

translations.literal: Xin Pi truly bright straight, yet nature hard and specialized; sagely consideration ought deeply examine.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Pi is candid and upright, but his temper is rigid and his manner uncompromising—Your Majesty should weigh that carefully."

sentences.zh: 」遂不用。

translations.literal: " Then did not use.
translations.idiomatic: The recommendation was not adopted.

sentences.zh: 出爲衞尉。

translations.literal: He went out and became Commandant of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He left court to serve as commandant of the guards.

sentences.zh: 帝方脩殿舍，百姓勞役，毗上疏曰：「竊聞諸葛亮講武治兵，而孫權巿馬遼東，量其意指，似欲相左右。

translations.literal: The emperor was repairing halls and chambers; the common people suffered under corvée labor. Xin Pi submitted a memorial saying: "I have heard that Zhuge Liang is drilling troops and training soldiers, while Sun Quan is buying horses in Liaodong; gauging their intentions, they seem to wish to act in concert on either flank.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was raising palace halls while the people staggered under forced labor. Xin Pi presented a memorial: "I hear that Zhuge Liang is training his army and that Sun Quan is purchasing horses in Liaodong. From the drift of their designs, they appear ready to move in tandem against us."

sentences.zh: 備豫不虞，古之善政，而今者宮室大興，加連年穀麥不收。

translations.literal: To prepare against the unforeseen is good government of antiquity; yet now palace chambers are built on a grand scale, added to successive years when neither grain nor wheat is harvested.
translations.idiomatic: Readiness against the unexpected was the mark of wise rule in olden days, yet today construction soars while the harvests have failed year after year."

sentences.zh: 詩云：『民亦勞止，迄可小康，惠此中國，以綏四方。

translations.literal: The Classic of Poetry says: 'The people indeed are weary; perhaps there can be a little repose; show favor to these central regions, thereby to soothe the four quarters.'
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Odes says, "The people are worn out; grant them a measure of ease; cherish the heartland, and the four quarters will be soothed."

sentences.zh: 』唯陛下爲社稷計。

translations.literal: Only your Majesty, for the altars of soil and grain, deliberate."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to act for the sake of the altars of state."

sentences.zh: 」帝報曰：「二虜未滅而治宮室，直諫者立名之時也。

translations.literal: The emperor replied: "The two bandit enemies are not yet destroyed, yet I build palace chambers; it is the hour for straight remonstrators to make their names.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered, "The two rebel powers still stand while I raise palaces—this is the very moment when blunt counsel earns a man his reputation."

sentences.zh: 夫王者之都，當及民勞兼辦，使後世無所復增，是蕭何爲漢規摹之略也。

translations.literal: As for a king's capital, one ought, while the people still labor, to accomplish it together, so that later generations have nothing further to add; this was the comprehensive plan Xiao He laid down for the Han.
translations.idiomatic: A king's capital should be finished while the people can still bear the burden, leaving posterity nothing essential to add—that was the grand layout Xiao He drew for the Han."

sentences.zh: 今卿爲魏重臣，亦宜解其大歸。

translations.literal: Now you are a weighty minister of Wei; you also ought to grasp its great outline."
translations.idiomatic: You are a pillar of Wei; you should grasp the larger design as well."

sentences.zh: 」帝又欲平北芒，令於其上作臺觀，則見孟津。

translations.literal: The emperor also wished to level the Northern Mang, ordering towers and belvederes built upon it, so that Meng Ford could be seen.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed leveling the Mang Hills north of Luoyang and erecting terraces there to command a view of the ford at Mengjin."

sentences.zh: 毗諫曰：「天地之性，高高下下，今而反之，旣非其理；

translations.literal: Xin Pi remonstrated: "The nature of Heaven and earth is that some places are high and some low; now to reverse this is already contrary to principle;
translations.idiomatic: Xin Pi objected: "Heaven and earth set heights and hollows as they are; to turn that order upside down offends their pattern;"

sentences.zh: 加以損費人功，民不堪役。

translations.literal: added to wasting human labor, the people cannot endure the service.
translations.idiomatic: and to squander labor on top of that would crush the people under corvée duty."

sentences.zh: 且若九河盈溢，洪水爲害，而丘陵皆夷，將何以禦之？

translations.literal: Moreover, if the nine rivers swell and floodwaters become a calamity, while every hill and mound is leveled, with what will you ward them off?"
translations.idiomatic: If the great rivers burst their banks and the hills have been shaved flat, what will hold the flood back?"

sentences.zh: 」帝乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor then desisted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor abandoned the project.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：諸葛亮圍祁山，不克，引退。

translations.literal: The Wei lüe says: Zhuge Liang besieged Mount Qi, could not take it, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Brief Account of Wei relates that Zhuge Liang besieged Qishan, failed to reduce it, and pulled back.

sentences.zh: 張郃追之，爲流矢所中死。

translations.literal: Zhang He pursued him, was struck by a stray arrow, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang He pursued the retreat and was killed by a stray arrow.

sentences.zh: 帝惜郃，臨朝而歎曰：「蜀未平而郃死，將若之何！

translations.literal: The emperor pitied He; facing the court he sighed and said: "Shu is not yet pacified, yet He is dead; what is to be done!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grieved for Zhang He and lamented at court, "Shu is still unconquered, and now Zhang He is gone—what can we do?"

sentences.zh: 」司空陳羣曰：「郃誠良將，國所依也。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Chen Qun said: "He was truly a fine general; the state depended on him.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Chen Qun said, "Zhang He was an outstanding commander on whom the state relied."

sentences.zh: 」毗心以爲郃雖可惜，然已死，不當內弱主意，而示外以不大也。

translations.literal: Xin Pi inwardly thought that although He was regrettable, yet he was already dead; one ought not inwardly weaken the ruler's intent, yet outwardly show oneself not great.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Pi thought the loss of Zhang He grievous, but the dead cannot be recalled; it would be wrong to sap the sovereign's resolve in court or to advertise weakness to the enemy."

sentences.zh: 乃持羣曰：「陳公，是何言歟！

translations.literal: Then he seized Qun and said: "Lord Chen, what manner of words are these!
translations.idiomatic: He seized Chen Qun by the arm and said, "Lord Chen, what sort of talk is this?"

sentences.zh: 當建安之末，天下不可一日無武皇帝也，及委國祚，而文皇帝受命，黃初之世，亦謂不可無文皇帝也，及委棄天下，而陛下龍興。

translations.literal: At the end of the Jian-an era, the realm could not for a day be without Martial Emperor; when the imperial mandate was entrusted and Emperor Wen received the mandate, in the Huang-chu era, people also said the realm could not be without Emperor Wen; when he abandoned the realm below and Your Majesty rose like a dragon.
translations.idiomatic: At the close of the Jian-an years the empire could not for a day do without Emperor Wu; when the mandate passed on, Emperor Wen took the throne, and in the Huangchu era men said the realm could not do without Emperor Wen; when he left the world to Your Majesty, you rose as the dragon successor."

sentences.zh: 今國內所少，豈張郃乎？

translations.literal: Now what the state within lacks, is it Zhang He?
translations.idiomatic: Tell me, is Zhang He the one thing our realm now lacks?"

sentences.zh: 」陳羣曰：「亦誠如辛毗言。

translations.literal: Chen Qun said: "It is indeed as Xin Pi says.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qun said, "Xin Pi speaks the truth."

sentences.zh: 」帝笑曰：「陳公可謂善變矣。

translations.literal: The emperor smiled and said: "Lord Chen can be called good at changing."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor smiled and said, "Lord Chen, you change your tune nimbly."

sentences.zh: 」 臣松之以爲擬人必於其倫，取譬宜引其類，故君子於其言，無所苟而已矣。

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi thinks that in comparing persons one must use their proper class; in taking analogies one ought to cite their kind; therefore the gentleman in his speech is not careless only.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi comments: When likening people to others, one must stay within their station; when choosing a figure of speech, one should stay within the same category. A gentleman does not speak lightly, and that is all."

sentences.zh: 毗欲弘廣主意，當舉若張遼之疇，安有於一將之死而可以祖宗爲譬哉？

translations.literal: If Xin Pi wished to broaden the ruler's intent, he ought to have cited men such as Zhang Liao's sort; how could there be, on one general's death, cause to use the dynastic founders as analogy?
translations.idiomatic: If Xin Pi meant to steady the emperor's mind, he should have named living champions such as Zhang Liao; the death of a single general is no occasion to invoke the founding emperors as parallels."

sentences.zh: 非所宜言，莫過於茲，進違其類，退似諂佞，佐治剛正之體，不宜有此。

translations.literal: Nothing less fitting to say than this; advancing it departed from its class, retreating it seemed flattery and fawning; Zuozhi's hard upright substance ought not have had this.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing could be more out of place; pushed forward it breaks category, drawn back it smacks of sycophancy—this is not what we expect of Xin Pi's blunt integrity."

sentences.zh: 《魏略》旣已難信，習氏又從而載之，竊謂斯人受誣不少。〉

translations.literal: The Wei lüe was already hard to trust, and the Xi family again followed and recorded it; I privately think this man has suffered no small slander.〉
translations.idiomatic: The Brief Account of Wei is already suspect, and the Xi family repeated the tale; I believe Xin Pi has been much maligned."

sentences.zh: 青龍二年，諸葛亮率衆出渭南。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qinglong, Zhuge Liang led the host south of the Wei River.
translations.idiomatic: In Qinglong 2 (234), Zhuge Liang marched his army to the south bank of the Wei.

sentences.zh: 先是，大將軍司馬宣王數請與亮戰，明帝終不聽。

translations.literal: Before this, Grand General Sima Yi several times requested to fight Liang, but Emperor Ming to the end did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Grand General Sima Yi had repeatedly asked leave to give battle, but Emperor Ming had always refused.

sentences.zh: 是歲恐不能禁，乃以毗爲大將軍軍師，使持節；

translations.literal: This year fearing he could not restrain him, then appointed Xin Pi as Grand General's Army Adviser, with credentials as envoy holding the staff;
translations.idiomatic: Fearing he could no longer hold Sima Yi in check that year, the court named Xin Pi army adviser to the grand general and gave him the staff of authority;

sentences.zh: 六軍皆肅，準毗節度，莫敢犯違。

translations.literal: the six armies all were solemn, obeyed Xin Pi's regulation and command, none dared violate.
translations.idiomatic: the six hosts stood in awe and accepted Xin Pi's orders; no one dared disobey.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：宣王數數欲進攻，毗禁不聽。

translations.literal: The Wei lüe says: Yi several times wished to advance and attack; Xin Pi forbade and would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The Brief Account of Wei says Sima Yi repeatedly pressed for an offensive, but Xin Pi forbade it and would not yield.

sentences.zh: 宣王雖能行意，而每屈於毗。〉

translations.literal: Although Yi could carry out his intent, yet each time he yielded to Xin Pi.〉
translations.idiomatic: Though Sima Yi could act on his own judgment, he repeatedly bowed to Xin Pi's restraint."

sentences.zh: 亮卒，復還爲衞尉。

translations.literal: When Liang died, he again returned and became Commandant of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhuge Liang's death Xin Pi resumed his post as commandant of the guards.

sentences.zh: 薨，謚曰肅侯。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous title said Solemn Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: He died and received the posthumous title Marquis Su ("the Stern").

sentences.zh: 子敞嗣，咸熈中爲河內太守。

translations.literal: His son Chang succeeded; in the Xianxi era became Administrator of Henan within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xin Chang inherited the title and later served as administrator of Henan during the Xianxi era.

sentences.zh: 〈《世語》曰：敞字泰雍，官至衞尉。

translations.literal: The Shiyu says: Chang courtesy name Taiyong, reached office Commandant of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: The Contemporary Tales says Xin Chang, courtesy name Taiyong, rose to the post of commandant of the guards.

sentences.zh: 毗女憲英，適太常泰山羊耽，外孫夏侯湛爲其傳曰：「憲英聦明有才鑒。

translations.literal: Xin Pi's daughter Xianying married Minister of Ceremonies Yang Dan of Taishan; her maternal grandson Xiahou Zhan wrote her biography saying: "Xianying was intelligent and had talent for judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Pi's daughter Xianying married Yang Dan of Taishan, the minister of ceremonies; her grandson Xiahou Zhan composed her biography, saying, "Xianying was clever and discerning."

sentences.zh: 初文帝與陳思王爭爲太子，旣而文帝得立，抱毗頸而喜曰：『辛君知我喜不？

translations.literal: When at first Emperor Wen and Prince Si of Chen contended to be heir apparent, afterward Emperor Wen obtained establishment; he embraced Xin Pi's neck and joyfully said: 'Lord Xin, do you know I am pleased or not?
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen was still heir apparent and vied with Cao Zhi, the Prince of Chen, Wen eventually won the succession. He threw his arms around Xin Pi's neck and cried, "Lord Xin, can you guess how happy I am?"

sentences.zh: 』毗以告憲英，憲英歎曰：『太子代君主宗廟社稷者也。

translations.literal: Xin Pi told Xianying; Xianying sighed and said: 'The heir apparent replaces the ruler in charge of the ancestral temple and altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Pi repeated this to Xianying, who sighed and said, "The heir takes the ruler's place before the ancestral shrines and the altars of state."

sentences.zh: 代君不可以不戚，主國不可以不懼，宜戚而喜，何以能乆？

translations.literal: To replace the ruler one cannot but grieve; to head the state one cannot but fear; ought to grieve yet is pleased; how can it long endure?
translations.idiomatic: To step into a father's place ought to bring sorrow, and to shoulder the realm ought to bring dread. If he is elated instead, how long can such a reign last?"

sentences.zh: 魏其不昌乎！

translations.literal: Wei will not flourish!
translations.idiomatic: Wei will not prosper under him!"

sentences.zh: 』弟敞爲大將軍曹爽參軍。

translations.literal: Her younger brother Chang was staff officer to Grand General Cao Shuang.
translations.idiomatic: Her younger brother Xin Chang served as an adviser on the staff of Grand General Cao Shuang.

sentences.zh: 司馬宣王將誅爽，因爽出，閉城門。

translations.literal: Sima Yi was about to execute Shuang; taking advantage of Shuang's outing, he closed the city gates.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Yi moved to purge Cao Shuang, he waited until Shuang had left the city and then sealed the gates.

sentences.zh: 大將軍司馬魯芝將爽府兵，犯門斬關，出城門赴爽，來呼敞俱去。

translations.literal: Grand General's Major Lu Zhi led Shuang's headquarters troops, broke through the gates and barricades, went out the city gate to join Shuang, came calling Chang to go together.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi, the major general under the grand general, led Cao Shuang's household troops, cut through the barricades, burst out of the city to reach Shuang, and urged Xin Chang to ride with him.

sentences.zh: 敞懼，問憲英曰：『天子在外，太傅閉城門，人云將不利國家，於事可得爾乎？

translations.literal: Chang was afraid and asked Xianying: 'The Son of Heaven is outside; the Grand Tutor has closed the city gates; people say this will not be good for the state; in the affair can it be so?
translations.idiomatic: Xin Chang was frightened and asked Xianying, "The emperor is outside the walls, the grand tutor has shut the gates, and rumor says the state is in peril—can things really be as bad as that?"

sentences.zh: 』憲英曰：『天下有不可知，然以吾度之，太傅殆不得不爾！

translations.literal: Xianying said: 'Under Heaven there are things one cannot know; yet by my reckoning, the Grand Tutor perforce could not do otherwise!
translations.idiomatic: She answered, "The world holds mysteries we cannot fathom, yet in my judgment the grand tutor had no choice but to act."

sentences.zh: 明皇帝臨崩，把太傅臂，以後事付之，此言猶在朝士之耳。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming faced death, he grasped the Grand Tutor's arm and entrusted him with the aftermath; these words are still in the ears of the courtiers.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed Emperor Ming seized the grand tutor's arm and entrusted him with the succession; every minister still remembers that charge."

sentences.zh: 且曹爽與太傅俱受寄託之任，而獨專權勢，行以驕奢，於王室不忠，於人道不直，此舉不過以誅曹爽耳。

translations.literal: Moreover Cao Shuang and the Grand Tutor alike received the charge of regency, yet alone monopolized power and influence, acting with arrogance and extravagance; toward the royal house not loyal, toward the human way not upright; this move is no more than to execute Cao Shuang.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Shuang received the same regency as the grand tutor, yet he hoarded power, lived in arrogance and luxury, betrayed the house of Wei, and broke faith with common decency. This coup aims only at removing Cao Shuang."

sentences.zh: 』敞曰：『然則事就乎？

translations.literal: Chang said: 'Then will the affair succeed?
translations.idiomatic: Xin Chang asked, "Then will the affair succeed?"

sentences.zh: 』憲英曰：『得無殆就！

translations.literal: Xianying said: 'Perhaps almost succeed!
translations.idiomatic: She said, "It may well succeed."

sentences.zh: 爽之才非太傅之偶也。

translations.literal: Shuang's talent is not a match for the Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Shuang is no match for the grand tutor."

sentences.zh: 』敞曰：『然則敞可以無出乎？

translations.literal: Chang said: 'Then can Chang not go out?
translations.idiomatic: Xin Chang asked, "Then may I stay home?"

sentences.zh: 』憲英曰：『安可以不出。

translations.literal: Xianying said: 'How can one not go out.
translations.idiomatic: She replied, "How could you stay away?"

sentences.zh: 職守，人之大義也。

translations.literal: Office and duty are the great righteousness of men.
translations.idiomatic: Office and duty are the first obligations of a gentleman."

sentences.zh: 凡人在難，猶或卹之；

translations.literal: Ordinary men in difficulty, still perhaps pity them;
translations.idiomatic: Even common folk in distress deserve compassion;"

sentences.zh: 爲人執鞭而棄其事，不祥，不可也。

translations.literal: for a man to hold the whip yet abandon his task is inauspicious; cannot.
translations.idiomatic: to take a post and then desert it when danger comes is ill-omened and wrong."

sentences.zh: 且爲人死，爲人任，親昵之職也，從衆而已。

translations.literal: Moreover to die for others, to bear responsibility for others, is the office of intimacy; follow the multitude only.
translations.idiomatic: To risk one's life for a lord and answer for his fate is the duty of a trusted officer—go with the rest."

sentences.zh: 』敞遂出。

translations.literal: Chang then went out.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Chang rode out.

sentences.zh: 宣王果誅爽。

translations.literal: Sima Yi indeed executed Shuang.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi did execute Cao Shuang.

sentences.zh: 事定之後，敞歎曰：『吾不謀於姊，幾不獲於義。

translations.literal: After the affair was settled, Chang sighed and said: 'Had I not consulted my elder sister, I would almost have failed in righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: When the dust settled, Xin Chang sighed, "Had I not asked my sister, I would nearly have failed in my duty."

sentences.zh: 』逮鍾會爲鎮西將軍，憲英謂從子羊祜曰：『鍾士季何故西出？

translations.literal: When Zhong Hui became General Who Guards the West, Xianying said to her nephew Yang Hu: 'Why does Zhong Shiji go west?
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Zhong Hui was named general who guards the west, Xianying asked her nephew Yang Hu, "Why is Zhong Hui marching west?"

sentences.zh: 』祜曰：『將爲滅蜀也。

translations.literal: Hu said: 'He will go to destroy Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hu said, "To conquer Shu."

sentences.zh: 』憲英曰：『會在事縱恣，非持乆處下之道，吾畏其有他志也。

translations.literal: Xianying said: 'Hui in affairs indulges his will; it is not the way to endure long below others; I fear he has other intentions.
translations.idiomatic: She said, "Zhong Hui indulges his whims in office; he is not a man who will long submit to another. I fear he harbors designs of his own."

sentences.zh: 』祜曰：『季母勿多言。

translations.literal: Hu said: 'Aunt, do not speak much.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hu said, "Aunt, say no more."

sentences.zh: 』其後會請子琇爲參軍，憲英憂曰：『他日見鍾會之出，吾爲國憂之矣。

translations.literal: Afterward Hui requested Zixiu as staff officer; Xianying worried and said: 'Other days seeing Zhong Hui's departure, I for the state worried.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhong Hui later asked Xin Xiu to join his staff as an adviser, Xianying said in alarm, "The day I saw Zhong Hui ride west I feared for the realm;"

sentences.zh: 今日難至吾家，此國之大事，必不得止也。

translations.literal: Today difficulty reaches my house; this is the state's great affair; surely cannot stop.
translations.idiomatic: today the trouble has reached our own door. This is a matter of state, and you cannot refuse."

sentences.zh: 』琇固請司馬文王，文王不聽。

translations.literal: Xiu firmly requested Sima Zhao; Sima Zhao would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Xiu pleaded with Sima Zhao, who would not release him.

sentences.zh: 憲英語琇曰：『行矣，戒之！

translations.literal: Xianying spoke to Xiu saying: 'Go; be on guard!
translations.idiomatic: Xianying told him, "You must go—guard yourself well."

sentences.zh: 古之君子，入則致孝於親，出則致節於國，在職思其所司，在義思其所立，不遺父母憂患而已。

translations.literal: The gentleman of antiquity, entering then extended filial piety to parents; going out then extended integrity to the state; in office thought what his charge was; in righteousness thought what he should establish; not leaving parents worry and calamity only.
translations.idiomatic: The gentlemen of old showed filial devotion at home and integrity abroad; in office they pondered their duty, in crisis they weighed what was right, and they strove never to bring grief upon their parents."

sentences.zh: 軍旅之間，可以濟者，其惟仁恕乎！

translations.literal: Between armies and hosts, what can help is perhaps only benevolence and forbearance!
translations.idiomatic: In the camp and on the battlefield, only kindness and restraint can save you."

sentences.zh: 汝其慎之！

translations.literal: You must be careful!
translations.idiomatic: Mark my words and be careful."

sentences.zh: 』琇竟以全身。

translations.literal: Xiu in the end thereby preserved his whole person.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Xiu followed her counsel and survived with his life."

sentences.zh: 憲英年至七十有九，泰始五年卒。」〉

translations.literal: Xianying's years reached seventy-nine; in the fifth year of Taishi she died."〉
translations.idiomatic: Xianying lived to seventy-nine and died in Taishi 5 (269)."

sentences.zh: 楊阜字義山，天水冀人也。

translations.literal: Yang Fu courtesy name Yishan, was a man of Ji in Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fu, courtesy name Yishan, was a native of Ji in Tianshui commandery.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：阜少與同郡尹奉次曾、趙昂偉章俱發名，偉章、次曾與阜俱爲涼州從事。〉

translations.literal: The Wei lüe says: Fu in youth with same commandery Yin Feng Ciceng, Zhao Ang Weizhang together rose to fame; Weizhang and Ciceng with Fu together were Liangzhou staff.
translations.idiomatic: The Brief Account of Wei says that in his youth Yang Fu won a local reputation alongside Yin Feng (courtesy Ciceng) and Zhao Ang (courtesy Weizhang) of the same commandery; Zhao and Yin served with Yang Fu as staff officers in Liangzhou."

sentences.zh: 以州從事爲牧韋端使詣許，拜安定長史。

translations.literal: As a commandery staff officer he was sent by Governor Wei Duan on mission to Xu, was appointed Chief Clerk of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: While serving on the provincial staff he was dispatched by Governor Wei Duan to the capital at Xu and was appointed chief clerk of Anding.

sentences.zh: 阜還，關右諸將問袁、曹勝敗孰在，阜曰：「袁公寬而不斷，好謀而少決；

translations.literal: When Fu returned, the generals west of the pass asked whether Yuan or Cao would win or lose; Fu said: "Lord Yuan is lenient yet indecisive, fond of plotting yet seldom decides;
translations.idiomatic: On his return the generals beyond the pass asked whether Yuan Shao or Cao Cao would prevail. Yang Fu said, "Yuan Shao is magnanimous but cannot decide, fond of counsel but slow to commit;"

sentences.zh: 不斷則無威，少決則失後事，今雖彊，終不能成大業。

translations.literal: if indecisive then there is no awe; if seldom decides then loses later affairs; now although strong, in the end cannot accomplish great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: indecision saps authority, and hesitation loses the moment. He may look strong now, yet he will never finish the great work."

sentences.zh: 曹公有雄才遠略，決機無疑，法一而兵精，能用度外之人，所任各盡其力，必能濟大事者也。

translations.literal: Lord Cao has heroic talent and far-reaching strategy, decides opportunities without doubt, law is unified and troops are keen, can employ men beyond ordinary measure, those he employs each exhaust their strength; he surely is one who can accomplish great matters.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Cao has heroic gifts and long vision, seizes his chances without wavering, keeps the law uniform and his soldiers sharp, and can use unusual men so that each gives his utmost. He is the man who will achieve the great enterprise."

sentences.zh: 」長史非其好，遂去官。

translations.literal: Chief clerk was not his liking; then left office.
translations.idiomatic: The chief clerk's post did not suit him, so he resigned.

sentences.zh: 而端徵爲太僕，其子康代爲刺史，辟阜爲別駕。

translations.literal: But Duan was summoned to be Grand Coachman; his son Kang replaced him as Inspector, summoned Fu as Attendant Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Duan was then recalled to serve as grand coachman, and his son Wei Kang succeeded him as provincial inspector, who appointed Yang Fu as attendant clerk.

sentences.zh: 察孝廉，辟丞相府，州表留參軍事。

translations.literal: He was nominated Filial and Incorrupt, summoned to the Chancellor's office; the province memorialized to retain him on military staff.
translations.idiomatic: Nominated as filial and incorrupt, he was called to the chancellor's headquarters, but the province petitioned to keep him on its military staff.

sentences.zh: 馬超之戰敗渭南也，走保諸戎。

translations.literal: When Ma Chao was defeated south of the Wei River in battle, he fled to protect himself among the various Rong.
translations.idiomatic: After Ma Chao was routed south of the Wei, he fled west among the Qiang and Rong tribes.

sentences.zh: 太祖追至安定，而蘇伯反河閒，將引軍東還。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor pursued to Anding, but Su Bo rebelled in Hejian; he was about to lead the army east back.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao pressed the pursuit to Anding, but Su Bo rose in revolt in Hejian, and he prepared to march the army back east.

sentences.zh: 阜時奉使，言於太祖曰：「超有信、布之勇，甚得羌、胡心，西州畏之。

translations.literal: Fu at the time was on mission and spoke to the Grand Progenitor saying: "Chao has the courage of Xin and Bu; he greatly wins the hearts of the Qiang and Hu; the western provinces fear him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fu, then away on assignment, warned Cao Cao, "Ma Chao has the dash of Han Xin and Ying Bu; the Qiang and Hu rally to him, and the west trembles at his name."

sentences.zh: 若大軍還，不嚴爲之備，隴上諸郡非國家之有也。

translations.literal: If the great army returns and does not strictly prepare against him, the commanderies on Long will not belong to the state.
translations.idiomatic: If the main force withdraws without leaving strong precautions, the commanderies along the Long plateau will no longer be ours."

sentences.zh: 」太祖善之，而軍還倉卒，爲備不周。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor deemed it good, yet the army returned in haste, and preparations were not thorough.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao saw the point, but the withdrawal was hurried and the dispositions were incomplete.

sentences.zh: 超率諸戎渠帥以擊隴上郡縣，隴上郡縣皆應之，惟冀城奉州郡以固守。

translations.literal: Chao led the chieftains of the various Rong to strike the commanderies and counties on Long; the Long commanderies and counties all responded to him; only Ji city with the province and commandery held fast.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao led the tribal chiefs against the Long counties, which rose for him one after another; only Ji city, loyal to the provincial and commandery authorities, held out.

sentences.zh: 超盡兼隴右之衆，而張魯又遣大將楊昂以助之，凡萬餘人，攻城。

translations.literal: Chao annexed all the hosts west of Long, and Zhang Lu also sent great general Yang Ang to assist him; in all more than ten thousand, besieging the city.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao absorbed every force west of the Long frontier, while Zhang Lu sent his general Yang Ang with reinforcements—more than ten thousand men in all—to storm the walls.

sentences.zh: 阜率國士大夫及宗族子弟勝兵者千餘人，使從弟岳於城上作偃月營，與超接戰，自正月至八月拒守而救兵不至。

translations.literal: Fu led the state's gentlemen and officials and clansmen's sons and younger brothers who could bear arms, more than a thousand, had cousin Yue on the city wall build a crescent camp, joined battle with Chao; from the first month to the eighth month resisted and defended yet relief troops did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fu rallied over a thousand gentlemen, officials, and kinsmen fit to bear arms, had his cousin Yang Yue throw up a crescent-shaped redoubt on the battlements, and traded blows with Ma Chao from the first month to the eighth, yet no relief column came.

sentences.zh: 州遣別駕閻溫循水潛出求救，爲超所殺，於是刺史、太守失色，始有降超之計。

translations.literal: The province sent Attendant Clerk Yan Wen along the water secretly out to seek rescue; he was killed by Chao; thereupon the Inspector and Administrator lost color and first had the plan to surrender to Chao.
translations.idiomatic: The province sent its attendant clerk Yan Wen to slip out along the river for help; Ma Chao caught and killed him. The inspector and the administrator then turned pale and began to speak of yielding the city.

sentences.zh: 阜流涕諫曰：「阜等率父兄子弟以義相勵，有死無二；

translations.literal: Fu weeping remonstrated saying: "We and others lead fathers, elder brothers, sons, and younger brothers, encouraging one another with righteousness; there is death, no second thought;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fu wept and remonstrated, "We have brought fathers, brothers, and sons together under the banner of duty; we are resolved to die rather than turn traitor;"

sentences.zh: 田單之守，不固於此也。

translations.literal: Tian Dan's defense was not more solid than this.
translations.idiomatic: even Tian Dan's defense of Jimo was no tighter than ours."

sentences.zh: 棄垂成之功，陷不義之名，阜以死守之。

translations.literal: To abandon a success nearly complete, to sink into a name of unrighteousness; Fu with death guards it.
translations.idiomatic: To throw away a victory within reach and earn the name of traitors—I will defend this wall with my life."

sentences.zh: 」遂號哭。

translations.literal: Thereupon they wailed and cried.
translations.idiomatic: The defenders broke into loud weeping.

sentences.zh: 刺史、太守卒遣人請和，開城門迎超。

translations.literal: The Inspector and Administrator finally sent men to request peace, opened the city gates and welcomed Chao.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the inspector and the administrator sent envoys to sue for terms, opened the gates, and admitted Ma Chao.

sentences.zh: 超入，拘岳於冀，使楊昂殺刺史、太守。

translations.literal: Chao entered, detained Yue at Ji, had Yang Ang kill the Inspector and Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao entered the city, held Yang Fu's cousin Yang Yue hostage in Ji, and had Yang Ang execute the inspector and the administrator.

sentences.zh: 阜內有報超之志，而未得其便。

translations.literal: Fu within had the intent to repay Chao, yet had not obtained the opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: Within himself Yang Fu burned to avenge Ma Chao, but he had not yet found his chance.

sentences.zh: 頃之，阜以喪妻求葬假。

translations.literal: Before long, Fu because of mourning wife requested burial leave.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he asked leave of absence to bury his wife.

sentences.zh: 阜外兄姜叙屯歷城。

translations.literal: Fu's elder cousin on his mother's side Jiang Xu garrisoned Licheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fu's maternal cousin Jiang Xu was encamped at Licheng.

sentences.zh: 阜少長叙家，見叙母及叙，說前在冀中時事，歔欷悲甚。

translations.literal: Fu from youth grew up in Xu's household; seeing Xu's mother and Xu, he spoke of earlier matters when in Ji, sighing and weeping extremely.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fu had been raised in Jiang Xu's home as a boy. When he saw Xu and Xu's mother, he told them what had happened during the siege of Ji and broke down in tears.

sentences.zh: 叙曰：「何爲乃爾？

translations.literal: Xu said: "Why is it thus?
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Xu asked, "Why this outpouring?"

sentences.zh: 」阜曰：「守城不能完，君亡不能死，亦何面目以視息於天下！

translations.literal: Fu said: "Defending the city yet could not preserve it; the lord perished yet could not die for him—what face have I to draw breath under Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fu said, "I held the walls yet could not save them; our lord fell yet I did not die at his side—how dare I show my face in the world?"

sentences.zh: 馬超背父叛君，虐殺州將，豈獨阜之憂責，一州士大夫皆蒙其恥。

translations.literal: Ma Chao betrayed father and rebelled against lord, cruelly killed the provincial generals; how is it only Fu's worry and blame—every gentleman of the province shares this shame.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao cast off his father and rebelled against his sovereign, butchered our commanders—this is not my private shame alone; every man of honor in Liangzhou bears the stain."

sentences.zh: 君擁兵專制而無討賊心，此趙盾所以書殺君也。

translations.literal: You hold troops and act autonomously yet have no mind to punish the traitor; this is why Zhao Dun was written as having killed his lord.
translations.idiomatic: You command an army and do as you please, yet you will not move against the traitor—the Chroniclers blamed Zhao Dun for regicide for less than this."

sentences.zh: 超彊而無義，多釁易圖耳。

translations.literal: Chao is strong yet without righteousness; many quarrels, easy to plot against.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao is fierce but faithless; his misrule gives us openings we can exploit."

sentences.zh: 」叙母慨然，勑叙從阜計。

translations.literal: Xu's mother was moved with resolve and ordered Xu to follow Fu's plan.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Xu's mother, stirred to indignation, bade her son follow Yang Fu's design.

sentences.zh: 計定，外與鄉人姜隱、趙昂、尹奉、姚瓊、孔信、武都人李俊、王靈結謀，定討超約，使從弟謨至冀語岳，并結安定梁寬、南安趙衢、龐恭等。

translations.literal: When the plan was fixed, outwardly with fellow townsman Jiang Yin, Zhao Ang, Yin Feng, Yao Qiong, Kong Xin, and from Wudu commandery Li Jun and Wang Ling they bound in conspiracy, fixed the covenant to punish Chao, had cousin Mo go to Ji to speak to Yue, and also linked Anding's Liang Kuan, Nan'an's Zhao Qu, Pang Gong, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Once the plot was set, they conspired in secret with Jiang Yin, Zhao Ang, Yin Feng, Yao Qiong, and Kong Xin of their home district, with Li Jun and Wang Ling of Wudu, swore to destroy Ma Chao, sent Yang Fu's cousin Yang Mo into Ji to warn Yang Yue, and won over Liang Kuan of Anding, Zhao Qu of Nan'an, and Pang Gong.

sentences.zh: 約誓旣明，十七年九月，與叙起兵於鹵城。

translations.literal: When the covenant oath was clear, in the ninth month of the seventeenth year they with Xu raised troops at Lucheng.
translations.idiomatic: The oath was sworn, and in the ninth month of Jian-an 17 (212) they rose with Jiang Xu at Lucheng.

sentences.zh: 超聞阜等兵起，自將出。

translations.literal: When Chao heard Fu and others' troops had risen, he personally led the army out.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Chao learned of the uprising, he marched out in person.

sentences.zh: 而衢、寬等解岳，閉冀城門，討超妻子。

translations.literal: Yet Qu, Kuan, and others released Yue, closed the gates of Ji city, and moved against Chao's wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Qu and Liang Kuan meanwhile freed Yang Yue, sealed the gates of Ji, and turned on Ma Chao's family.

sentences.zh: 超襲歷城，得叙母。

translations.literal: Chao raided Licheng and captured Xu's mother.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao struck Licheng and seized Jiang Xu's mother.

sentences.zh: 叙母罵之曰：「汝背父之逆子，殺君之桀賊，天地豈乆容汝，而不早死，敢以面目視人乎！

translations.literal: Xu's mother reviled him saying: "You unfilial son who betrayed your father, tyrant who killed his lord—how can Heaven and Earth long endure you? Why do you not die soon, yet dare show your face to men!
translations.idiomatic: She cursed him: "Rebel son who turned on his father, butcher who murdered his lord—does Heaven intend to shelter you forever? Why were you not struck down long ago? How dare you look honest men in the eye?"

sentences.zh: 」超怒，殺之。

translations.literal: Chao was angry and killed her.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao in his fury put her to death.

sentences.zh: 阜與超戰，身被五創，宗族昆弟死者七人。

translations.literal: Fu fought with Chao; his body received five wounds; of clan agnates and younger brothers who died, seven persons.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fu fought Ma Chao in person, took five wounds, and lost seven kinsmen in the battle.

sentences.zh: 超遂南奔張魯。

translations.literal: Chao then fled south to Zhang Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao then fled south into Zhang Lu's protection.

sentences.zh: 隴右平定，太祖封討超之功，侯者十一人，賜阜爵關內侯。

translations.literal: When Long's right was pacified, the Grand Progenitor enfeoffed those who had merit in punishing Chao—eleven persons became marquises—and granted Fu rank as secondary marquis within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: After the Long frontier was secured, Cao Cao enfeoffed eleven men for their part in crushing Ma Chao and awarded Yang Fu the rank of secondary marquis within the passes.

sentences.zh: 阜讓曰：「阜君存無扞難之功，君亡無死節之効，於義當絀，於法當誅；

translations.literal: Fu declined saying: "While my lord lived I had no merit in defending against calamity; when my lord died I had no effect of dying for integrity; in righteousness I ought to be demoted, in law I ought to be executed;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fu demurred: "While my lord lived I did not save him from disaster; when he fell I did not die with him—by every rule of honor I deserve demotion, by every statute I deserve execution;"

sentences.zh: 超又不死，無宜苟荷爵祿。

translations.literal: moreover Chao again did not die; there is no reason to undeservedly bear title and stipend.
translations.idiomatic: and Ma Chao still lives—I have no right to accept rank and emolument without shame."

sentences.zh: 」太祖報曰：「君與羣賢共建大功，西土之人以爲美談。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor replied: "You with the host of worthies together established great merit; the people of the western lands take it as a fine tale.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao answered, "You and your comrades won a signal victory; the west still tells the story with admiration."

sentences.zh: 子貢辭賞，仲尼謂之止善。

translations.literal: Zigong declined reward; Zhongni called that stopping good.
translations.idiomatic: When Zi Gong refused a reward, Confucius said he had blocked the way of virtue."

sentences.zh: 君其剖心以順國命。

translations.literal: You ought lay open your heart to comply with the state's command.
translations.idiomatic: Open your heart and accept what the state offers you."

sentences.zh: 姜叙之母，勸叙早發，明智乃爾，雖楊敞之妻蓋不過此。

translations.literal: Jiang Xu's mother urged Xu to rise early; her wisdom was thus—although Yang Chang's wife, surely not more than this.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Xu's mother spurred her son to strike first; such clear-sightedness—even the wife of Yang Chang could not surpass it."

sentences.zh: 賢哉，賢哉！

translations.literal: Worthy indeed, worthy indeed!
translations.idiomatic: How worthy, how worthy!"

sentences.zh: 良史記錄，必不墜於地矣。」

translations.literal: Good historians' records surely will not fall to the ground."
translations.idiomatic: A careful historian will not let such deeds be forgotten."

sentences.zh: 〈皇甫謐《列女傳》曰：姜叙母者，天水姜伯弈之母也。

translations.literal: Huangfu Mi's Biographies of Exemplary Women says: Jiang Xu's mother was the mother of Jiang Boyi of Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Mi's Exemplary Women relates that Jiang Xu's mother was the mother of Jiang Boyi of Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 建安中，馬超攻冀，害涼州刺史韋康，州人悽然，莫不感憤。

translations.literal: In the Jian-an era, Ma Chao attacked Ji, killed Liangzhou Inspector Wei Kang; the people of the province were mournful; none did not feel indignant.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jian-an years Ma Chao stormed Ji and slew Inspector Wei Kang of Liangzhou, leaving the province in grief and fury.

sentences.zh: 叙爲撫夷將軍，擁兵屯歷。

translations.literal: Xu was General Who Pacifies the Yi, held troops and garrisoned Li.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Xu held the title of general who pacifies the Yi and camped his force at Li.

sentences.zh: 叙姑子楊阜，故爲康從事，同等十餘人，皆略屬超，陰相結爲康報仇，未有閒。

translations.literal: Xu's aunt's son Yang Fu, formerly had been Kang's staff officer; more than ten peers of the same rank were all roughly subject to Chao, secretly bound together to avenge Kang for Chao, yet had no opening.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fu, Jiang Xu's cousin by marriage, had formerly served on Wei Kang's staff; a dozen or so of his colleagues were likewise forced to submit to Ma Chao while secretly plotting vengeance, but they could find no opportunity.

sentences.zh: 會阜妻死，辭超寧歸西，因過至歷，候叙母，說康被害及冀中之難，相對泣良乆。

translations.literal: When Fu's wife died, he took leave of Chao to mourn and return west, thereby passing to Li, waited on Xu's mother, spoke of Kang's murder and the calamity in Ji; they faced each other weeping a long time.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Fu's wife died, he begged Ma Chao for leave to carry her west for burial, stopped at Licheng to call on Jiang Xu's mother, and told her how Wei Kang had been slain and Ji thrown into chaos; mother and son wept together for a long while.

sentences.zh: 姜叙舉室感悲，叙母曰：「咄！

translations.literal: Jiang Xu's whole household was moved with grief; Xu's mother said: "Tsk!
translations.idiomatic: The whole Jiang household was in tears. The old woman cried, "Enough!"

sentences.zh: 伯弈，韋使君遇難，豈一州之恥，亦汝之負，豈獨義山哉？

translations.literal: Boyi, when Inspector Wei met disaster, was it not one province's shame, also your burden—how is it only Yishan?
translations.idiomatic: Boyi, Inspector Wei's murder shames all Liangzhou and falls on your shoulders as much as on Yishan's."

sentences.zh: 汝無顧我，事淹變生。

translations.literal: You have no need to look to me; affairs drag on and change will arise.
translations.idiomatic: Do not linger for my sake—delay will only breed new danger."

sentences.zh: 人誰不死？

translations.literal: Who among men does not die?
translations.idiomatic: Every man must die sometime."

sentences.zh: 死國，忠義之大者。

translations.literal: To die for the state is the greatest of loyalty and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: To die for one's country is the highest act of loyalty."

sentences.zh: 但當速發，我自爲汝當之，不以餘年累汝也。

translations.literal: Only ought to rise quickly; I myself will answer for you, not with remaining years burden you.
translations.idiomatic: Strike at once. I will answer for whatever follows—I will not chain your last years to my old age."

sentences.zh: 」因勑叙與阜參議，許諾，分人使語鄉里尹奉、趙昂及安定梁寬等，令叙先舉兵叛超，超怒，必自來擊叙，寬等因從後閉門。

translations.literal: Therefore ordered Xu with Fu to consult in council; they promised, divided men to speak to fellow towns Yin Feng, Zhao Ang, and Anding's Liang Kuan and others, ordered Xu first to raise troops in rebellion against Chao; Chao would be angry and surely personally come strike Xu; Kuan and others then from behind would close the gates.
translations.idiomatic: She then told Jiang Xu to take counsel with Yang Fu. They agreed, sent word to Yin Feng, Zhao Ang, Liang Kuan of Anding, and the rest, and arranged for Jiang Xu to rebel first so that Ma Chao, in his rage, would march against Licheng in person, while Liang Kuan and his party would seal the gates of Ji behind him."

sentences.zh: 約誓以定，叙遂進兵入鹵，昂、奉守祁山。

translations.literal: When the covenant oath was settled, Xu then advanced troops into Lu; Ang and Feng guarded Mount Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Once the oath was sworn, Jiang Xu marched into Lucheng while Zhao Ang and Yin Feng held Qishan.

sentences.zh: 超聞，果自出擊叙，寬等從後閉冀門，超失據。

translations.literal: When Chao heard, indeed personally went out to strike Xu; Kuan and others from behind closed the Ji gate; Chao lost his foothold.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao heard the news and led his host against Jiang Xu as planned; Liang Kuan and the others shut the gates of Ji behind him, leaving Ma Chao without a base.

sentences.zh: 過鹵，叙守鹵。

translations.literal: Passing Lu, Xu guarded Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao passed through Lucheng, where Jiang Xu stood ready.

sentences.zh: 超因進至歷，歷中見超往，以爲叙軍還。

translations.literal: Chao therefore advanced to Li; within Li seeing Chao go, they thought Xu's army had returned.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed on to Licheng. The townsfolk, seeing Ma Chao's banners, mistook them for Jiang Xu's column returning.

sentences.zh: 又傳聞超以走奔漢中，故歷無備。

translations.literal: Also rumor spread that Chao had fled to Hanzhong; therefore Li had no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors also claimed that Ma Chao had fled to Hanzhong, so Licheng lowered its guard.

sentences.zh: 及超入歷，執叙母，母怒罵超。

translations.literal: When Chao entered Li, he seized Xu's mother; the mother angrily reviled Chao.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Chao entered the town he seized Jiang Xu's mother, who reviled him to his face.

sentences.zh: 超被罵大怒，即殺叙母及其子，燒城而去。

translations.literal: Chao, reviled, was greatly angry; immediately killed Xu's mother and her son, burned the city and left.
translations.idiomatic: Stung by her curses, he slew her and her son, fired the town, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 阜等以狀聞，太祖甚嘉之，手令襃揚，語如本傳。

translations.literal: Fu and others reported the situation; the Grand Progenitor greatly praised them, personally issued orders of commendation, words as in the main biography.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fu and his allies reported these deeds to Cao Cao, who praised them warmly and issued a personal decree of commendation, as recorded in the main text.

sentences.zh: 臣松之案：謐稱阜爲叙姑子，而本傳云叙爲阜外兄，與今名內外爲不同。

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi investigates: Mi called Fu Xu's aunt's son, yet the main biography says Xu is Fu's elder cousin on the mother's side; with present names inside and outside are different.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes that Huangfu Mi calls Yang Fu Jiang Xu's cousin by marriage, whereas the principal biography makes Jiang Xu Yang Fu's maternal cousin—the relationship is described differently.

sentences.zh: 謐又載趙昂妻曰：趙昂妻異者，故益州刺史天水趙偉璋妻，王氏女也。

translations.literal: Mi also records Zhao Ang's wife, saying: Zhao Ang's wife Yi was the daughter of the Wang clan, wife of former Yi Province Inspector Zhao Weizhang of Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Mi further records Zhao Ang's wife: Lady Yi, of the Wang clan, was the wife of Zhao Weizhang of Tianshui, the former inspector of Yi Province.

sentences.zh: 昂爲羌道令，留異在西。

translations.literal: Ang was magistrate of Qiangdao, left Yi in the west.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ang served as magistrate of Qiangdao, leaving his wife Yi in the west.

sentences.zh: 會同郡梁雙反，攻破西城，害異兩男。

translations.literal: When fellow commandery Liang Shuang rebelled, broke and took Xicheng, killed Yi's two sons.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang Shuang of the same commandery revolted, stormed Xicheng, and slew Lady Yi's two sons,

sentences.zh: 異女英，年六歲，獨與異在城中。

translations.literal: Yi's daughter Ying, age six, alone was with Yi in the city.
translations.idiomatic: six-year-old Ying alone remained in the city with her mother.

sentences.zh: 異見兩男已死，又恐爲雙所侵，引刀欲自刎，顧英而歎曰：「身死爾棄，當誰恃哉！

translations.literal: Yi saw both sons already dead, also feared violation by Shuang; drew knife wishing to kill herself, looked at Ying and sighed saying: "If body dies you are abandoned, whom shall you rely on!
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yi, seeing both sons dead and fearing rape at Liang Shuang's hands, drew a knife to end her life, then looked at Ying and sighed, "If I die I leave you helpless—

sentences.zh: 吾聞西施蒙不絜之服，則人掩鼻，況我貌非西施乎？

translations.literal: I have heard when Xishi put on unclean garments, people covered their noses; moreover my appearance is not Xishi's?
translations.idiomatic: I have read that when Xi Shi wore foul clothing passersby hid their noses—and I am no beauty like Xi Shi."

sentences.zh: 」乃以溷糞涅麻而被之，尠食瘠形，自春至冬。

translations.literal: Then with privy filth smeared hemp and covered herself, ate little emaciated body, from spring to winter.
translations.idiomatic: She smeared herself with filth from the privy and wrapped her body in rough hemp, ate sparingly, and wasted away from spring until winter."

sentences.zh: 雙與州郡和，異竟以是免難。

translations.literal: Shuang with the province and commandery made peace; Yi by this in the end escaped calamity.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang Shuang made peace with the authorities, Lady Yi survived the ordeal.

sentences.zh: 昂遣吏迎之，未至三十里，止謂英曰：「婦人無符信保傅，則不出房闈。

translations.literal: Ang sent an official to welcome her; not yet thirty li, she stopped and said to Ying: "For a woman without tally-token or nurse-mentor, then does not leave inner chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ang sent a clerk to escort them home. Thirty li short of the city she halted and told Ying, "A woman without credentials or a chaperone does not step beyond her inner rooms."

sentences.zh: 昭姜沈流，伯姬待燒，每讀其傳，心壯其節。

translations.literal: The Zhao maiden who drowned herself in the deep current, Bo Ji who waited for the consuming fire; each time I read their biographies, my heart is stirred by their integrity.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhao maiden who sank into the river, the princess Bo Ji who stayed to burn—whenever I read their tales my spirit rises at their resolve."

sentences.zh: 今吾遭亂不能死，將何以復見諸姑？

translations.literal: Now I meet chaos yet cannot die; with what shall I again see the various aunts?
translations.idiomatic: Now I have lived through rebellion without dying—how can I face my husband's kinswomen?"

sentences.zh: 所以偷生不死，惟憐汝耳。

translations.literal: The reason I stole life and did not die is only pitying you.
translations.idiomatic: The only reason I clung to life was pity for you."

sentences.zh: 今官舍已近，吾去汝死矣。

translations.literal: Now the official quarters are near; I go from you and die.
translations.idiomatic: The yamen is close now. I leave you and mean to die."

sentences.zh: 」遂飲毒藥而絕。

translations.literal: Then drank poison drug and cut off.
translations.idiomatic: She swallowed poison.

sentences.zh: 時適有解毒藥良湯，撅口灌之，良乆迺蘇。
