translations.literal: At the time there happened to be antidote medicine good broth; they pried open the mouth and poured it in; after a long time then revived.
translations.idiomatic: Someone forced an antidote down her throat, and after a long while she stirred again.

sentences.zh: 建安中，昂轉參軍事，徙居冀。

translations.literal: In the Jian-an era, Ang transferred to military staff, moved residence to Ji.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jian-an years Zhao Ang was posted to military staff and moved his household to Ji.

sentences.zh: 會馬超攻冀，異躬著布韝，佐昂守備，又悉脫所佩環、黼黻以賞戰士。

translations.literal: When Ma Chao attacked Ji, Yi personally wore cloth arm-guards, assisted Ang in defense, also entirely removed the rings she wore and embroidered sashes to reward fighting soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Chao besieged Ji, Lady Yi donned plain armlets and helped Zhao Ang hold the walls, stripping off her jewelry and silks to reward the defenders.

sentences.zh: 及超攻急，城中饑困，刺史韋康素仁，愍吏民傷殘，欲與超和。

translations.literal: When Chao's attack pressed urgently, within the city hunger and distress, Inspector Wei Kang by nature was benevolent, pitied officials and people wounded and maimed, wished to make peace with Chao.
translations.idiomatic: As the siege tightened and hunger gripped the city, the kindly Inspector Wei Kang, grieving for his battered people, wished to treat with Ma Chao.

sentences.zh: 昂諫不聽，歸以語異，異曰：「君有爭臣，大夫有專利之義；

translations.literal: Ang remonstrated and was not listened to; returned and told Yi; Yi said: "The lord has contentious ministers; a great officer has the righteousness of acting on his own authority;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ang's remonstrance went unheeded. When he told his wife, she said, "A ruler should heed outspoken ministers, and a minister may act without waiting for orders when duty demands it;"

sentences.zh: 專不爲非也。

translations.literal: to act on one's own is not to do wrong.
translations.idiomatic: to seize the initiative is not wrongdoing."

sentences.zh: 焉知救兵不到關隴哉？

translations.literal: How know relief troops will not reach Pass and Long?
translations.idiomatic: Who can say relief will never reach the Long frontier?"

sentences.zh: 當共勉卒高勳，全節致死，不可從也。

translations.literal: Ought together encourage to the end high merit, preserve integrity unto death; cannot follow this.
translations.idiomatic: We must steel ourselves to win glory and die for the cause—we cannot consent to surrender."

sentences.zh: 」比昂還，康與超和。

translations.literal: By the time Ang returned, Kang had made peace with Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Before Zhao Ang could return, Wei Kang had already capitulated to Ma Chao.

sentences.zh: 超遂背約害康，又劫昂，質其嫡子月於南鄭。

translations.literal: Chao then betrayed the covenant and harmed Kang, also coerced Ang, taking his legitimate son Yue as hostage at Nan Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao broke faith, murdered Wei Kang, seized Zhao Ang, and held his heir Yue hostage at Nan'zheng.

sentences.zh: 欲要昂以爲己用，然心未甚信。

translations.literal: Wished to require Ang to be used by himself, yet in the heart not very trusting.
translations.idiomatic: He meant to employ Zhao Ang but still did not trust him fully.

sentences.zh: 超妻楊聞異節行，請與讌終日。

translations.literal: Chao's wife Yang heard of Yi's integrity and conduct, requested to feast with her a whole day.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao's wife Lady Yang, hearing of Lady Yi's virtue, asked to spend a day feasting with her.

sentences.zh: 異欲信昂於超以濟其謀，謂楊曰：「昔管仲入齊，立九合之功；

translations.literal: Yi wished to make Ang trusted by Chao in order to advance their plot; said to Yang: "Of old when Guan Zhong entered Qi, he established the merit of nine alliances;
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yi meant to win Ma Chao's confidence in Zhao Ang and further their plot. She told Lady Yang, "When Guan Zhong entered Qi he forged the league of nine hegemons;"

sentences.zh: 由余適秦，穆公成霸。

translations.literal: You Yu went to Qin, Duke Mu accomplished hegemony.
translations.idiomatic: when You Yu went west, Duke Mu of Qin rose to supremacy."

sentences.zh: 方今社稷初定，治亂在於得人，涼州士馬，迺可與中夏爭鋒，不可不詳也。

translations.literal: Just now the altars of soil and grain are first settled; ordering chaos lies in obtaining the right men; Liangzhou's soldiers and horses, then can contend with the Central Plain—cannot not examine in detail.
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty is only now taking shape, and order depends on winning the right men. Liangzhou's cavalry can match the heartland—this is not a detail you can afford to overlook."

sentences.zh: 」楊深感之，以爲忠於己，遂與異重相接結。

translations.literal: Yang was deeply moved by this, thought her loyal to herself, then with Yi heavily continued connecting.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yang was moved, believed Lady Yi spoke for her own good, and grew intimate with her.

sentences.zh: 昂所以得信於超，全功免禍者，異之力也。

translations.literal: The reason Ang obtained trust from Chao, whole merit avoiding disaster, was Yi's force.
translations.idiomatic: It was Lady Yi's doing that Zhao Ang won Ma Chao's trust and escaped harm while the plot matured.

sentences.zh: 及昂與楊阜等結謀討超，告異曰：「吾謀如是，事必萬全，當柰月何？

translations.literal: When Ang with Yang Fu and others bound in conspiracy to punish Chao, told Yi saying: "Our plot is thus; the affair must be ten thousand times secure; what shall we do about Yue?
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Ang and Yang Fu prepared to strike Ma Chao, he confided in Lady Yi, "The plan is sound, but what of our son Yue?"

sentences.zh: 」異厲聲應曰：「忠義立於身，雪君父之大恥，喪元不足爲重，況一子哉？

translations.literal: Yi in stern voice replied saying: "Loyalty and righteousness are established in the person; to wipe away the great shame of lord and father, losing the head is not enough to weigh as heavy, moreover one son!
translations.idiomatic: She answered sharply, "Honor is built in one's own breast. To avenge our lord and master matters more than my life—what is one child?"

sentences.zh: 夫項託、顏淵，豈復百年，貴義存耳。

translations.literal: As for Xiang Tuo and Yan Yuan, how again a hundred years; precious is righteousness existing only.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Tuo and Yan Yuan did not live a century; what endures is the righteousness they left behind."

sentences.zh: 」昂曰：「善。

translations.literal: Ang said: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ang said, "Well spoken."

sentences.zh: 」遂共閉門逐超，超奔漢中，從張魯得兵還。

translations.literal: Then together closed the gates driving out Chao; Chao fled to Hanzhong, from Zhang Lu obtained troops and returned.
translations.idiomatic: They barred the gates, drove Ma Chao out, and he fled to Hanzhong, where Zhang Lu gave him troops for a counterattack.

sentences.zh: 異復與昂保祁山，爲超所圍，三十日救兵到，乃解。

translations.literal: Yi again with Ang guarded Mount Qi, was besieged by Chao; thirty days relief troops arrived, then was relieved.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yi joined Zhao Ang in defending Qishan; Ma Chao besieged them thirty days until relief broke the siege.

sentences.zh: 超卒殺異子月。

translations.literal: Chao in the end killed Yi's son Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao later executed their son Yue.

sentences.zh: 凡自冀城之難，至于祁山，昂出九奇，異輒參焉。〉

translations.literal: From the Ji city difficulty, reaching Mount Qi, Ang produced nine stratagems, Yi always joined therein.〉
translations.idiomatic: From the fall of Ji to the stand at Qishan, Zhao Ang devised nine stratagems, and Lady Yi had a hand in each."

sentences.zh: 太祖征漢中，以阜爲益州刺史。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor campaigned against Hanzhong, appointed Fu as Inspector of Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao marched on Hanzhong he named Yang Fu inspector of Yi Province.

sentences.zh: 還，拜金城太守，未發，轉武都太守。

translations.literal: Returned, appointed Administrator of Jincheng, before setting out, transferred to Administrator of Wudu.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was named administrator of Jincheng, but before he could take up the post he was shifted to Wudu.

sentences.zh: 郡濵蜀漢，阜請依龔遂故事，安之而已。

translations.literal: The commandery bordered Shu and Han; Fu requested to follow Gong Sui's old precedent, pacify them and that is all.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery lay on the border of Shu; Yang Fu asked leave to follow Gong Sui's example and soothe the people without needless severity.

sentences.zh: 會劉備遣張飛、馬超等從沮道趣下辯，而氐雷定等七部萬餘落反應之。

translations.literal: When Liu Bei sent Zhang Fei, Ma Chao, and others by the Ju road to hurry toward Xiabian, and Di chieftain Lei Ding and seven divisions of more than ten thousand settlements rebelled in response.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei dispatched Zhang Fei and Ma Chao along the Ju valley toward Xiabian, and Lei Ding of the Di with seven tribes of more than ten thousand tents rose in support.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣都護曹洪禦超等，超等退還。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor sent Chief Protector Cao Hong to resist Chao and others; Chao and others retreated and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao sent Chief Protector Cao Hong to check Ma Chao, who then drew back.

sentences.zh: 洪置酒大會，令女倡著羅縠之衣，蹋鼓，一坐皆笑。

translations.literal: Hong set wine and held a great banquet, ordered female entertainers to wear gauze thin robes, tread the drum; the whole seat all laughed.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Hong gave a victory feast and had singing girls dance in sheer silk before the drum while the guests roared with laughter.

sentences.zh: 阜厲聲責洪曰：「男女之別，國之大節，何有於廣坐之中裸女人形體！

translations.literal: Fu in stern voice rebuked Hong saying: "Distinction between man and woman is the state's great norm; how can there be, in the midst of a broad sitting, exposing women's naked forms!
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fu rebuked him sharply: "The separation of the sexes is a pillar of public decency—how dare you parade women's bodies before a hall full of men?"

sentences.zh: 雖桀、紂之亂，不甚於此。

translations.literal: Although Jie and Zhou's chaos, not worse than this.
translations.idiomatic: Even the debauchery of Jie and Zhou went no further than this."

sentences.zh: 」遂奮衣辭出。

translations.literal: Then flung garment and took leave to go out.
translations.idiomatic: He threw down his napkin and walked out.

sentences.zh: 洪立罷女樂，請阜還坐，肅然憚焉。

translations.literal: Hong immediately stopped the female music, requested Fu to return to seat, was solemn and feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Hong dismissed the musicians, begged Yang Fu back to his place, and afterward treated him with wary respect.

sentences.zh: 及劉備取漢中以逼下辯，太祖以武都孤遠，欲移之，恐吏民戀土。

translations.literal: When Liu Bei took Hanzhong to press Xiabian, the Grand Progenitor because Wudu was isolated and distant, wished to move it, feared officials and people clung to the soil.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bei seized Hanzhong to threaten Xiabian, Cao Cao considered Wudu too remote and planned to evacuate the commandery, yet feared the people would not wish to leave their land.

sentences.zh: 阜威信素著，前後徙民、氐，使居京兆、扶風、天水界者萬餘戶，徙郡小槐里，百姓襁負而隨之。

translations.literal: Fu's authority and trustworthiness long had been manifest; before and after moving people and Di, those made to dwell within the borders of Jingzhao, Fufeng, and Tianshui were more than ten thousand households; moved the commandery to minor Huaili; the hundred surnames carried infants on back and followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fu's prestige had long stood high; he had already resettled more than ten thousand households of commoners and Di between Jingzhao, Fufeng, and Tianshui, and when he shifted the seat to minor Huaili the people shouldered their children and followed without demur.

sentences.zh: 爲政舉大綱而已，下不忍欺也。

translations.literal: In governing he raised only the great outline; subordinates could not bear to deceive him.
translations.idiomatic: He governed by broad principles alone, and his subordinates would not dream of deceiving him.

sentences.zh: 文帝問侍中劉曄等：「武都太守何如人也？

translations.literal: Wendi asked Palace Attendant Liu Ye and others: "What manner of man is the Administrator of Wudu?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen asked his attendants Liu Ye and the rest, "What sort of man is the administrator of Wudu?"

sentences.zh: 」皆稱阜有公輔之節。

translations.literal: They all praised Fu as having the bearing of a minister fit for the highest office.
translations.idiomatic: Every one of them said Yang Fu had the stature of a man who could serve as chief minister.

sentences.zh: 未及用，會帝崩。

translations.literal: Before he could be employed to that end, the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: He was not promoted in time: Emperor Wen passed away first.

sentences.zh: 在郡十餘年，徵拜城門校尉。

translations.literal: After more than ten years in the commandery, he was summoned and appointed Colonel of the City Gates.
translations.idiomatic: He spent over a decade in Wudu, then was recalled and named colonel of the city gates.

sentences.zh: 阜常見明帝著𧛕，被縹綾半裦袖，阜問帝曰：「此於禮何法服也？

translations.literal: Fu often saw Emperor Ming wearing a cap, draped in pale gauze half-sleeved jacket; Fu asked the emperor: "By ritual, what sort of regulated dress is this?
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fu once found Emperor Ming in a cap and a short pale-silk jacket and asked, "What canonical garment is this by the rites?"

sentences.zh: 」帝默然不荅，自是不法服不以見阜。

translations.literal: The emperor was silent and did not answer; from this time onward he did not receive Fu except in full court dress.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave no reply, and thereafter he never received Yang Fu unless he was properly robed.

sentences.zh: 遷將作大匠。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Court Architect.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to the post of court architect.

sentences.zh: 時初治宮室，發美女以充後庭，數出入弋獵。

translations.literal: At the time they had begun building palace halls, drafted beautiful women to fill the rear quarters, and repeatedly went out hunting.
translations.idiomatic: Palace construction had just begun, the inner apartments were being filled with selected women, and the emperor often rode out on the chase.

sentences.zh: 秋，大雨震電，多殺鳥雀。

translations.literal: In autumn came heavy rain, thunder, and lightning, and many birds and sparrows were struck dead.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn storms broke, lightning flashed, and countless small birds were killed.

sentences.zh: 阜上疏曰：「臣聞明主在上，羣下盡辭。

translations.literal: Fu submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant has heard that when an enlightened sovereign sits above, his ministers speak their minds to the last word.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fu presented a memorial: "I have read that when a wise ruler holds the throne, his officials leave nothing unsaid."

sentences.zh: 堯、舜聖德，求非索諫；

translations.literal: Yao and Shun in their sage virtue sought out faults and solicited remonstrance;
translations.idiomatic: Yao and Shun in their holiness invited criticism and welcomed frank advice;

sentences.zh: 大禹勤功，務卑宮室；

translations.literal: Great Yu toiled at his task and kept his halls humble;
translations.idiomatic: the Great Yu earned merit through labor and disdained lofty palaces;

sentences.zh: 成湯遭旱，歸咎責己；

translations.literal: Cheng Tang met drought and laid the blame on himself;
translations.idiomatic: Tang of Shang faced drought and blamed his own rule;

sentences.zh: 周文刑於寡妻，以御家邦；

translations.literal: King Wen set the standard for his consorts and thereby ordered his household and state;
translations.idiomatic: King Wen taught restraint to his wives and so brought order to clan and kingdom;

sentences.zh: 漢文躬行節儉，身衣弋綈：此皆能昭令問，貽厥孫謀者也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Han personally practiced thrift and wore coarse silk—each of these could display a shining reputation and bequeath wise counsel to posterity.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Han lived plainly and dressed in homespun—all these rulers won renown and left their heirs a pattern worth following."

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下奉武皇帝開拓之大業，守文皇帝克終之元緒，誠宜思齊往古聖賢之善治，總觀季世放盪之惡政。

translations.literal: Humbly I reflect that Your Majesty inherits the great enterprise Martial Emperor opened and expands, and upholds the founding work Civil Emperor brought to completion; you truly ought to aspire to the good government of the ancient sages and survey at a glance the vicious rule of fallen ages.
translations.idiomatic: You inherit the realm Martial Emperor carved out and the order Civil Emperor perfected; you should measure yourself against the sage-kings of antiquity and take warning from every decadent late reign."

sentences.zh: 所謂善治者，務儉約、重民力也；

translations.literal: What is called good government is to insist on frugality and to cherish the people's strength;
translations.idiomatic: Good government means austerity and respect for the people's labor;

sentences.zh: 所謂惡政者，從心恣欲，觸情而發也。

translations.literal: what is called vicious government is to follow one's whims, stirred by mere appetite.
translations.idiomatic: bad government means indulging every impulse of the heart."

sentences.zh: 惟陛下稽古世代之初所以明赫，及季世所以衰弱至于泯滅，近覽漢末之變，足以動心誡懼矣。

translations.literal: Only let Your Majesty study how each dynasty blazed bright at its founding and withered at its close until it perished; take to heart the convulsions at the end of Han—enough to stir the soul and teach fear.
translations.idiomatic: Trace how each house shone at its dawn and guttered at its dusk; ponder the Han collapse—it should freeze the blood."

sentences.zh: 曩使桓、靈不廢高祖之法，文、景之恭儉，太祖雖有神武，於何所施其能邪？

translations.literal: If long ago Huan and Ling had not cast aside the laws of the High Founder and the sober thrift of Emperors Wen and Jing, even if the Grand Progenitor had possessed divine martial prowess, where could he have displayed it?
translations.idiomatic: Had Emperors Huan and Ling not torn down Gaozu's statutes and Wen and Jing's frugality, our martial founder, for all his genius, would have had no opening to act."

sentences.zh: 而陛下何由處斯尊哉？

translations.literal: Then by what path would Your Majesty occupy this exalted seat?
translations.idiomatic: On what foundation, then, would you sit on the throne today?"

sentences.zh: 今吳、蜀未定，軍旅在外，願陛下動則三思，慮而後行，重慎出入，以往鑒來，言之若輕，成敗甚重。

translations.literal: Now Wu and Shu are not yet pacified and armies stand in the field; I pray that whenever Your Majesty stirs, you will think thrice, deliberate, and then act, and that you will weigh every outing and return, taking past error as a mirror for the future—words may sound slight, yet success or failure hang upon them.
translations.idiomatic: Wu and Shu still stand unconquered and our hosts are abroad. May every move you make be thrice weighed; look before you leap; guard each coming and going; let past mistakes instruct the future—speech is easy, but the stakes are immense."

sentences.zh: 頃者天雨，又多卒暴雷電非常，至殺鳥雀。

translations.literal: Recently Heaven has sent rain and sudden, violent lightning out of season, killing birds and sparrows.
translations.idiomatic: Of late the skies have poured rain and unleashed freakish thunderbolts that have struck down birds in flocks."

sentences.zh: 天地神明，以王者爲子也，政有不當，則見災譴。

translations.literal: Heaven, earth, and the spirits regard the Son of Heaven as their child; when government goes awry, they show reproof through calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth treat the king as a son; when policy goes wrong, they answer with portents and scourges."

sentences.zh: 克己內訟，聖人所記。

translations.literal: To discipline oneself and search one's heart is what the sages commend.
translations.idiomatic: Self-scrutiny and inward reckoning are what the sages enjoin."

sentences.zh: 惟陛下慮患無形之外，慎萌纖微之初，法漢孝文出惠帝美人，令得自嫁；

translations.literal: Only let Your Majesty guard against disaster before it takes shape and nip evil in its first faint sprout; follow Emperor Xiao of Han, who released Emperor Hui's palace women and allowed them to marry as they chose;
translations.idiomatic: Guard against unseen peril and crush mischief at the bud; follow Han Emperor Wen, who freed Hui's palace ladies to find husbands of their own;

sentences.zh: 頃所調送小女，遠聞不令，宜爲後圖。

translations.literal: as for the young girls lately drafted and sent in, I have heard from afar that the order was harsh—you should plan for their future.
translations.idiomatic: and as for the little girls recently impressed into service, distant rumor says the levy was cruel—you should think ahead for them as well."

sentences.zh: 諸所繕治，務從約節。

translations.literal: In all building and repair, demand strict economy.
translations.idiomatic: Let every new work be done with the utmost frugality."

sentences.zh: 書曰：『九族旣睦，恊和萬國。

translations.literal: The Document 《Shang shu》 says: "When the nine branches of the kin are at peace, harmony reaches the myriad states."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says, "Harmonize the nine kin, and the myriad regions will be at peace."

sentences.zh: 』事思厥宜，以從中道，精心計謀，省息費用。

translations.literal: In every matter weigh what is fitting, follow the middle way, plan with care, and cut waste.
translations.idiomatic: Weigh each policy for fitness, keep to the golden mean, scheme with a clear mind, and spare the treasury."

sentences.zh: 吳、蜀以定，爾乃上安下樂，九親熈熈。

translations.literal: When Wu and Shu are pacified, then above will rest secure and below will rejoice, and the nine kin will flourish in warmth.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wu and Shu are subdued, ruler and people will be at ease and the royal kin will thrive in concord."

sentences.zh: 如此以往，祖考心歡，堯舜其猶病諸。

translations.literal: If you govern thus, the hearts of the ancestral spirits will be glad—yet even Yao and Shun would call such perfection hard to attain.
translations.idiomatic: Continue in this spirit and the shades of your forebears will rejoice—though even Yao and Shun would call that standard almost too high to meet."

sentences.zh: 今宜開大信於天下，以安衆庶，以示遠人。

translations.literal: Now you should open great trust throughout the realm to reassure the common people and signal sincerity to those beyond your borders.
translations.idiomatic: Now is the time to broadcast steadfast faith across the empire, steady the common folk, and show distant lands that you mean peace."

sentences.zh: 」時雍丘王植怨於不齒，藩國至親，法禁峻密，故阜又陳九族之義焉。

translations.literal: At the time Prince Zhi of Yongqiu nursed a grievance at being passed over for office; the princely houses were the emperor's closest kin, yet the laws binding them were harsh—therefore Fu also expounded the meaning of harmony among the nine kin.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Prince Cao Zhi of Yongqiu smarted at his exclusion from power; the imperial clansmen were bone of the ruler's bone, yet they labored under suffocating restrictions—so Yang Fu enlarged on the duty of harmony within the nine branches of kin."

sentences.zh: 詔報曰：「閒得密表，先陳往古明王聖主，以諷闇政，切至之辭，款誠篤實。

translations.literal: An edict replied: "I have lately received a sealed memorial that first rehearses the enlightened kings of antiquity in order to criticize dark governance; the language cuts to the quick and the devotion is genuine.
translations.idiomatic: The throne answered, "Your sealed memorial rehearses the sage-kings of old to reproach present failings; your words bite to the bone and your loyalty is plain."

sentences.zh: 退思補過，將順匡救，備至悉矣。

translations.literal: In retirement you reflect on mending faults, will comply and rescue—your care is exhaustive.
translations.idiomatic: You withdraw to mend what is wrong, you would guide and save—the thoroughness of your care leaves nothing out."

sentences.zh: 覽思苦言，吾甚嘉之。」

translations.literal: Having read and pondered these bitter truths, I greatly approve of them."
translations.idiomatic: I have weighed your hard counsel and approve it with all my heart."

sentences.zh: 後遷少府。

translations.literal: Later he was promoted to Minister of the Less Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He was later advanced to minister of the less treasury.

sentences.zh: 是時大司馬曹真伐蜀，遇雨不進。

translations.literal: At that time Grand Marshal Cao Zhen campaigned against Shu but was halted by rain and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Cao Zhen was then leading an expedition against Shu but had bogged down in the rains.

sentences.zh: 阜上疏曰：「昔文王有赤烏之符，而猶日仄不暇食；

translations.literal: Fu submitted a memorial saying: "Of old King Wen had the omen of the red crow, yet still the sun slanted and he had no leisure to eat;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fu wrote, "King Wen received the red-bird portent, yet the sun was past the meridian before he could eat;

sentences.zh: 武王白魚入舟，君臣變色。

translations.literal: when King Wu saw the white fish leap into his boat, ruler and ministers changed color.
translations.idiomatic: when King Wu saw the white fish leap into the barge, he and his ministers blanched."

sentences.zh: 而動得吉瑞，猶尚憂懼，況有災異而不戰竦者哉？

translations.literal: Even when their actions drew auspicious signs, they still trembled with fear—how much more, when Heaven sends prodigies, should we not be shaken to the marrow?
translations.idiomatic: Even good omens left them anxious—how much more, when Heaven sends warnings, ought we not stand aghast?"

sentences.zh: 今吳、蜀未平，而天屢降變，陛下宜深有以專精應荅，側席而坐，思示遠以德，綏邇以儉。

translations.literal: Now Wu and Shu are not yet subdued, yet Heaven has repeatedly sent strange portents; Your Majesty should respond with concentrated reverence, sit as though off the mat in apprehension, win the distant through virtue, and soothe those near you through thrift.
translations.idiomatic: Wu and Shu still defy us while omens pile up; you should answer with single-minded awe, hold court as if the mat were uneven, draw the far lands with virtue, and comfort your own people with restraint."

sentences.zh: 閒者諸軍始進，便有天雨之患，稽閡山險，以積日矣。

translations.literal: Lately, as soon as the armies marched, they were stopped by rain, blocked in the mountain defiles, and have remained stuck for many days.
translations.idiomatic: No sooner did the hosts move than storms penned them in the passes, and they have been stuck there day after day."

sentences.zh: 轉運之勞，擔負之苦，所費以多，若有不繼，必違本圖。

translations.literal: The strain on transport and bearers has already cost a fortune; if supplies fail, the original plan will collapse.
translations.idiomatic: The cost in carts and bearers mounts hourly; if the line breaks, the whole design fails."

sentences.zh: 傳曰：『見可而進，知難而退，軍之善政也。

translations.literal: The tradition says: "Advance when you see your chance, withdraw when you know the odds—such is the good government of armies."
translations.idiomatic: The military maxim runs, "Strike when the moment favors you, retire when the terrain forbids—that is sound command."

sentences.zh: 』徒使六軍困於山谷之間，進無所略，退又不得，非主兵之道也。

translations.literal: To leave the six hosts stranded in the valleys, unable to advance for plunder or to retire without loss, is not the way of one who commands troops.
translations.idiomatic: To trap the imperial army between cliffs with no ground to win and no road to retreat is no way to lead soldiers."

sentences.zh: 武王還師，殷卒以亡，知天期也。

translations.literal: When King Wu drew back his host, the Yin soldiers perished of themselves—he read Heaven's appointed hour.
translations.idiomatic: King Wu turned his legions about and Yin collapsed of its own accord—he had read Heaven's timetable aright."

sentences.zh: 今年凶民饑，宜發明詔損膳減服，技巧珍玩之物，皆可罷之。

translations.literal: This year brings ill omens and famine among the people; issue a clear edict to cut palace meals and wardrobe, and suspend every ingenious toy and costly trifle.
translations.idiomatic: The year is inauspicious and the people are starving; proclaim a public order to reduce court fare and dress and to scrap ingenious luxuries."

sentences.zh: 昔邵信臣爲少府於無事之世，而奏罷浮食；

translations.literal: In peaceful times Shao Xinchen, as minister of the less treasury, memorialized to abolish superfluous offices;
translations.idiomatic: In an age without crises Shao Xinchen pruned useless offices from the less treasury;

sentences.zh: 今者軍用不足，益宜節度。

translations.literal: now that military expenditure falls short, restraint is all the more imperative."
translations.idiomatic: now that the army strains the treasury, economy is twice as urgent."

sentences.zh: 」帝即召諸軍還。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon recalled every army.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at once ordered all columns home.

sentences.zh: 後詔大議政治之不便於民者，阜議以爲：「致治在於任賢，興國在於務農。

translations.literal: Later an edict called for wide debate on policies that harmed the people; Fu argued that "order depends on employing the worthy, and the state flourishes when agriculture is honored.
translations.idiomatic: An edict later invited debate on burdensome policies; Yang Fu held that "good rule rests on choosing able men, and a strong realm rests on farming."

sentences.zh: 若舍賢而任所私，此忘治之甚者也。

translations.literal: To cast aside the worthy and promote one's favorites is the worst forgetfulness of good government.
translations.idiomatic: To spurn talent and elevate favorites is the gravest neglect of governance."

sentences.zh: 廣開宮館，高爲臺榭，以妨民務，此害農之甚者也。

translations.literal: To throw open endless lodges and raise towering terraces at the cost of the people's labor is the worst injury to farming.
translations.idiomatic: To multiply palaces and pavilions at the expense of peasant labor is the gravest wound to agriculture."

sentences.zh: 百工不敦其器，而競作奇巧，以合上欲，此傷本之甚者也。

translations.literal: When craftsmen neglect their proper work and vie to produce curiosities to please their superiors, the root of the state is deeply harmed.
translations.idiomatic: When artisans abandon useful craft to chase novelties for the court, the foundations of the realm are undermined."

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：『苛政甚於猛虎。

translations.literal: Confucius said: "Harsh government is fiercer than a tiger."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "Cruel rule is worse than a tiger."

sentences.zh: 』今守功文俗之吏，爲政不通治體，苟好煩苛，此亂民之甚者也。

translations.literal: Today the petty clerks who cling to precedent neither grasp the principles of rule nor shrink from petty harassment—this is the worst way to vex the people.
translations.idiomatic: Petty officials who cling to paperwork, never grasp how government should work, and delight in nagging regulations are the worst plague on the commoners."

sentences.zh: 當今之急，宜去四甚，並詔公卿郡國，舉賢良方正敦樸之士而選用之，此亦求賢之一端也。」

translations.literal: The pressing task is to remove these four excesses and to order the high ministers and the commanderies to recommend upright, plain, and honest men for appointment—such is another path to finding worthies."
translations.idiomatic: Urgent business is to strike these four evils and command the nobles and provinces to nominate honest, plain-spoken talent—that too is a road to worthy ministers."

sentences.zh: 阜又上疏欲省宮人諸不見幸者，乃召御府吏問後宮人數。

translations.literal: Fu again memorialized, asking to reduce the number of palace women who enjoyed no favor, and summoned the clerk of the imperial wardrobe to ask how many women were in the rear apartments.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fu again asked to release neglected palace ladies and sent for the wardrobe clerk to learn the size of the harem.

sentences.zh: 吏守舊令，對曰：「禁密，不得宣露。

translations.literal: The clerk clung to the old rule and answered: "It is forbidden and secret; I may not disclose it."
translations.idiomatic: The clerk cited the standing rule: "The figure is classified; I cannot reveal it."

sentences.zh: 」阜怒，杖吏一百，數之曰：「國家不與九卿爲密，反與小吏爲密乎？

translations.literal: Fu grew angry, had him beaten a hundred strokes, and rebuked him: "Does the state keep its secrets from the Nine Ministers only to share them with petty clerks?"
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fu had him flogged a hundred blows and shouted, "Are state secrets withheld from the Nine Ministers yet whispered to underlings?"

sentences.zh: 」帝聞而愈敬憚阜。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard this, he respected and feared Fu all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming, hearing the story, only esteemed Yang Fu the more—and feared his tongue.

sentences.zh: 帝愛女淑，未期而夭，帝痛之甚，追封平原公主，立廟洛陽，葬於南陵。

translations.literal: The emperor's beloved daughter Shu died before her first year; he grieved her bitterly, posthumously enfeoffed her as Princess of Pingyuan, built a temple in Luoyang, and buried her at Nanling.
translations.idiomatic: His favorite daughter Shu died in infancy; in his grief he posthumously titled her Princess of Pingyuan, raised a shrine in Luoyang, and laid her to rest at Nanling.

sentences.zh: 將自臨送，阜上疏曰：「文皇帝、武宣皇后崩，陛下皆不送葬，所以重社稷、備不虞也。

translations.literal: He was about to attend the funeral in person when Fu memorialized: "When Emperor Wen and Empress Wu Xuan died, Your Majesty did not go to the burials, precisely to honor the altars of state and guard against the unforeseen.
translations.idiomatic: As he prepared to follow the cortège, Yang Fu wrote, "You stayed away from the funerals of Emperor Wen and Empress Dowager Bian to shield the altars of state and leave no opening to danger."

sentences.zh: 何至孩抱之赤子而可送葬也哉？

translations.literal: How can an infant still in swaddling clothes warrant the risk of a royal funeral train?"
translations.idiomatic: Would you now hazard the succession for a child still in blankets?"

sentences.zh: 」帝不從。

translations.literal: The emperor did not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 帝旣新作許宮，又營洛陽宮殿觀閣。

translations.literal: The emperor had just built the palace at Xu and was now raising halls and belvederes in Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He had just finished the Xu palace and was already raising new towers in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 阜上疏曰：「堯尚茅茨而萬國安其居，禹卑宮室而天下樂其業；

translations.literal: Fu memorialized: "Yao was content with thatched roofs, yet the myriad regions dwelt in peace; Yu kept his halls low, yet the realm rejoiced in its labors;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fu wrote, "Yao lived under thatch and the world kept house in peace; Yu kept his halls low and all men gladly toiled;"

sentences.zh: 及至殷、周，或堂崇三尺，度以九筵耳。

translations.literal: by the time of Yin and Zhou, some audience halls rose only three feet and were measured in spans of nine mats.
translations.idiomatic: under Yin and Zhou the grand hall stood three feet high and nine mats across—no more."

sentences.zh: 古之聖帝明王，未有極宮室之高麗以彫弊百姓之財力者也。

translations.literal: Never did the sage-kings of old exhaust the wealth and strength of the people to build palaces of impossible splendor.
translations.idiomatic: No wise founder ever beggared his people to pile up marble and gold."

sentences.zh: 桀作琁室、象廊，紂爲傾宮、鹿臺，以喪其社稷，楚靈以築章華而身受其禍；

translations.literal: Jie built the Jade Chamber and Ivory Gallery; Zhou raised the Leaning Palace and the Deer Terrace—and lost his altars; King Ling of Chu reared the Zhanghua Terrace and brought calamity on himself.
translations.idiomatic: Jie raised the Jade Chamber and Ivory Gallery; Zhou built the Leaning Tower and Deer Terrace and lost the throne; King Ling of Chu built Zhanghua and perished by it."

sentences.zh: 秦始皇作阿房而殃及其子，天下叛之，二世而滅。

translations.literal: The First Emperor of Qin built Epang, and disaster overtook his heir; the realm rose against him, and the line died in two reigns.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Shihuang piled up Epang and ruin reached his son—the empire rebelled and the line ended in two generations."

sentences.zh: 夫不度萬民之力，以從耳目之欲，未有不亡者也。

translations.literal: Whoever ignores the strength of the people to gratify eye and ear has never long survived.
translations.idiomatic: No ruler who spends the people without measure to please his senses has long endured."

sentences.zh: 陛下當以堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武爲法則，夏桀、殷紂、楚靈、秦皇爲深誡。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should take Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu as your models and Jie of Xia, Zhou of Shang, King Ling of Chu, and the Qin First Emperor as your warnings.
translations.idiomatic: Take Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu as your pattern and Jie, Zhou, King Ling, and the First Emperor as your mirror."

sentences.zh: 高高在上，實監后德。

translations.literal: "Lofty High Above" truly watches the virtue of those who follow."
translations.idiomatic: Heaven on high truly watches the virtue of kings."

sentences.zh: 慎守天位，以承祖考，巍巍大業，猶恐失之。

translations.literal: Guard the Mandate with care to carry on your ancestors; even this towering enterprise may yet slip away.
translations.idiomatic: Guard the Mandate handed down by your forebears—this great enterprise can still be lost."

sentences.zh: 不夙夜敬止，允恭卹民，而乃自暇自逸，惟宮臺是侈是飾，必有顛覆危亡之禍。

translations.literal: If you do not revere duty morning and night, show sincere pity for the people, but instead idle in ease and lavish ornament on palace towers, you invite the doom of overturn.
translations.idiomatic: If you neglect dawn-to-dusk vigilance, fail in compassion for the people, and idle while palaces climb ever higher, you court ruin."

sentences.zh: 易曰：『豐其屋，蔀其家，闚其戶，閴其無人。

translations.literal: The Changes says: "He enlarges his house, screens his family, peers at his door, and finds it empty and still."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes reads, "He roofs his hall too high, blinds his household, peers through the gate, and meets silence—no one within."

sentences.zh: 』王者以天下爲家，言豐屋之禍，至於家無人也。

translations.literal: The king takes all under Heaven as his household; the text warns that when halls swell too large, the house may stand empty.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven owns the realm as his house; the verse means that vainglorious building ends in desolation."

sentences.zh: 方今二虜合從，謀危宗廟，十萬之軍，東西奔赴，邊境無一日之娛；

translations.literal: Today the two rebels stand in league and plot against the ancestral shrines; hosts of a hundred thousand hurry east and west, and the frontier knows no day of rest;
translations.idiomatic: The two enemy states league against us; armies of a hundred thousand race along the frontiers without pause;

sentences.zh: 農夫廢業，民有饑色。

translations.literal: farmers abandon their fields and the people show the pallor of hunger.
translations.idiomatic: the plow lies idle and the people wear famine on their faces."

sentences.zh: 陛下不以是爲憂，而營作宮室，無有已時。

translations.literal: Yet Your Majesty does not grieve over this but keeps raising palaces without end.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you fret not over that, but pour labor into endless palaces."

sentences.zh: 使國亡而臣可以獨存，臣又不言也；

translations.literal: If the state were to perish yet your servant could survive alone, your servant would still not keep silence;
translations.idiomatic: If the dynasty could fall while I alone might outlive it, I could not hold my peace;

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之以爲忠至之道，以亡己爲理。

translations.literal: 〈Your servant Songzhi considers that the way of utmost loyalty takes self-annihilation as its principle.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi comments: the path of perfect loyalty is to forget the self—

sentences.zh: 是以匡救其惡，不爲身計。

translations.literal: Therefore one corrects and saves evil in the ruler, not calculating for one's own body.
translations.idiomatic: one corrects the ruler's faults without reckoning personal cost."

sentences.zh: 而阜表云「使國亡而臣可以獨存，臣又不言也」，此則發憤爲己，豈爲國哉？

translations.literal: Yet Fu's memorial says, "If the state were to perish yet your servant could survive alone, your servant would still not keep silence"—is this not indignation for oneself rather than for the state?
translations.idiomatic: Yet the sentence "If the realm could fall while I survived, I would not stay silent" reads like private pique, not devotion to the altars."

sentences.zh: 斯言也，豈不傷讜烈之義，爲一表之病乎！〉

translations.literal: Such language surely mars the meaning of blunt integrity and is a blemish on an otherwise noble memorial.〉
translations.idiomatic: Such wording jars with fearless integrity and mars an otherwise splendid memorial."

sentences.zh: 君作元首，臣爲股肱，存亡一體，得失同之。

translations.literal: The lord is the head and his ministers the limbs; they share life and death, gain and loss alike.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler is the head, the ministers the limbs—we live or perish together, prosper or fail as one."

sentences.zh: 孝經曰：『天子有爭臣七人，雖無道不失其天下。

translations.literal: The Classic of Filial Piety says: "If the Son of Heaven has seven ministers who remonstrate with him, even without the Way he will not lose the realm."
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Filial Piety says, "Give the Son of Heaven seven ministers who dare remonstrate, and he will not lose the realm though he stray from the Way."

sentences.zh: 』臣雖駑怯，敢忘爭臣之義？

translations.literal: " Though your servant is dull and timid, how dare he forget the duty of a remonstrating minister?
translations.idiomatic: Though I am slow and faint-hearted, would I forget the office of a remonstrating minister?"

sentences.zh: 言不切至，不足以感寤陛下。

translations.literal: Unless the words cut to the quick, they cannot awaken Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Unless the words wound, they will not rouse you."

sentences.zh: 陛下不察臣言，恐皇祖烈考之祚，將墜于地。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty does not heed your servant's counsel, I fear the blessing won by your imperial ancestors will crash to earth.
translations.idiomatic: If you brush this aside, the mandate won by your august forebears may crumble to dust."

sentences.zh: 使臣身死有補萬一，則死之日，猶生之年也。

translations.literal: If my death could avail one chance in ten thousand, the day I die would still be a day I had lived to purpose.
translations.idiomatic: If my death could help the throne one jot, I would count the day of execution as a day of life."

sentences.zh: 謹叩棺沐浴，伏俟重誅。

translations.literal: I therefore knock upon my coffin, bathe, and await the axe."
translations.idiomatic: I have bathed and stand ready at my coffin, awaiting sentence."

sentences.zh: 」奏御，天子感其忠言，手筆詔荅。

translations.literal: When the memorial reached the throne, the Son of Heaven was moved by his loyal words and answered with an edict in his own hand.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read it and was stirred; he answered with a brush-written rescript.

sentences.zh: 每朝廷會議，阜常侃然以天下爲己任。

translations.literal: Whenever the court met in council, Fu spoke bluntly and shouldered the realm as his own charge.
translations.idiomatic: At every court conference Yang Fu spoke as though the fate of the empire rested on him alone.

sentences.zh: 數諫爭，不聽，乃屢乞遜位，未許。

translations.literal: Time after time he remonstrated; when his advice went unheeded, he repeatedly begged to resign, but permission was never granted.
translations.idiomatic: He remonstrated again and again, and when he was ignored he asked to retire—yet the throne would not release him."

sentences.zh: 會卒，家無餘財。

translations.literal: When he died, his household had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: He died leaving no hoarded wealth.

sentences.zh: 孫豹嗣。

translations.literal: His grandson Bao inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Yang Bao inherited the fief.

sentences.zh: 高堂隆

translations.literal: Gaotang Long.
translations.idiomatic: Gaotang Long.

sentences.zh: 高堂隆字升平，泰山平陽人，魯高堂生後也。

translations.literal: Gaotang Long courtesy name Shengping, was a man of Pingyang in Taishan, a descendant of the Lu scholar Gaotang Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Gaotang Long, courtesy name Shengping, came from Pingyang in Taishan and traced his line to the classical master Gaotang Sheng of Lu.

sentences.zh: 少爲諸生，泰山太守薛悌命爲督郵。

translations.literal: In youth he was a student; the Taishan Administrator Xue Ti appointed him Chief of the Postal Stations.
translations.idiomatic: As a young scholar he was named chief of postal stations by Xue Ti, the Taishan administrator.

sentences.zh: 郡督軍與悌爭論，名悌而呵之。

translations.literal: The commandery's military overseer disputed with Ti, called Ti by his personal name and berated him.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery's army supervisor quarreled with Xue Ti, addressed him by his private name, and shouted him down.

sentences.zh: 隆按劒叱督軍曰：「昔魯定見侮，仲尼歷階；

translations.literal: Long grasped his sword and rebuked the military overseer: "Of old when Duke Ding of Lu was insulted, Confucius mounted the steps in wrath;
translations.idiomatic: Gaotang Long seized his sword and cried, "When Duke Ding of Lu was slighted, Confucius sprang up the hall steps;

sentences.zh: 趙彈秦箏，相如進缶。

translations.literal: when the King of Zhao played the Qin zither, Xiang Ru advanced the fou drum.
translations.idiomatic: when the King of Zhao strummed the Qin zither, Lin Xiang Ru stepped forward with the clay drum."

sentences.zh: 臨臣名君，義之所討也。

translations.literal: For a subject facing his lord to call the ruler by name is what righteousness condemns.
translations.idiomatic: For an underling to bandy his lord's personal name is a crime against duty."

sentences.zh: 」督軍失色，悌驚起止之。

translations.literal: The military overseer lost color; Ti rose in alarm and stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: The supervisor turned pale; Xue Ti leapt up to restrain Long.

sentences.zh: 後去吏，避地濟南。

translations.literal: Later he left office and took refuge in Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: He later resigned and fled to Jinan for safety.

sentences.zh: 建安十八年，太祖召爲丞相軍議掾，後爲歷城侯徽文學，轉爲相。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Jian-an, the Grand Progenitor summoned him as a consultant on the staff of the chancellor; afterward he became literary instructor to Marquis Hui of Licheng, then was promoted to chancellor of the estate.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian-an 18 (213) Cao Cao named him a staff adviser to the chancellor, then tutor in letters to Cao Hui, Marquis of Licheng, and finally chancellor of that princely household.

sentences.zh: 徽遭太祖喪，不哀，反游獵馳騁；

translations.literal: When Hui met the Grand Progenitor's death, he did not mourn but instead went hunting and galloping;
translations.idiomatic: Cao Hui showed no grief at Cao Cao's death but rode out to hunt;

sentences.zh: 隆以義正諫，甚得輔導之節。

translations.literal: Long with righteous remonstrance corrected him and fully observed the bearing of a tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Gaotang Long rebuked him on grounds of duty and comported himself as a true mentor should.

sentences.zh: 黃初中，爲堂陽長，以選爲平原王傅。

translations.literal: In the Huang-chu era he became magistrate of Tangyang and, on selection, tutor to the Prince of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: During Huangchu he served as magistrate of Tangyang and was then chosen as tutor to the Prince of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 王即尊位，是爲明帝。

translations.literal: The prince ascended the exalted seat; this was Emperor Ming.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince took the throne he became Emperor Ming.

sentences.zh: 以隆爲給事中、博士、駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: Long was appointed Palace Attendant, Erudite, and Commandant of the Horse for the imperial sons-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Gaotang Long received appointments as palace attendant, erudite, and commandant of convoy for the princesses' consorts.

sentences.zh: 帝初踐阼，羣臣或以爲宜響會，隆曰：「唐、虞有遏密之哀，高宗有不言之思，是以至德雍熈，光于四海。

translations.literal: When the emperor first mounted the throne, some ministers thought a celebratory assembly should be held; Long said: "Tang and Yu observed the hushed mourning of E-mi; the High Ancestor of Shang kept silent in reflection—thereby their supreme virtue spread in harmony and their light filled the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the reign some courtiers urged a public celebration; Gaotang Long said, "The sage-kings Tang and Yu mourned in silence; Gaozong of Shang spoke not for three years—thus their perfect virtue shone and filled the realm."

sentences.zh: 」以爲不宜爲會，帝敬納之。

translations.literal: He held that an assembly should not be held; the emperor respectfully accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: He argued against the feast, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 遷陳留太守。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Administrator of Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to administrator of Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 犢民酉牧，年七十餘，有至行，舉爲計曹掾；

translations.literal: Du min You Mu, more than seventy years old, had consummate conduct and was nominated clerk of the accounts bureau;
translations.idiomatic: A local man named You Mu, past seventy and famed for virtue, was nominated clerk of the accounts bureau;

sentences.zh: 帝嘉之，特除郎中以顯焉。

translations.literal: the emperor praised this and specially appointed him gentleman of the interior to honor him.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor commended the choice and specially named him a gentleman of the interior.

sentences.zh: 徵隆爲散騎常侍，賜爵關內侯。

translations.literal: Long was summoned as Regular Attendant of the Gentlemen of the Household and granted rank as secondary marquis within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Gaotang Long was recalled to serve as regular attendant of the household gentlemen and given the rank of secondary marquis within the passes.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：太史上漢歷不及天時，因更推步弦望朔晦，爲太和歷。

translations.literal: The Wei lüe says: The Grand Clerk reported that the Han calendar fell short of celestial phenomena; therefore they recalculated the phases of new and full moon and produced the Taihe calendar.
translations.idiomatic: The Brief Account of Wei states that the grand clerk found the Han calendar out of step with Heaven and recomputed lunations to draft the Taihe calendar.

sentences.zh: 帝以隆學問優深，於天文又精，乃詔使隆與尚書郎楊偉、太史待詔駱祿參共推校。

translations.literal: Because Long's learning was profound and he was also expert in astronomy, an edict ordered Long with Palace Gentleman Yang Wei and awaiting-edict astrologer Luo Lu jointly to verify the computations.
translations.idiomatic: Since Gaotang Long's scholarship ran deep and he excelled at astronomy, the court paired him with Yang Wei of the secretariat and the astrologer Luo Lu to cross-check the new system.

sentences.zh: 偉、祿是太史，隆故據舊歷更相劾奏，紛紜數歲，偉稱祿得日蝕而月晦不盡，隆不得日蝕而月晦盡，詔從太史。

translations.literal: Wei and Lu were of the Grand Clerk's office; Long therefore relied on the old calendar and they impeached one another in turn; for several years the dispute raged; Wei claimed Lu caught solar eclipses while the last day of the month was not fully dark, Long failed on eclipses yet had the last day fully dark—the edict followed the Grand Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wei and Luo Lu belonged to the astrological bureau, while Gaotang Long defended the older tables; they traded memorials of accusation for years. Wei argued that Lu predicted eclipses but misjudged the darkness of month-end, whereas Long missed eclipses yet matched month-end darkness—the throne ruled in favor of the bureau.

sentences.zh: 隆所爭雖不得，而遠近猶知其精微也。〉

translations.literal: Although Long's side did not prevail, near and far still knew his subtle mastery.〉
translations.idiomatic: Gaotang Long lost the debate, yet everyone acknowledged his mathematical finesse."

sentences.zh: 青龍中，大治殿舍，西取長安大鍾。

translations.literal: In the Qinglong era they built palace halls on a grand scale and fetched the great bell from Chang'an in the west.
translations.idiomatic: During Qinglong the court raised vast halls and sent west for the great bell that had hung at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 隆上疏曰；

translations.literal: Long submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Gaotang Long presented a memorial:

sentences.zh: 「昔周景王不儀刑文、武之明德，忽公旦之聖制，旣鑄大錢，又作大鍾，單穆公諫而弗聽，泠州鳩對而弗從，遂迷不反，周德以衰，良史記焉，以爲永鑒。

translations.literal: "Of old King Jing of Zhou did not take as his model the bright virtue of Wen and Wu, spurned the sage institutions of the Duke of Zhou, cast great cash coins, and cast a great bell; Duke Shan of Shan remonstrated and he would not listen, Leng Zhoujiu answered him and he would not follow—thus he wandered without return and Zhou virtue declined; good historians recorded it as an everlasting mirror.
translations.idiomatic: "King Jing of Zhou spurned the shining examples of Wen and Wu, ignored the Duke of Zhou's institutions, minted giant coins, and hung a giant bell; Duke Shan remonstrated in vain, Leng Zhoujiu spoke to no avail, and the king wandered ever deeper into folly until Zhou power waned—the scribes set that tale before posterity as a warning."

sentences.zh: 然今之小人，好說秦、漢之奢靡以盪聖心，求取亡國不度之器，勞役費損，以傷德政，非所以興禮樂之和，保神明之休也。

translations.literal: Yet today's petty men love to cite the extravagance of Qin and Han to shake the sage mind, seeking instruments that helped bring down states without measuring fitness, wasting labor and treasure to harm virtuous rule—this is no way to raise the harmony of ritual and music or preserve the repose of the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Petty flatterers now retail Qin and Han excess to sway you, bidding you fetch tokens of fallen dynasties without thought of measure, bleeding the people to wound good government—such is no path to ritual harmony or the gods' blessing."

sentences.zh: 」是日，帝幸上方，隆與卞蘭從。

translations.literal: " That day the emperor visited Shangfang; Long followed with Bian Lan.
translations.idiomatic: That very day the emperor toured the imperial workshops; Gaotang Long accompanied him with Bian Lan.

sentences.zh: 帝以隆表授蘭，使難隆曰：「興衰在政，樂何爲也？

translations.literal: The emperor handed Long's memorial to Lan and had him challenge Long: "Rise and fall lie in government—what has music to do with it?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave Bian Lan Gaotang Long's memorial and told him to press the point: "Order rests with policy—what has a bell to do with it?"

sentences.zh: 化之不明，豈鍾之罪？

translations.literal: If transformation is unclear, is it the bell's crime?"
translations.idiomatic: If moral suasion fails, can you blame a bronze?"

sentences.zh: 」隆曰：「夫禮樂者，爲治之大本也。

translations.literal: Long said: "Ritual and music are the great root of good order.
translations.idiomatic: Gaotang Long answered, "Rites and music are the taproot of governance."

sentences.zh: 故簫韶九成，鳳皇來儀，雷鼓六變，天神以降，政是以平，刑是以錯，和之至也。

translations.literal: Therefore when the Shao pipe played its nine movements, the phoenix came in courtly dance; when the thunder drum sounded its six changes, the spirits of Heaven descended—by this government was balanced and punishments set aside; such is the summit of harmony.
translations.idiomatic: When the nine sections of Shao were played, phoenixes came to dance; when the thunder drum rolled through six changes, the gods descended—thus punishments fell idle and the realm was tuned to perfection."

sentences.zh: 新聲發響，商辛以隕，大鍾旣鑄，周景以弊，存亡之機，恒由斯作，安在廢興之不階也？

translations.literal: When new tunes rang out, Shang Xin perished; when the great bell was cast, King Jing of Zhou stumbled—whether a state stands or falls always hinges on such things; how can rise and fall lack steps?
translations.idiomatic: Novel music undid King Zhou of Shang; the giant bell undid King Jing of Zhou—fortune and ruin turn on such choices; do you imagine dynastic fate has no rungs?"

sentences.zh: 君舉必書，古之道也，作而不法，何以示後？

translations.literal: The ruler's every deed must be written—such is the way of antiquity; if you act without law, how will you instruct posterity?
translations.idiomatic: The scribes record a sovereign's every act; to act outside the norm is to leave posterity no pattern."

sentences.zh: 聖王樂聞其闕，故有箴規之道；

translations.literal: Sage kings delight to hear their faults; therefore there is the path of admonition;
translations.idiomatic: Sage kings welcome word of their failings and keep advisers at hand;

sentences.zh: 忠臣願竭其節，故有匪躬之義也。

translations.literal: loyal ministers wish to exhaust their integrity; therefore there is the duty of forgetting self for the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: loyal ministers burn to give their utmost and forget private safety for the throne."

sentences.zh: 」帝稱善。

translations.literal: The emperor praised him as right.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor conceded the point.

sentences.zh: 遷侍中，猶領太史令。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Palace Attendant while still holding the post of Grand Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to palace attendant and kept concurrent charge as grand clerk.

sentences.zh: 崇華殿災，詔問隆：「此何咎？

translations.literal: The Chonghua Hall caught fire; an edict asked Long: "What fault does this signify?
translations.idiomatic: When Chonghua Hall burned, the emperor asked Gaotang Long, "What reproof does this carry?"

sentences.zh: 於禮，寧有祈禳之義乎？

translations.literal: By the rites, is there meaning in prayer to avert calamity?"
translations.idiomatic: Does ritual allow us to pray it away?"

sentences.zh: 」隆對曰：

translations.literal: Long replied:
translations.idiomatic: Gaotang Long answered:

sentences.zh: 夫災變之發，皆所以明教誡也，惟率禮脩德，可以勝之。

translations.literal: When calamitous portents appear, they are all meant to instruct and warn; only by leading with ritual and cultivating virtue can one overcome them.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven sends warnings to teach the throne; only ritual conduct and moral cultivation can answer them."

sentences.zh: 易傳曰：『上不儉，下不節，孽火燒其室。

translations.literal: The Yi commentary says: "If those above are not frugal and those below are not restrained, baleful fire will burn their chambers."
translations.idiomatic: The tradition on the Changes reads, "When those aloft waste and those below spend, a curse of fire consumes the hall."

sentences.zh: 』又曰：『君高其臺，天火爲災。

translations.literal: It also says: "If the ruler raises his terrace high, Heaven sends fire as disaster."
translations.idiomatic: It adds, "When the king piles his towers high, Heaven answers with flame."

sentences.zh: 』此人君苟飾宮室，不知百姓空竭，故天應之以旱，火從高殿起也。

translations.literal: This means that when a ruler vainly adorns palace chambers without seeing that the people are emptied, Heaven answers with drought and fire begins in the high halls.
translations.idiomatic: The gloss means a king who decks out palaces while the people are drained will meet drought from Heaven and fire that starts in the loftiest roof."

sentences.zh: 上天降鑒，故譴告陛下；

translations.literal: High Heaven lowers its mirror and therefore rebukes and informs Your Majesty;
translations.idiomatic: Heaven lowers its bright mirror and so warns Your Majesty;

sentences.zh: 陛下宜增崇人道，以荅天意。

translations.literal: Your Majesty ought to exalt the human way to answer Heaven's mind.
translations.idiomatic: you should magnify humane rule to match its intent."

sentences.zh: 昔太戊有桑穀生於朝，武丁有雊雉登於鼎，皆聞災恐懼，側身脩德，三年之後，遠夷朝貢，故號曰中宗、高宗。

translations.literal: Of old Taiwu had mulberry and grain sprout in his court; Wuding had a crowing pheasant alight on his cauldron—each heard of the portent with fear, straightened his person, and cultivated virtue; after three years distant barbarians came to court, and therefore they were styled Middle Ancestor and High Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu of Shang saw freak mulberry in the courtyard; Wuding saw a shrieking pheasant on the tripod—both trembled, mended their ways, and within three years distant peoples paid tribute, earning the titles Middle and High Ancestor."

sentences.zh: 此則前代之明鑒也。

translations.literal: These are clear mirrors of earlier ages.
translations.idiomatic: They are plain mirrors from antiquity."

sentences.zh: 今案舊占，災火之發，皆以臺榭宮室爲誡。

translations.literal: Now examining old prognostications, the outbreak of baleful fire always takes towers and palace chambers as its warning.
translations.idiomatic: Old divination books agree that such fires warn against terraces and halls."

sentences.zh: 然今宮室之所以充廣者，實由宮人猥多之故。

translations.literal: Yet the reason palace chambers have swollen so wide today is truly the multitude of palace women.
translations.idiomatic: The reason your halls have swollen is the swarm of palace women."

sentences.zh: 宜簡擇留其淑懿，如周之制，罷省其餘。

translations.literal: You ought to select and keep the virtuous and fair, as Zhou's institutions prescribed, and dismiss the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Winnow the inner court, keep the virtuous as Zhou did, and send the surplus away."

sentences.zh: 此則祖乙之所以訓高宗，高宗之所以享遠號也。

translations.literal: This is how Zu Yi instructed Gaozong, and how Gaozong won his far-reaching title.
translations.idiomatic: So Zu Yi taught Gaozong of Shang, and Gaozong won his glorious temple name."

sentences.zh: 」詔問隆：「吾聞漢武帝時，栢梁災，而大起宮殿以厭之，其義云何？

translations.literal: " An edict asked Long: "I have heard that under Emperor Wu of Han, when the Bailiang Terrace burned, he raised great palaces to suppress it—what was the meaning?"
translations.idiomatic: The throne then asked, "When Emperor Wu's Bailiang Terrace burned, he built still grander palaces to ward off the omen—what sense had that?"

sentences.zh: 」隆對曰：「臣聞西京栢梁旣災，越巫陳方，建章是經，以厭火祥；

translations.literal: Long replied: "Your servant has heard that after the western capital's Bailiang burned, Yue wizards offered a formula, so the Weaving Palaces rose to quell the fire omen;
translations.idiomatic: Gaotang Long said, "When the western capital's Bailiang burned, southern shamans peddled a rite and the Weaving Palaces went up to counter the fire omen;"

sentences.zh: 乃夷越之巫所爲，非聖賢之明訓也。

translations.literal: this was the work of barbarian Yue wizards, not the clear teaching of sages worthies.
translations.idiomatic: that was barbarian sorcery, not the teaching of the sages."

sentences.zh: 五行志曰：『栢梁災，其後有江充巫蠱也，衞太子事。

translations.literal: The Treatise on the Five Phases says: "After the Bailiang fire came Jiang Chong's witchcraft and the affair of Crown Prince Wei."
translations.idiomatic: The Han Treatise on the Five Phases records that after the Bailiang blaze came Jiang Chong's witch-hunt and the ruin of Crown Prince Wei."

sentences.zh: 』如志之言，越巫建章無所厭也。

translations.literal: According to that record, the Yue wizards' Weaving Palaces accomplished no suppression.
translations.idiomatic: By that account the shamans' new halls averted nothing."

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：『災者脩類應行，精祲相感，以戒人君。

translations.literal: Confucius said: "Calamities are categories responding to conduct; essences and influences mutually touch to warn the lord of men."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "Disasters match deeds; subtle forces answer one another to warn the ruler."

sentences.zh: 』是以聖主覩災責躬，退而脩德，以消復之。

translations.literal: Therefore the sage sovereign, seeing calamity, blames himself, withdraws, and cultivates virtue to dispel and restore.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the sage king, seeing a portent, blames himself, retires to mend his virtue, and turns the omen aside."

sentences.zh: 今宜罷散民役。

translations.literal: Now you should dismiss scattered corvée among the people.
translations.idiomatic: Now dismiss the people's forced labor gangs."

sentences.zh: 宮室之制，務從約節，內足以待風雨，外足以講禮儀。

translations.literal: Palace construction should insist on austerity: within enough to shelter from wind and rain, without enough to conduct ritual and ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Let halls be modest—roof enough for wind and rain, courtyard enough for rites."

sentences.zh: 清埽所災之處，不敢於此有所立作，萐莆、嘉禾必生此地，以報陛下虔恭之德。

translations.literal: Sweep clear the burned ground and dare not raise new work there; then the lucky grain and the sha-pu plant will spring from that soil to repay Your Majesty's reverent virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Clear the scorched earth and build nothing new there; lucky grain and auspicious sha-pu will sprout to answer your reverence."

sentences.zh: 豈可疲民之力，竭民之財！

translations.literal: How can one exhaust the people's strength and drain the people's wealth!
translations.idiomatic: You cannot beggar strength and treasure out of the people!"

sentences.zh: 實非所以致符瑞而懷遠人也。

translations.literal: That is truly not the way to summon auspicious tokens and cherish those from afar.
translations.idiomatic: That is no way to draw omens of grace or win distant peoples."

sentences.zh: 帝遂復崇華殿，時郡國有九龍見，故改曰九龍殿。

translations.literal: The emperor nonetheless rebuilt Chonghua Hall; at the time commanderies reported nine dragons appearing, so it was renamed Hall of Nine Dragons.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuilt Chonghua anyway; because nine dragons were reported in the provinces he renamed it the Hall of Nine Dragons.

sentences.zh: 陵霄闕始構，有鵲巢其上，帝以問隆，對曰：「詩云『惟鵲有巢，惟鳩居之』。

translations.literal: As the Lingxiao Gate tower was first framed, magpies built nests on it; the emperor asked Long, who answered: "The Odes say, 'The magpie has its nest; the turtledove dwells in it.'"
translations.idiomatic: When carpenters began the Lingxiao watchtower, magpies nested on the timbers. Gaotang Long quoted the Odes: "The magpie builds the nest; the dove takes it."

sentences.zh: 今興宮室，起陵霄闕，而鵲巢之，此宮室未成身不得居之象也。

translations.literal: Now we raise palace chambers and rear the Lingxiao gate, yet magpies nest there—this is the image of the chambers unfinished and the person unable to dwell in them.
translations.idiomatic: You raise towers to the clouds, yet birds claim them first—a sign that the halls are unfinished and no Son of Heaven yet owns them."

sentences.zh: 天意若曰，宮室未成，將有他姓制御之，斯乃上天之戒也。

translations.literal: Heaven's meaning seems to say: the chambers are not finished; another surname will control them—this is a warning from on high.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven seems to warn that the palace is not yours to finish—that another house will seize the throne."

sentences.zh: 夫天道無親，惟與善人，不可不深防，不可不深慮。

translations.literal: The way of Heaven shows no partiality; it aids only the good—you must guard against this deeply and ponder it deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven is impartial and helps only the virtuous—ponder that with care."

sentences.zh: 夏、商之季，皆繼體也，不欽承上天之明命，惟讒諂是從，廢德適欲，故其亡也忽焉。

translations.literal: The ends of Xia and Shang were both legitimate heirs who would not reverently accept Heaven's bright charge but followed slander and flattery, cast aside virtue and chased appetite—therefore their perishing came in a flash.
translations.idiomatic: The last kings of Xia and Shang were lawful heirs who spurned Heaven's charge, heeded flatterers, and abandoned virtue for lust—so they fell overnight."

sentences.zh: 太戊、武丁，覩災竦懼，祗承天戒，故其興也勃焉。

translations.literal: Taiwu and Wuding, seeing portents, stood in dread and respectfully accepted Heaven's warning—therefore their rise was sudden.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu and Wuding trembled at omens and answered Heaven—so they rose with equal speed."

sentences.zh: 今若休罷百役，儉以足用，增崇德政，動遵帝則，除普天之所患，興兆民之所利，三王可四，五帝可六，豈惟殷宗轉禍爲福而已哉！

translations.literal: If now we halt the hundred corvées, keep thrift so supplies suffice, exalt virtuous government, move in accord with the Five Emperors' norms, remove what all the realm dreads, and advance what the myriad people desire, then the Three Kings could become four and the Five Emperors six—how would that be merely the Shang house turning calamity into fortune!
translations.idiomatic: End the levies, live within your means, lift good rule, walk as the Five Emperors walked, lift the people's burdens and grant their wishes, and you could outshine the Three Kings and match six emperors—far more than copying Shang's escape from disaster!"

sentences.zh: 臣備腹心，苟可以繁祉聖躬，安存社稷，臣雖灰身破族，猶生之年也。

translations.literal: Your servant stands in the innermost circle; if aught can multiply the blessings of the sacred person and keep the altars secure, though your servant's body be ground to ash and his clan destroyed, it would still be a year of life.
translations.idiomatic: I am close to your heart: if my death could heap blessings on you and steady the state, I would count annihilation of my kin a living year."

sentences.zh: 豈憚忤逆之災，而令陛下不聞至言乎？

translations.literal: How could I fear the disaster of disobedience and keep Your Majesty from hearing utmost truth?
translations.idiomatic: Would I shrink from offending you and leave you deaf to honest counsel?"

sentences.zh: 」於是帝改容動色。

translations.literal: Thereupon the emperor changed expression and was moved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's face changed and he took the words to heart.

sentences.zh: 是歲，有星孛于大辰。

translations.literal: That year a comet appeared in the Great Fire asterism.
translations.idiomatic: That year a comet blazed in the Fang and Heart mansions.

sentences.zh: 隆上疏曰：「凡帝王徙都立邑，皆先定天地社稷之位，敬恭以奉之。

translations.literal: Long submitted a memorial: "Whenever emperors move the capital or found a city, they always first fix the positions of Heaven, Earth, and the altars of soil and grain, serving them with reverence.
translations.idiomatic: Gaotang Long wrote, "Kings who shift capitals first set the sites of Heaven, Earth, and the soil-and-grain shrines and serve them with awe."

sentences.zh: 將營宮室，則宗廟爲先，廄庫爲次，居室爲後。

translations.literal: When about to build palace chambers, they put the ancestral temple first, the stables and storehouses second, and dwelling quarters last.
translations.idiomatic: When they build, the ancestral temple comes first, granaries and stables second, living quarters last."

sentences.zh: 今圜丘、方澤、南北郊、明堂、社稷，神位未定，宗廟之制又未如禮，而崇飾居室，士民失業。

translations.literal: Now the round mound, the square pool, the southern and northern suburban altars, the Bright Hall, and the altars of soil and grain lack fixed spirit seats; the ancestral temple system still falls short of the rites, yet you richly adorn dwelling quarters while gentlemen and commoners lose their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: Today those sacred sites stand unsettled, the temple system still breaks ritual, yet you gild private halls while nobles and peasants lose their trades."

sentences.zh: 外人咸云宮人之用，與興戎軍國之費，所盡略齊。

translations.literal: Outsiders all say the cost of palace women roughly matches the expense of armies and the state.
translations.idiomatic: Gossip says the inner court costs as much as the army."

sentences.zh: 民不堪命，皆有怨怒。

translations.literal: The people cannot bear the decree and all harbor resentment and anger.
translations.idiomatic: The people cannot endure the levies and nurse anger."

sentences.zh: 書曰『天聦明自我民聦明，天明畏自我民明威』，輿人作頌，則嚮以五福，民怒吁嗟，則威以六極，言天之賞罰，隨民言，順民心也。

translations.literal: The Document says, 'Heaven hears as my people hear; Heaven sees as my people see'—when the multitude composes hymns, Heaven responds with the five blessings; when the people groan in anger, Heaven shows the six extremes—meaning Heaven's rewards and punishments follow the people's words and accord with the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says Heaven hears through the people's ears and sees through their eyes—when they sing praise Heaven sends the five blessings, when they sigh in wrath Heaven sends the six extremes."

sentences.zh: 是以臨政務在安民爲先，然後稽古之化，格于上下，自古及今，未嘗不然也。

translations.literal: Therefore holding government always puts pacifying the people first; only afterward does one examine antiquity's transformation so that it reaches high and low—from antiquity to now it has never been otherwise.
translations.idiomatic: Rule must settle the people first, then borrow ancient models to touch every rank—so it has always been."

sentences.zh: 夫采椽卑宮，唐、虞、大禹之所以垂皇風也；

translations.literal: Thatched rafters and low halls are how Tang, Yu, and Great Yu left a royal wind;
translations.idiomatic: Timber rafters and low roofs are how Yao, Shun, and Yu left their royal style;

sentences.zh: 玉臺瓊室，夏癸、商辛之所以犯昊天也。

translations.literal: jade towers and carnelian chambers are how Jie of Xia and Xin of Shang offended August Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: jade towers and jeweled halls are how Jie and Zhou offended Heaven."

sentences.zh: 今之宮室，實違禮度，乃更建立九龍，華飾過前。

translations.literal: Today's palace chambers truly violate ritual measure, yet you raise the Nine Dragons and outshine what went before.
translations.idiomatic: Your halls already break the rites, yet you outdo them with the Nine Dragons."

sentences.zh: 天彗章灼，始起於房心，犯帝坐而干紫微，此乃皇天子愛陛下，是以發教戒之象，始卒皆於尊位，殷勤鄭重，欲必覺寤陛下；

translations.literal: The comet blazes clear: it began in Fang and Heart, struck the Imperial Seat, and impinged on Purple Tenuity—this is August Heaven's love for Your Majesty, therefore it sends the image of instruction and warning, beginning and ending on the seats of honor, earnest and solemn, desiring surely to awaken Your Majesty;
translations.idiomatic: The comet rose in Fang and Heart, crossed the throne stars, and brushed Ziwei—Heaven cherishes you and marks the throne again and again, pressing you to wake."

sentences.zh: 斯乃慈父懇切之訓，宜崇孝子祗聳之禮，以率先天下，以昭示後昆，不宜有忽，以重天怒。」

translations.literal: this is the urgent lesson of a loving father; you should exalt the trembling filial rite of a good son to lead all under Heaven and show later generations—one ought not treat it lightly and double Heaven's anger."
translations.idiomatic: It is a father's stern lesson; answer with a son's awe, lead the realm by example, and teach posterity—do not slight it and rouse Heaven twice."

sentences.zh: 時軍國多事，用法深重。

translations.literal: At the time military and state affairs were many and the laws were applied with severity.
translations.idiomatic: Military crises multiplied and punishments grew harsh.

sentences.zh: 隆上疏曰：「夫拓跡垂統，必俟聖明，輔世匡治，亦須良佐，用能庶績其凝而品物康乂也。

translations.literal: Long submitted a memorial: "To widen the tracks and hang down the thread of succession one must await a sage brightness; to aid the age and set right the realm also requires good assistants—only then can many tasks find rest and the myriad things enjoy peace.
translations.idiomatic: Gaotang Long wrote, "Founding a line and handing down rule waits on a sage; steadying the age needs good ministers—only then do the myriad offices settle and the realm find peace."

sentences.zh: 夫移風易俗，宣明道化，使四表同風，回首面內，德教光熈，九服慕義，固非俗吏之所能也。

translations.literal: To shift custom and change habit, to proclaim and clarify the transforming way, so that the four quarters share one wind and turn their faces inward, so that virtuous instruction shines and the nine circuits yearn for righteousness—this is indeed not what vulgar clerks can accomplish.
translations.idiomatic: To change custom, spread the moral way, draw the four seas to one temper, and make distant lands face inward—no petty clerk can do that."

sentences.zh: 今有司務糾刑書，不本大道，是以刑用而不措，俗弊而不敦。

translations.literal: Now the offices busy themselves picking at penal texts and do not root themselves in the great Way—therefore punishments are used yet not set aside, custom is flawed yet not improved.
translations.idiomatic: Today yamen nitpick statutes and ignore the great Way—so punishments never end and manners never mend."

sentences.zh: 宜崇禮樂，班叙明堂，脩三雍、大射、養老，營建郊廟，尊儒士，舉逸民，表章制度，改正朔，易服色，布愷悌，尚儉素，然後備禮封禪，歸功天地，使雅頌之聲盈于六合，緝熈之化混于後嗣。

translations.literal: You ought to honor ritual and music, set in order the Bright Hall, repair the three Yong, the great archery rite, and the honoring of the aged, build suburban and ancestral temples, honor Confucian scholars, summon recluses, display institutions in edicts, change the calendar's inaugural month, alter robe colors, spread kindness, esteem plainness—only then prepare the feng and shan rites and return merit to Heaven and Earth, so that the airs and hymns fill the six directions and a radiant transformation mingles with posterity.
translations.idiomatic: Exalt rites and music, order the Bright Hall, restore the three academies, the great archery feast, and the care of the aged, build suburban shrines, honor literati, call forth hidden talent, proclaim institutions, fix the calendar, change court dress, spread mercy, prize simplicity—then you may mount feng and shan and offer merit to Heaven and Earth until song fills the realm and a gentle transformation reaches your heirs."

sentences.zh: 斯蓋至治之美事，不朽之貴業也。

translations.literal: This is the fairest work of perfect order, the noble enterprise that never decays.
translations.idiomatic: That is the crown of good rule and an immortal achievement."

sentences.zh: 然九域之內，可揖讓而治，尚何憂哉！

translations.literal: Then within the nine domains one may rule by yielding—what is left to worry about!
translations.idiomatic: Then the nine provinces may be governed with ease—what trouble remains?"

sentences.zh: 不正其本而救其末，譬猶棼絲，非政理也。

translations.literal: To neglect the root and doctor the twigs is like tangling silk—it is not the way of government.
translations.idiomatic: To ignore the root and trim the branches is to snarl the skein of rule."

sentences.zh: 可命羣公卿士通儒，造具其事，以爲典式。

translations.literal: Order the dukes, ministers, and learned Confucians to draw up the program in full and make it a lasting statute.
translations.idiomatic: Bid the high ministers and great scholars draft the program and set it as law."

sentences.zh: 」隆又以爲改正朔，易服色，殊徽號，異器械，自古帝王所以神明其政，變民耳目，故三春稱王，明三統也。

translations.literal: " Long also held that to change the calendar's first month, alter robe colors, change insignia, and vary implements is how ancient emperors made their government numinous and transformed the people's eyes and ears—therefore the three springs are called kings, clarifying the three threads.
translations.idiomatic: Gaotang Long also urged changing the inaugural month, court colors, emblems, and ritual gear—the means by which sage kings made rule numinous and renewed the people's sight and hearing—so that the three "springs" of the calendar display the three legitimate lines."

sentences.zh: 於是敷演舊章，奏而改焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon he spread out the old regulations, memorialized, and changed them.
translations.idiomatic: He laid out the classical precedents, submitted them, and the court adopted the changes.

sentences.zh: 帝從其議，改青龍五年春三月爲景初元年孟夏四月，服色尚黃，犧牲用白，從地正也。

translations.literal: The emperor followed his proposal, changing the spring third month of the fifth year of Qinglong to the first month of summer in the first year of Jingchu, robe color honoring yellow, sacrificial victims using white, following the earth's correct alignment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted: Qinglong 5, month 3, became Jingchu 1, month 4 of summer; court dress favored yellow, sacrifices used white victims, following the "earth" reckoning of the calendar.

sentences.zh: 遷光祿勳。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Supervisor of the Household.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to supervisor of the imperial household.

sentences.zh: 帝愈增崇宮殿，彫飾觀閣，鑿太行之石英，采穀城之文石，起景陽山於芳林之園，建昭陽殿於太極之北，鑄作黃龍鳳皇奇偉之獸，飾金墉、陵雲臺、陵霄闕。

translations.literal: The emperor further enlarged palace halls, carved and painted belvederes, quarried quartz from the Taihang range, took patterned stone from Gucheng, raised Mount Jingyang in the Fragrant Grove Park, built the Zhaoyang Hall north of the Great Ultimate Hall, cast yellow dragons and phoenixes and other prodigious beasts, and adorned the Metal Wall, the Cloud-Resting Terrace, and the Cloud-Piercing Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming piled on palaces: quartz from Taihang, figured marble from Gucheng, an artificial Jingyang hill in Fragrant Grove Park, Zhaoyang Hall north of the main hall, gilded bronze dragons and phoenixes, and fresh ornament for the Metal Rampart, Lingyun Tower, and Lingxiao Gate.

sentences.zh: 百役繁興，作者萬數，公卿以下至于學生，莫不展力，帝乃躬自握土以率之。

translations.literal: A hundred corvées flourished; those at work numbered in the myriads; from dukes and ministers down to students, none failed to stretch their strength, and the emperor himself grasped earth to lead them.
translations.idiomatic: Labor gangs swelled to tens of thousands; nobles, officials, even students were pressed into the dirt; the emperor took a spade himself to set the pace.

sentences.zh: 而遼東不朝。

translations.literal: Yet Liaodong did not come to court.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Liaodong withheld tribute.

sentences.zh: 悼皇后崩。

translations.literal: Empress Dao died.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager Dao passed away.

sentences.zh: 天作淫雨，冀州水出，漂沒民物。

translations.literal: Heaven sent excessive rains; Ji Province's rivers rose and swept away people and goods.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven sent ceaseless rain; Ji Province flooded and washed away lives and property.

sentences.zh: 隆上疏切諫曰：

translations.literal: Long submitted a memorial remonstrating sharply:
translations.idiomatic: Gaotang Long laid before the throne a blunt memorial:

sentences.zh: 蓋「天地之大德曰生，聖人之大寶曰位；
