translations.literal: Covering "The great virtue of Heaven and Earth is called life; the great treasure of the sage is called position;
translations.idiomatic: He quoted the Changes: "The great virtue of Heaven and Earth is life; the great treasure of the sage is his position;"

sentences.zh: 何以守位？

translations.literal: how shall one guard the position?
translations.idiomatic: "How does he guard that position?"

sentences.zh: 曰仁；

translations.literal: It is said: benevolence;
translations.idiomatic: The answer is, "With benevolence;"

sentences.zh: 何以聚人？

translations.literal: how shall one gather the people?
translations.idiomatic: "How does he gather the people?"

sentences.zh: 曰財」。

translations.literal: It is said: wealth."
translations.idiomatic: The answer is, "With wealth."

sentences.zh: 然則士民者，乃國家之鎮也；

translations.literal: Thus gentlemen and commoners are the state's ballast;
translations.idiomatic: The gentry and the people are the ballast of the state;

sentences.zh: 穀帛者，乃士民之命也。

translations.literal: grain and silk are the life of gentlemen and commoners.
translations.idiomatic: grain and silk are the lifeblood of the people."

sentences.zh: 穀帛非造化不育，非人力不成。

translations.literal: Grain and silk are not born without transforming creation, nor completed without human labor.
translations.idiomatic: Neither grain nor silk grows without Heaven's nurture nor ripens without human toil.

sentences.zh: 是以帝耕以勸農，后桑以成服，所以昭事上帝，告虔報施也。

translations.literal: Therefore the emperor plows to encourage farming, the empress tends silkworms to complete garments—thereby to display service to Supreme Heaven, declare reverence, and repay its gifts.
translations.idiomatic: So the Son of Heaven breaks clod to urge the harvest and the empress tends silkworms to supply robes—showing service to Heaven and gratitude for its bounty."

sentences.zh: 昔在伊唐，世值陽九厄運之會，洪水滔天，使鯀治之，績用不成，乃舉文命，隨山刊木，前後歷年二十二載。

translations.literal: Of old in the age of Tang of Yi, the generation met the convergence of the ninefold yang misfortune; the flood covered Heaven; they had Gun control it, but his achievement was not completed; then they raised Wenming, who followed the mountains and cut the trees—before and after it took twenty-two years.
translations.idiomatic: In high antiquity, under Yao of Tang, the age met the ninefold flood; waters covered the sky; Gun failed to dam them; Shun raised Yu, who tracked the ranges and hewed timber—twenty-two years in all before the work was done."

sentences.zh: 災眚之甚，莫過於彼，力役之興，莫久於此，堯、舜君臣，南面而已。

translations.literal: No calamity was greater than that, no labor levy longer—yet Yao and Shun, ruler and ministers, faced south and that was all.
translations.idiomatic: No disaster matched that flood, no corvée ran longer—yet Yao and Shun, king and ministers, faced south and issued orders, nothing more."

sentences.zh: 禹敷九州，庶士庸勳，各有等差，君子小人，物有服章。

translations.literal: Yu spread the nine provinces; many officers had merit, each with his rank; gentleman and petty man, things had their dress and pattern.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu divided the nine provinces, every officer earned a rank, high and low each had his insignia."

sentences.zh: 今無若時之急，而使公卿大夫並與厮徒共供事役，聞之四夷，非嘉聲也，垂之竹帛，非令名也。

translations.literal: Now we lack such urgency, yet we make dukes, ministers, and grandees labor together with convicts; when the four barbarians hear of it, it is no good report; when it is written on bamboo and silk, it is no fair name.
translations.idiomatic: Today we face no such crisis, yet we yoke nobles to the same gangs as convicts—foreigners will hear no praise of it, historians will inscribe no glory."

sentences.zh: 是以有國有家者，近取諸身，遠取諸物，嫗煦養育，故稱「愷悌君子，民之父母」。

translations.literal: Therefore those who possess state and clan take from themselves what is near and from things what is far, cherishing and nurturing—hence they are called "kindly gentlemen, fathers and mothers of the people."
translations.idiomatic: True kings nurture the people as parents, drawing lessons from near and far—hence the Odes call them "gentle and kind, fathers and mothers to the folk."

sentences.zh: 今上下勞役，疾病凶荒，耕稼者寡，饑饉荐臻，無以卒歲；

translations.literal: Now high and low labor under service, sickness and famine stalk the land, few plow the fields, hunger comes again and again, and there is no means to finish the year;
translations.idiomatic: Today corvée crushes high and low, plague and dearth spread, fields lie idle, famine returns each season, and families cannot see the year out;

sentences.zh: 宜加愍卹，以救其困。

translations.literal: you ought to add pity and relief to rescue their distress.
translations.idiomatic: add mercy and relief to save them."

sentences.zh: 臣觀在昔書籍所載，天人之際，未有不應也。

translations.literal: Your servant observes that in the books of old, wherever Heaven and man meet, there has never been a case without correspondence.
translations.idiomatic: Every record of Heaven and humanity shows they answer each other.

sentences.zh: 是以古先哲王，畏上天之明命，循陰陽之逆順，矜矜業業，惟恐有違。

translations.literal: Therefore the wise kings of antiquity feared August Heaven's bright charge, followed yin and yang in their proper order, stood in trembling awe, fearful only of straying.
translations.idiomatic: The sage-kings feared Heaven's mandate, followed the seasons, and trod softly lest they stray.

sentences.zh: 然後治道用興，德與神符，災異旣發，懼而脩政，未有不延期流祚者也。

translations.literal: Afterward the way of rule flourished through use, virtue matched the spirits, and when calamities arose they were afraid and mended government—none failed to lengthen their years and extend their blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Then good order rose, virtue matched the gods, and when portents came they mended their ways—none failed to win long reigns."

sentences.zh: 爰及末葉，闇君荒主，不崇先王之令軌，不納正士之直言，以遂其情志，恬忽變戒，未有不尋踐禍難，至於顛覆者也。

translations.literal: Down to the late generations, benighted lords and wastrel rulers did not honor the tracks of the former kings, did not accept the straight words of upright men, followed their whims and moods, treated warnings with indifference—none failed soon to tread disaster and overturn.
translations.idiomatic: Later tyrants spurned ancient models, spurned honest counsel, chased whim, shrugged at omens—and every one soon fell."

sentences.zh: 天道旣著，請以人道論之。

translations.literal: The way of Heaven is already clear; allow your servant to speak from the human way.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's lesson is plain; hear the human side as well."

sentences.zh: 夫六情五性，同在於人，嗜欲廉貞，各居其一。

translations.literal: The six emotions and five natures alike dwell in man; craving and integrity each hold one part.
translations.idiomatic: Six passions and five temperaments share one breast; desire and purity vie for a seat."

sentences.zh: 及其動也，交爭于心。

translations.literal: When they stir, they cross-fight in the heart.
translations.idiomatic: When they stir, they war within the mind."

sentences.zh: 欲彊質弱，則縱濫不禁；

translations.literal: If desire grows strong while substance grows weak, then wanton excess cannot be checked;
translations.idiomatic: If appetite outmuscles restraint, excess runs wild;

sentences.zh: 精誠不制，則放溢無極。

translations.literal: if earnest sincerity does not curb it, then dissipation knows no limit.
translations.idiomatic: if earnest intent does not rein it, dissipation knows no bound."

sentences.zh: 夫情之所在，非好則美，而美好之集，非人力不成，非穀帛不立。

translations.literal: Where emotion fixes, one loves only the beautiful, yet the gathering of the beautiful is not completed without human labor, nor established without grain and silk.
translations.idiomatic: The heart craves beauty, yet beauty costs labor and grain, not wishes alone."

sentences.zh: 情苟無極，則人不堪其勞，物不充其求。

translations.literal: If emotion knows no limit, then people cannot bear the toil and things cannot satisfy the demand.
translations.idiomatic: If passion knows no limit, men break under the work and the world cannot feed the greed."

sentences.zh: 勞求並至，將起禍亂。

translations.literal: When toil and demand meet together, rebellion will arise.
translations.idiomatic: When labor and greed collide, rebellion follows."

sentences.zh: 故不割情，無以相供。

translations.literal: Therefore without cutting emotion, there is no way to supply one another.
translations.idiomatic: Trim desire or nothing can be supplied."

sentences.zh: 仲尼云：「人無遠慮，必有近憂。

translations.literal: Zhongni said: "A man who does not think far ahead will have trouble near at hand."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "He who plans no afar will mourn at his door."

sentences.zh: 」由此觀之，禮義之制，非苟拘分，將以遠害而興治也。

translations.literal: From this we see that the regulation of ritual and righteousness is not mere pedantic division of roles; it is meant to ward off harm and raise good order.
translations.idiomatic: Rites exist not to nag petty rules but to forestall ruin and build order."

sentences.zh: 今吳、蜀二賊，非徒白地小虜、聚邑之寇，乃據險乘流，跨有士衆，僭號稱帝，欲與中國爭衡。

translations.literal: Now the two bandits of Wu and Shu are not mere white-ground petty raiders or village brigands; they hold defiles and ride the rivers, stride hosts of gentry and commoners, usurp titles and call themselves emperors, and mean to contend with the Central Plain.
translations.idiomatic: Wu and Shu are no bandit gangs: they hold river defiles, command armies, style themselves emperors, and aim at the heartland."

sentences.zh: 今若有人來告，權、備並脩德政，復履清儉，輕省租賦，不治玩好，動咨耆賢，事遵禮度。

translations.literal: Suppose someone reported that Sun Quan and Liu Bei had both cultivated virtuous government, returned to purity and thrift, lightened rents and taxes, renounced trifling pleasures, consulted the aged in every move, and acted within ritual measure.
translations.idiomatic: Picture a messenger saying Sun Quan and Liu Bei had turned frugal, cut taxes, spurned luxuries, and heeded elders—

sentences.zh: 陛下聞之，豈不惕然惡其如此，以爲難卒討滅，而爲國憂乎？

translations.literal: Would Your Majesty, on hearing this, not shrink with dread at such news, thinking them hard to destroy in the end and a worry for the state?
translations.idiomatic: would you not blanch and dread them as a lasting peril to the realm?"

sentences.zh: 若使告者曰，彼二賊並爲無道，崇侈無度，役其士民，重其徵賦，下不堪命，吁嗟日甚。

translations.literal: Suppose instead the messenger said that both rebels were without the Way, extravagant beyond measure, driving their soldiers and people, doubling levies until the lower ranks could not endure their orders and groaned louder each day.
translations.idiomatic: Suppose instead he said they wallowed in excess, drove their people, and doubled taxes until the folk groaned without end—

sentences.zh: 陛下聞之，豈不勃然忿其困我無辜之民，而欲速加之誅，其次，豈不幸彼疲弊而取之不難乎？

translations.literal: Would Your Majesty, on hearing this, not blaze with anger at their tormenting your innocent people and wish to punish them at once; next, would you not rejoice that they are exhausted and therefore easy to take?
translations.idiomatic: would you not burn to avenge your innocent subjects and then smile that weary foes are easy prey?"

sentences.zh: 苟如此，則可易心而度，事義之數亦不遠矣。

translations.literal: If it is so, then one may shift one's mind to measure them—the reckoning of right and wrong is not far off.
translations.idiomatic: Weigh the two tales and the right policy is plain."

sentences.zh: 且秦始皇不築道德之基，而築阿房之宮，不憂蕭墻之變，而脩長城之役。

translations.literal: Moreover the First Emperor of Qin did not build the foundation of virtue and morality but built the Epang Palace; he did not fear trouble within his own walls but repaired the Great Wall.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Shihuang raised Epang, not virtue; he feared not court intrigue but built the Long Wall."

sentences.zh: 當其君臣爲此計也，亦欲立萬世之業，使子孫長有天下，豈意一朝匹夫大呼，而天下傾覆哉？

translations.literal: When their ruler and ministers planned thus, they also wished to establish an enterprise for ten thousand generations and make their sons and grandsons long possess the realm—who imagined that in one morning a common fellow would shout and the realm would overturn?
translations.idiomatic: They meant to found an eternal line—who dreamed one cry would topple Qin?"

sentences.zh: 故臣以爲使先代之君知其所行必將至於敗，則弗爲之矣。

translations.literal: Therefore your servant holds that if the rulers of old had known their deeds would surely end in defeat, they would not have done them.
translations.idiomatic: Had ancient kings foreseen ruin, they would never have begun."

sentences.zh: 是以亡國之主自謂不亡，然後至於亡；

translations.literal: Thus the lords of lost states always thought themselves not lost, and then reached loss;
translations.idiomatic: Doomed kings always thought themselves safe until they fell;

sentences.zh: 賢聖之君自謂將亡，然後至於不亡。

translations.literal: sage and worthy lords always thought themselves about to perish, and then reached not perishing.
translations.idiomatic: wise kings always acted as if ruin were near—and so escaped it."

sentences.zh: 昔漢文帝稱爲賢主，躬行約儉，惠下養民，而賈誼方之，以爲天下倒縣，可爲痛哭者一，可爲流涕者二，可爲長歎息者三。

translations.literal: Of old Emperor Wen of Han was called a worthy ruler; he personally practiced austerity, showed kindness below and nurtured the people—yet Jia Yi compared him to it and thought the realm hung upside down: one matter for bitter weeping, two for tears, three for long sighing.
translations.idiomatic: Han Wendi was praised as wise, lived plainly, and loved the people—yet Jia Yi said the empire hung inverted, with one cause to weep for, two to mourn, three to sigh over."

sentences.zh: 況今天下彫弊，民無儋石之儲，國無終年之畜，外有彊敵，六軍暴邊，內興土功，州郡騷動，若有寇警，則臣懼版築之士不能投命虜庭矣。

translations.literal: Moreover today the realm is wasted, the people lack a peck of stored grain, the state lacks a year's reserve; outside stand strong foes and the six hosts stand exposed on the border; within, earthworks rise and commanderies are in turmoil—if raiders strike, I fear the men who carry mortar cannot hurl their lives at the barbarian court.
translations.idiomatic: Today the land is stripped, homes hold no peck of grain, the treasury no year's store; enemies press the frontiers while palaces rise inland—if war comes, your bricklayers cannot march to meet it."

sentences.zh: 又，將吏奉祿，稍見折減，方之於昔，五分居一；

translations.literal: Moreover the stipends of generals and clerks have been gradually cut; compared with former times they are now one part in five;
translations.idiomatic: Officers' pay has been pared to a fifth of what it was;

sentences.zh: 諸受休者又絕廩賜，不應輸者今皆出半：此爲官入兼多於舊，其所出與參少於昔。

translations.literal: those granted rest have also lost their grain allowances, and categories that once owed no tribute now pay half: this means official income is several times more than of old while what goes out to the rank and file is somewhat less than before.
translations.idiomatic: furloughed men lost their rations, and former tax exemptions now pay half—revenue rises while what reaches troops shrinks."

sentences.zh: 而度支經用，更每不足，牛肉小賦，前後相繼。

translations.literal: Yet the fiscal office's regular expenses are repeatedly insufficient, and petty levies on cattle follow one another.
translations.idiomatic: Still the budget runs short and petty beef taxes multiply."

sentences.zh: 反而推之，凡此諸費，必有所在。

translations.literal: Turn it over in thought—all these expenses must be going somewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Every coin must be going somewhere."

sentences.zh: 且夫祿賜穀帛，人主所以惠養吏民而爲之司命者也，若今有廢，是奪其命矣。

translations.literal: Moreover stipends, gifts, grain, and silk are what the lord of men uses to favor and nurture clerks and people and to be their arbiter of life; if now they are abolished, that is to seize their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Stipends are the breath of officials and people; to cut them is to strangle life."

sentences.zh: 旣得之而又失之，此生怨之府也。

translations.literal: To have obtained them and then lose them is the storehouse of resentment.
translations.idiomatic: To give bounty and then snatch it back breeds hatred."

sentences.zh: 周禮，天府掌九伐之則以給九式之用，入有其分，出有其所，不相干乘而用各足。

translations.literal: In the Rites of Zhou, the celestial treasury holds the rules of the nine punishments to supply the nine standard expenditures—incoming has its allotment, outgoing has its place, they do not encroach on one another and each use is sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou treasury matched nine incomes to nine outlays so none crossed another."

sentences.zh: 各足之後，乃以式貢之餘，供王玩好。

translations.literal: After each was sufficient, then the surplus from the standard tribute supplied the king's playthings.
translations.idiomatic: Only after needs were met did surplus fund the king's pleasures."

sentences.zh: 又上用財，必考于司會。

translations.literal: Moreover when the superior used wealth, he always examined it with the comptroller.
translations.idiomatic: The king's spending passed review by the comptroller."

sentences.zh: 〈會音膾。〉

translations.literal: 〈A marginal note: the word here glossed 'hui' is to be read like 'kuai,' in the sense of the comptroller.〉
translations.idiomatic: A gloss indicates the word is read kuai, referring to the comptroller's office.

sentences.zh: 今陛下所與共坐廊廟治天下者，非三司九列，則臺閣近臣，皆腹心造膝，宜在無諱。

translations.literal: Now those who sit with Your Majesty in the hall to order the realm are, if not the three departments and nine ranks, then the near ministers of the terraces and pavilions—all are heart-and-belly confidants who kneel at your knee and ought to speak without reserve.
translations.idiomatic: Those who share your council are the Nine Ministers or your closest attendants—men who should speak freely."

sentences.zh: 若見豐省而不敢以告，從命奔走，惟恐不勝，是則具臣，非鯁輔也。

translations.literal: If they see plenty or want yet dare not report it, only hasten to obey orders for fear of falling short, they are mere place-holders, not bone-set ministers.
translations.idiomatic: If they see waste yet stay mute, they are seat-fillers, not true counsellors."

sentences.zh: 昔李斯教秦二世曰：「爲人主而不恣睢，命之曰天下桎梏。

translations.literal: Of old Li Si taught the Second Emperor of Qin: "To be lord of men yet not give free rein to whim is called making the realm a prisoner's cangue."
translations.idiomatic: Li Si told Qin Ershi, "A king who does not indulge his whims wears the cangue of empire."

sentences.zh: 」二世用之，秦國以覆，斯亦滅族。

translations.literal: The Second Emperor used this counsel; the state of Qin thereby overturned, and Si's clan was also exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Ershi listened, Qin fell, and Li Si's kin perished with him."

sentences.zh: 是以史遷議其不正諫，而爲世誡。

translations.literal: Therefore Sima Qian judged him for not remonstrating correctly and made him a warning for the age.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Qian condemned him for crooked counsel to warn posterity."

sentences.zh: 書奏，帝覽焉，謂中書監、令曰：「觀隆此奏，使朕懼哉！」

translations.literal: When the memorial was presented, the emperor read it and said to the Supervisor and Director of the Secretariat: "Reading Long's memorial makes me afraid!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read it and told Liu Fang and Sun Zi, "This memorial frightens me."

sentences.zh: 隆疾篤，口占上疏曰：

translations.literal: Long was gravely ill and dictated a memorial:
translations.idiomatic: Gaotang Long, dying, dictated a final memorial:

sentences.zh: 曾子有疾，孟敬子問之。

translations.literal: Master Zeng was ill; Meng Jingzi asked after him.
translations.idiomatic: When Master Zeng lay sick, Meng Jingzi visited him."

sentences.zh: 曾子曰：「鳥之將死，其鳴也哀；

translations.literal: Master Zeng said: "When a bird is about to die, its cry is mournful;
translations.idiomatic: Zengzi said, "A dying bird's call is sad;

sentences.zh: 人之將死，其言也善。

translations.literal: when a man is about to die, his words are good."
translations.idiomatic: a dying man's words are true."

sentences.zh: 」臣寢疾病，有增無損，常懼奄忽，忠款不昭。

translations.literal: " Your servant lies ill; there is increase without improvement; I always fear sudden end, and loyal sincerity will not shine forth.
translations.idiomatic: I lie abed worse each day and fear I may die tonight with my loyalty untold."

sentences.zh: 臣之丹誠，豈惟曾子，願陛下少垂省覽！

translations.literal: Your servant's vermilion loyalty is not only Zengzi's—I pray Your Majesty will briefly lower your gaze and read.
translations.idiomatic: My heart is no less honest than Zengzi's—deign to read."

sentences.zh: 渙然改往事之過謬，勃然興來事之淵塞，使神人嚮應，殊方慕義，四靈效珍，玉衡曜精，則三王可邁，五帝可越，非徒繼體守文而已也。

translations.literal: Melt away the errors of things past, rise with vigor to dredge what lies ahead for coming affairs, so that spirits and men respond in concert, distant regions yearn for righteousness, the four numina offer treasures, and the Jade Scepter constellation gleams—then the Three Kings may be surpassed, the Five Emperors overtaken; it is not merely inheriting the body and guarding the text.
translations.idiomatic: Cast off old mistakes, seize new beginnings, until gods and men answer, distant lands admire you, prodigies appear, and the Dipper shines bright—then you outrun the Three Kings and Five Emperors, far more than "keeping the text."

sentences.zh: 臣常疾世主莫不思紹堯、舜、湯、武之治，而蹈踵桀、紂、幽、厲之跡，莫不蚩笑季世惑亂亡國之主，而不登踐虞、夏、殷、周之軌。

translations.literal: Your servant has always grieved that worldly lords never fail to think of continuing the rule of Yao, Shun, Tang, and Wu, yet tread in the tracks of Jie, Zhou, You, and Li; they never fail to sneer at the deluded rulers who lost states in late ages, yet they do not mount the chariot-road of Yu, Xia, Yin, and Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Rulers always swear to match Yao, Shun, Tang, and Wu, yet walk the path of Jie and Zhou; they mock fallen tyrants yet refuse the ruts of the true sage-kings."

sentences.zh: 悲夫！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!"

sentences.zh: 以若所爲，求若所致，猶緣木求魚，煎水作冰，其不可得，明矣。

translations.literal: With such conduct to seek such an outcome is like climbing a tree to catch a fish or boiling water to make ice—plainly it cannot be gained.
translations.idiomatic: Seeking glory by such means is fishing in a tree or making ice from steam—it cannot work."

sentences.zh: 尋觀三代之有天下也，聖賢相承，歷載數百，尺土莫非其有，一民莫非其臣，萬國咸寧，九有有截；

translations.literal: Looking back, when the Three Dynasties held the realm, sages succeeded one another through hundreds of years; not an inch of soil was not theirs, not a commoner not their subject; the myriad regions were all at peace, the nine provinces had clear bounds;
translations.idiomatic: Under the three dynasties sages handed power through centuries; every clod was theirs, every subject loyal, the nine regions trim;

sentences.zh: 鹿臺之金，巨橋之粟，無所用之，仍舊南面，夫何爲哉！

translations.literal: the gold of the Deer Terrace, the grain of the Giant Bridge, had no use for them—yet still they faced south; what did they need to do!
translations.idiomatic: Deer Terrace gold and Giant Bridge grain went unused—yet they faced south in ease."

sentences.zh: 然癸、辛之徒，恃其旅力，知足以拒諫，才足以飾非，諂諛是尚，臺觀是崇，淫樂是好，倡優是說，作靡靡之樂，安濮上之音。

translations.literal: Yet men like Gui and Xin relied on their hosts' strength, their cleverness enough to reject remonstrance, their talent enough to cloak wrong, exalting flattery, prizing terraces and belvederes, loving dissolute music, delighting in actors and jesters, making decadent music, soothing themselves with the tunes of Pu.
translations.idiomatic: Jie and Zhou trusted brute force, rejected advice, masked fault, flattered favorites, piled towers, drowned in music and players, spun decadent airs from Pu."

sentences.zh: 上天不蠲，眷然回顧，宗國爲墟，下夷于隷，紂縣白旗，桀放鳴條；

translations.literal: High Heaven did not cleanse them; it turned its gaze and looked back—the ancestral state became ruins, they were brought low to slaves; Zhou hung on the white banner, Jie was banished to Mingtiao;
translations.idiomatic: Heaven withdrew favor; capitals turned to dust; kings fell to slaves—Zhou died on the white standard, Jie died in exile;

sentences.zh: 天子之尊，湯、武有之，豈伊異人，皆明王之胄也。

translations.literal: the honor of the Son of Heaven Tang and Wu possessed—were they other men? All were scions of enlightened kings.
translations.idiomatic: yet Tang and Wu took the throne—men of the same royal blood."

sentences.zh: 且當六國之時，天下殷熾，秦旣兼之，不脩聖道，乃構阿房之宮，築長城之守，矜夸中國，威服百蠻，天下震竦，道路以目；

translations.literal: Moreover in the age of the Warring States the realm was rich; once Qin swallowed it, it did not cultivate the sage way but built the Epang Palace and the Long Wall garrison, boasting within China and awing the hundred barbarians until the realm trembled and men exchanged glances on the road.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin united the rich Warring States it built Epang and the Wall, swaggered within China, terrified the tribes, until men dared only whisper."

sentences.zh: 自謂本枝百葉，永垂洪暉，豈寤二世而滅，社稷崩圮哉？

translations.literal: They thought their trunk and branches would flourish forever and shed great radiance—who woke to the Second Generation's ruin and the altars' collapse?
translations.idiomatic: They dreamed their line would branch forever—who foresaw the second reign's crash?"

sentences.zh: 近漢孝武乘文、景之福，外攘夷狄，內興宮殿，十餘年間，天下嚻然。

translations.literal: Near at hand Emperor Wu of Han rode the fortune of Wen and Jing, repelled the barbarians without and raised palaces within; in a decade the realm was in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: Han Wudi spent Wen and Jing's surplus on barbarian wars and palace mania until the empire seethed within ten years."

sentences.zh: 乃信越巫，懟天遷怒，起建章之宮，千門萬戶，卒致江充妖蠱之變，至於宮室乖離，父子相殘，殃咎之毒，禍流數世。

translations.literal: Then he trusted Yue wizards, blamed Heaven and shifted wrath, raised the Weaving Palaces with their thousand gates and myriad doors, until in the end came Jiang Chong's witchcraft affair, so that palace chambers were torn apart and father slew son—the poison of calamity and fault flowed down many reigns.
translations.idiomatic: He then trusted southern shamans, raised Weaving Palaces, and brought Jiang Chong's witch-hunt—palaces turned battlefield, father killed son, and the curse lasted generations."

sentences.zh: 臣觀黃初之際，天兆其戒，異類之鳥，育長燕巢，口爪胷赤，此魏室之大異也，宜防鷹揚之臣於蕭牆之內。

translations.literal: Your servant observes that at the beginning of Huangchu Heaven showed its warning: a bird of strange kind was reared in a swallow's nest in Yan, its beak, claws, and breast red—this was a great anomaly for the house of Wei; one should guard against a hawk-like minister within one's own walls.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangchu a freak chick was raised in a swallow's nest—red beak and breast—a dire omen for Wei: beware a strong minister inside the gate."

sentences.zh: 可選諸王，使君國典兵，往往棊跱，鎮撫皇畿，翼亮帝室。

translations.literal: You may select the various princes, charge them with states and command of troops, station them like chess pieces on a board, pacify the imperial domain, and support the brightening of the imperial house.
translations.idiomatic: Enfeoff princes with troops like chessmen ringing the capital to shield the throne."

sentences.zh: 昔周之東遷，晉、鄭是依，漢呂之亂，實賴朱虛，斯蓋前代之明鑒。

translations.literal: Of old when Zhou moved east, it relied on Jin and Zheng; when the Lü clan troubled Han, it truly depended on the Marquis of Zhu-xu—these are clear mirrors of former ages.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou's eastern move leaned on Jin and Zheng; Han's Lü purge needed Liu Zhang—history's lesson."

sentences.zh: 夫皇天無親，惟德是輔。

translations.literal: High Heaven is not partial; it aids only the virtuous.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven is impartial—it helps the virtuous alone."

sentences.zh: 民詠德政，則延期過歷，下有怨歎，掇錄授能。

translations.literal: When the people sing of virtuous rule, the years are lengthened beyond the tally; when below there is resentment and sighing, the mandate is plucked off and given to the able.
translations.idiomatic: The people's praise lengthens a reign; their groans cost a throne."

sentences.zh: 由此觀之，天下之天下，非獨陛下之天下也。

translations.literal: From this we see: the realm under Heaven is the realm under Heaven—it is not Your Majesty's realm alone.
translations.idiomatic: The empire belongs to the empire—not to you alone."

sentences.zh: 臣百疾所鍾，氣力稍微，輒自輿出，歸還里舍，若遂沈淪，魂而有知，結草以報。

translations.literal: Your servant is struck by a hundred illnesses; my breath is slight; I have had myself carried out and returned to my village house; if I sink into the dark and my soul still has awareness, I will tie grass to repay.
translations.idiomatic: Disease wastes me; I had myself borne home; if I die, my ghost will still tie grass in your debt."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「生廉侔伯夷，直過史魚，執心堅白，謇謇匪躬，如何微疾未除，退身里舍？

translations.literal: An edict said: "In life you matched Boyi for purity, surpassed Shi Yu in straightness, held a heart hard as white jade, remonstrated tirelessly, forgetting self—how can a slight illness remain and you retire to your village house?
translations.idiomatic: The throne answered, "You rival Boyi in purity, surpass Shi Yu in bluntness—how can a passing illness send you home?"

sentences.zh: 昔邴吉以陰德，疾除而延壽；

translations.literal: Of old Bing Ji through hidden virtue had his illness removed and prolonged his years;
translations.idiomatic: Bing Ji's secret virtue cured him;

sentences.zh: 貢禹以守節，疾篤而濟愈。

translations.literal: Gong Yu through guarding integrity, though gravely ill, recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Yu's steadfastness healed his worst sickbed."

sentences.zh: 生其彊飯專精以自持。

translations.literal: Sir, you must force yourself to eat and concentrate your spirit to preserve yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Eat, gather your strength, and endure."

sentences.zh: 」隆卒，遺令薄葬，歛以時服。

translations.literal: " Long died; he left instructions for a thin burial, enshrouded in timely dress.
translations.idiomatic: Gaotang Long died, ordering a plain coffin and the clothes he wore."

sentences.zh: 〈習鑿齒曰：高堂隆可謂忠臣矣。

translations.literal: Xi Zuochi says: Gaotang Long may be called a loyal minister.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Zuochi says Gaotang Long was a true loyal minister.

sentences.zh: 君侈每思諫其惡，將死不忘憂社稷，正辭動於昏主，明戒驗於身後，謇諤足以勵物，德音沒而弥彰，可不謂忠且智乎！

translations.literal: Whenever the ruler grew extravagant he always thought to remonstrate against his evil; facing death he did not forget to worry for the altars of soil and grain; with upright words he moved a benighted lord; clear warnings were verified after his death; his blunt remonstrance was enough to stir things; his virtuous reputation, though gone, grows brighter—can he not be called loyal and wise!
translations.idiomatic: When the court turned extravagant he still rebuked vice; on his deathbed he still fretted for the state; his blunt words stirred a dull sovereign and proved true after he was gone—his voice rings louder in death. What is that if not loyalty and wisdom?"

sentences.zh: 詩云：「聽用我謀，庶無大悔。

translations.literal: The Odes say: "If you heed my plans, perhaps you will have no great regrets."
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Poetry says, "Heed my counsel and you may escape deep regret."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「曾是莫聽，大命以傾。

translations.literal: It also says: "They would not listen at all, and so the great mandate was overturned."
translations.idiomatic: It also says, "They would not listen, and the great mandate collapsed."

sentences.zh: 」其高堂隆之謂也。〉

translations.literal: This is what is meant by Gaotang Long.〉
translations.idiomatic: That is the man Gaotang Long was."

sentences.zh: 初，太和中，中護軍蔣濟上疏曰「宜遵古封禪」。

translations.literal: At the beginning, in the Taihe era, Central Army Protector Jiang Ji submitted a memorial saying "One ought to follow antiquity in performing the feng and shan sacrifices."
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taihe era Jiang Ji of the central guard urged the court to revive the classical feng and shan rites on Mount Tai.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「聞濟斯言，使吾汗出流足。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Hearing Ji's words makes my sweat run to my feet.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered, "Jiang Ji's words set my feet sweating."

sentences.zh: 」事寢歷歲，後遂議脩之，使隆撰其禮儀。

translations.literal: The matter lay dormant for years; afterward they finally debated performing it and ordered Long to draft the ritual protocol.
translations.idiomatic: The plan slept for years, then the court revived it and told Gaotang Long to draft the liturgy."

sentences.zh: 帝聞隆沒，歎息曰：「天不欲成吾事，高堂生舍我亡也。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard that Long had died, he sighed and said: "Heaven does not wish to complete my affair; the Master of the Gaotang line has left me and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaotang Long died, the emperor mourned, "Heaven bars my rite—the man I needed is gone."

sentences.zh: 」子琛嗣爵。

translations.literal: His son Chen inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gaotang Chen inherited the fief.

sentences.zh: 始，景初中，帝以蘇林、秦靜等並老，恐無能傳業者。

translations.literal: At the beginning, in the Jingchu era, the emperor thought Su Lin, Qin Jing, and others were all old and feared there would be none able to transmit their learning.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jingchu the emperor saw Su Lin, Qin Jing, and other masters aging and feared their learning would die with them.

sentences.zh: 乃詔曰：「昔先聖旣沒，而其遺言餘教，著於六藝。

translations.literal: Then an edict said: "Of old, after the former sages had passed away, their surviving words and teachings were fixed in the Six Arts.
translations.idiomatic: He issued an edict: "When the sages died, their teaching lived on in the Six Classics."

sentences.zh: 六藝之文，禮又爲急，弗可斯須離者也。

translations.literal: Among the texts of the Six Arts, the Rites are most urgent; one cannot be parted from them for a moment.
translations.idiomatic: Of those texts the Rites matter most—they cannot be neglected for an instant."

sentences.zh: 末俗背本，所由來乆。

translations.literal: The customs of late ages turn their backs on the root; the source lies far back.
translations.idiomatic: Decadent habit has long turned from the root."

sentences.zh: 故閔子譏原伯之不學，荀卿醜秦世之坑儒，儒學旣廢，則風化曷由興哉？

translations.literal: Therefore Min Zi mocked Yuan Bo for not studying; Xun Qing reviled the burying of scholars in the Qin age—once Confucian learning is abandoned, how can transformation and teaching arise?
translations.idiomatic: Min Zi mocked sloth, Xun Qing cursed Qin's persecution of scholars—without Confucian study, how can manners revive?"

sentences.zh: 方今宿生巨儒，並各年高，教訓之道，孰爲其繼？

translations.literal: Now the veteran scholars and great Confucians are each advanced in years; who will continue the way of instruction?
translations.idiomatic: Our old masters are dying—who will teach the next generation?"

sentences.zh: 昔伏生將老，漢文帝嗣以鼂錯；

translations.literal: Of old when Fu Sheng was growing old, Han Wendi continued him with Chao Cuo;
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Sheng grew old, Wendi sent Chao Cuo to learn from him;

sentences.zh: 穀梁寡疇，宣帝承以十郎。

translations.literal: the Guliang had few transmitters, and Xuandi continued it with ten gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: when the Guliang commentary lacked heirs, Xuandi assigned ten scholars to master it."

sentences.zh: 其科郎吏高才解經義者三十人，從光祿勳隆、散騎常侍林、博士靜，分受四經三禮，主者具爲設課試之法。

translations.literal: Let thirty clerk-officials of high talent who grasp the classics be chosen to follow Supervisor of the Household Long, Regular Attendant Lin, and Erudite Jing, each receiving instruction in the Four Classics and the Three Rites; the presiding offices shall fully set methods of lessons and examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Pick thirty able clerks who know the canon to study under Gaotang Long, Su Lin, and Qin Jing in the Four Books and Three Rites, with formal curricula and exams."

sentences.zh: 夏侯勝有言：『士病不明經術，經術苟明，其取青紫如俯拾地芥耳。

translations.literal: Xiahou Sheng had a saying: "The trouble with scholars is not mastering the classics; once the classics are mastered, taking the purple and blue robes is like stooping to pick weeds from the ground."
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Sheng said, "Scholars fail by not mastering the classics; master them and high office is yours for the picking."

sentences.zh: 』今學者有能究極經道，則爵祿榮寵，不期而至。

translations.literal: Now if scholars can exhaust the way of the classics, then rank, stipend, glory, and favor will come without being sought.
translations.idiomatic: Today whoever masters the canon will win rank and honor unsought."

sentences.zh: 可不勉哉！

translations.literal: Can they not strive!
translations.idiomatic: Let them strive!"

sentences.zh: 」數年，隆等皆卒，學者遂廢。

translations.literal: " After several years, Long and the others all died, and the scholars' undertaking then lapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years Gaotang Long and the rest were dead, and the school project died with them."

sentences.zh: 初，任城棧潛，太祖世歷縣令，

translations.literal: At the beginning, Zhan Qian of Rencheng, in the era of the Grand Progenitor successively served as county magistrate,
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the main biographies comes Zhan Qian of Rencheng, who under Cao Cao served as a series of county magistrates

sentences.zh: 〈潛字彥皇，見應璩《書林》。〉

translations.literal: 〈Qian's courtesy name was Yanhuang; he appears in Ying Qu's Forest of Letters.〉
translations.idiomatic: His courtesy name was Yanhuang, as Ying Qu's Forest of Letters records."

sentences.zh: 嘗督守鄴城。

translations.literal: He once supervised the defense of Ye city.
translations.idiomatic: He once commanded the defense of Ye.

sentences.zh: 時文帝爲太子，耽樂田獵，晨出夜還。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Wen was heir apparent and indulged in field hunting, going out at dawn and returning at night.
translations.idiomatic: While the heir Cao Pi was addicted to the chase, riding out at dawn and back past dark,

sentences.zh: 潛諫曰：「王公設險以固其國，都城禁衞，用戒不虞。

translations.literal: Qian remonstrated: "The kingly duke sets defenses to secure his state; the capital's guards exist to guard against the unforeseen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan Qian warned him, "Walls and guards exist to secure the capital and guard against surprise."

sentences.zh: 大雅云：『宗子維城，無俾城壞。

translations.literal: The Greater Elegantiae say: 'The eldest son is the wall; do not let the wall crumble.'
translations.idiomatic: The Odes say, "The heir is the city wall—do not let it crumble."

sentences.zh: 』又曰：『猶之未遠，是用大簡。

translations.literal: They also say: 'The fault is not yet far—therefore we use great simplicity.'
translations.idiomatic: They add, "The fault is still near—so apply stern simplicity."

sentences.zh: 』若逸于遊田，晨出昏歸，以一日從禽之娛，而忘無垠之釁，愚竊惑之。

translations.literal: If you indulge in hunting, going out at dawn and returning at dusk, for the pleasure of a single day's chase forgetting measureless peril—I foolishly find this perplexing.
translations.idiomatic: To risk the realm for one day's sport baffles me."

sentences.zh: 」太子不恱，然自後游出差簡。

translations.literal: The heir apparent was not pleased, yet afterward his hunting outings were somewhat reduced.
translations.idiomatic: The heir was annoyed, but his hunts grew rarer afterward.

sentences.zh: 黃初中，文帝將立郭貴嬪爲皇后，潛上疏諫，語在

translations.literal: In the Huang-chu era, when Emperor Wen was about to establish Concubine Guo as empress, Qian submitted a memorial remonstrating; as to his words, they are recorded in
translations.idiomatic: In Huangchu, when Wen meant to raise Lady Guo to empress, Zhan Qian remonstrated; the text of his memorial stands in

sentences.zh: 〈后妃傳〉

translations.literal: 〈the "Biographies of Empresses and Consorts."〉
translations.idiomatic: the "Biographies of Empresses and Consorts."
See that chapter for the full wording.

sentences.zh: 明帝時，衆役並興，戚屬疏斥，潛上疏曰：

translations.literal: In Emperor Ming's time, when many corvées arose at once and kinsmen of the imperial house were kept at a distance, Qian submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming, as labor levies multiplied and imperial kin were sidelined, Zhan Qian wrote:

sentences.zh: 天生蒸民而樹之君，所以覆燾羣生，熈育兆庶，故方制四海匪爲天子，裂土分疆匪爲諸侯也。

translations.literal: Heaven bore the teeming people and set up rulers for them in order to shelter all living things and nurture the myriad commoners—therefore the four seas are bounded not for the Son of Heaven alone, and territory is divided not for the feudal lords alone.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven made the people and set rulers over them to shelter and feed them—the realm is not the emperor's private estate nor the fiefs the nobles' playthings alone."

sentences.zh: 始自三皇，爰曁唐、虞，咸以愽濟加于天下，醇德以洽，黎元賴之。

translations.literal: Beginning with the Three August Ones down to Tang and Yu, all broadly aided the realm below and joined it with pure virtue, and the black-haired people relied on them.
translations.idiomatic: From the Three Sovereigns through Yao and Shun, kings aided all under Heaven with simple virtue, and the people leaned on them."

sentences.zh: 三王旣微，降逮于漢，治日益少，喪亂弘多，自時厥後，亦罔克乂。

translations.literal: The Three Kings declined; descending to Han, good order grew ever scarcer and great disorder ever greater; from that time onward, none could again bring peace.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Kings waned; by Han order thinned and chaos thickened, and no later reign matched the sages."

sentences.zh: 太祖濬哲神武，芟除暴亂，克復王綱，以開帝業。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor was profound, wise, and divinely martial; he cut away violence and chaos, restored the kingly net, and thereby opened the imperial enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao was wise and martial: he swept away rebels, restored the royal pattern, and founded your line."

sentences.zh: 文帝受天明命，廓恢皇基，踐阼七載，每事未遑。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen received Heaven's bright mandate, widened and restored the imperial foundation; in the seven years since ascending the throne, on each matter there was no leisure.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen took Heaven's mandate, widened the base, yet seven years on the throne left every task unfinished."

sentences.zh: 陛下聖德，纂承洪緒，宜崇晏晏，與民休息。

translations.literal: Your Majesty in sage virtue inherits the great thread; you ought to honor tranquillity and let the people rest.
translations.idiomatic: You inherit his work in sage virtue—you should prize peace and let the people breathe."

sentences.zh: 而方隅匪寧，征夫遠戍，有事海外，縣旌萬里，六軍騷動，水陸轉運，百姓舍業，日費千金。

translations.literal: Yet the corners of the realm are not tranquil, soldiers stand guard far away, there are affairs beyond the seas, banners fly ten thousand li, the six hosts are in turmoil, transport goes by water and land, the hundred surnames abandon their occupations, and a thousand in gold is spent each day.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the frontiers boil, armies camp overseas, fleets and carts drain the treasury, and commoners abandon their trades while costs mount daily."

sentences.zh: 大興殿舍，功作萬計，徂來之松，刊山窮谷，怪石珷玞，浮于河、淮，都圻之內，盡爲甸服，當供稾秸銍粟之調，而爲苑囿擇禽之府，盛林莽之穢，豐鹿兎之藪；

translations.literal: Palace halls rise on a grand scale; works number in the myriads; pines from Culai are hewn in mountain valleys; strange stones from riverbeds float down the Yellow and Huai; within the capital region all has become royal domain that ought to supply hay, straw, and grain levies, yet it is made a preserve for choosing birds; thickets and marshes abound, runs for deer and rabbits multiply;
translations.idiomatic: You raise halls without count, haul timber from Culai and stone down the rivers, turn the whole capital district—meant for grain tribute—into hunting parks thick with scrub and game pens;

sentences.zh: 傷害農功，地繁茨棘，災疫流行，民物大潰，上減和氣，嘉禾不植。

translations.literal: they harm farming, the ground bristles with brambles, plague spreads, people and goods collapse in ruin, harmonious vapor wanes above, and lucky grain will not grow.
translations.idiomatic: farms are ruined, thorns choke the soil, pestilence spreads, harmony flees the skies, and the lucky grain will not sprout."

sentences.zh: 臣聞文王作豐，經始勿亟，百姓子來，不日而成。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that when King Wen built Feng, he planned the start without haste, and the hundred surnames came like children, completing it in no time.
translations.idiomatic: King Wen built Feng without haste, and the people flocked to finish it overnight."

sentences.zh: 靈沼、靈囿，與民共之。

translations.literal: The Spirit Pond and Spirit Park he shared with the people.
translations.idiomatic: He shared his Spirit Pond and Park with the commoners."

sentences.zh: 今宮觀崇侈，彫鏤極妙，忘有虞之總期，思殷辛之瓊室，禁地千里，舉足投網，麗擬阿房，役百乾谿，臣恐民力彫盡，下不堪命也。

translations.literal: Now belvederes and towers are lofty and carved to utmost subtlety; forgetting Shun's single-minded planning, you think of Zhou of Shang's carnelian chambers; forbidden ground stretches a thousand li, every step falls into a net; splendor rivals Epang, corvée outdoes the dry gully of Chu—your servant fears the people's strength is exhausted and those below cannot bear the command.
translations.idiomatic: Today your towers outshine Shun's thrift and copy Zhou of Shang's jade halls; closed parks span a thousand li; splendor rivals Epang; labor outdoes King Ling's dry trench—I fear the people are spent and cannot obey."

sentences.zh: 昔秦據殽函以制六合，自以德高三皇，功兼五帝，欲號謚至萬葉，而二世顛覆，願爲黔首，由枝幹旣杌，本實先拔也。

translations.literal: Of old Qin held Yao and Han passes to control the six directions, deeming its virtue higher than the Three August Ones and its merit embracing the Five Emperors, wishing its title to last ten thousand generations—yet the Second Generation overturned and it wished to be a black-headed commoner, because the branches were broken and the root was pulled up first.
translations.idiomatic: Qin held the passes, boasted past all sage-kings, dreamed eternal rule—yet the second reign collapsed, for the trunk was sawn through at the root."

sentences.zh: 蓋聖王之御世也，克明俊德，庸勳親親；

translations.literal: As for the sage king's governing the age, he could brighten lofty virtue and employ merit and cherish kin;
translations.idiomatic: The sage king brightens virtue, rewards merit, cherishes kin;

sentences.zh: 俊乂在官，則功業可隆，親親顯用，則安危同憂；

translations.literal: when outstanding men hold office, great deeds can be exalted; when kin are honored and employed, safety and danger are shared in one sorrow;
translations.idiomatic: when worthies serve, glory rises; when kin share power, the house weathers storm together;

sentences.zh: 深根固本，並爲幹翼，雖歷盛衰，內外有輔。

translations.literal: deep roots and firm trunk together become stem and wing—though prosperity and decline alternate, there are helpers within and without.
translations.idiomatic: deep roots and strong limbs brace the throne through rise and fall."

sentences.zh: 昔成王幼沖，未能莅政，周、呂、召、畢，並在左右；

translations.literal: Of old King Cheng was young and could not yet attend to government; the Zhou, Lü, Shao, and Bi all stood at his side;
translations.idiomatic: King Cheng was a child, yet the Duke of Zhou, the Grand Duke, Shao, and Bi guarded him;

sentences.zh: 今旣無衞侯、康叔之監，分陝所任，又非旦、奭。

translations.literal: now there are neither supervisors like the Marquis of Wei and Uncle Kang nor a division of Shaan like Dan and Shi.
translations.idiomatic: today you have no such guardians, no second line like the Duke of Zhou and Shi."

sentences.zh: 東宮未建，天下無副。

translations.literal: The eastern palace is not yet established; the realm lacks an heir.
translations.idiomatic: No heir apparent is named—the empire has no second pillar."

sentences.zh: 願陛下留心關塞，永保無極，則海內幸甚。

translations.literal: I pray Your Majesty give heed to the passes and frontiers, forever preserve the boundless—then within the seas there will be great fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Watch the frontiers, secure the succession, and the realm will count itself blessed."

sentences.zh: 後爲燕中尉，辭疾不就，卒。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed marshal of Yan but declined on grounds of illness and did not take office; he died.
translations.idiomatic: He was later named marshal of Yan but pleaded illness, never took the post, and died.

translations.literal: 【Appraisal】
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal

sentences.zh: 評曰：辛毗、楊阜，剛亮公直，正諫匪躬，亞乎汲黯之高風焉。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: Xin Pi and Yang Fu were hard, bright, and upright, remonstrating bluntly without sparing themselves—next in stature to the high bearing of Ji An.
translations.idiomatic: The historian concludes: Xin Pi and Yang Fu were blunt as Ji An, remonstrating at personal risk.

sentences.zh: 高堂隆學業脩明，志在匡君，因變陳戒，發於懇誠，忠矣哉！

translations.literal: Gaotang Long's learning was cultivated and clear, his intent set on aiding his lord; he seized on portents to offer warnings, issuing from earnest sincerity—loyal indeed!
translations.idiomatic: Gaotang Long mastered the classics and served his ruler with portent and plea—loyal indeed."

sentences.zh: 及至必改正朔，俾魏祖虞，所謂意過其通者歟！

translations.literal: Yet when it came to insisting on changing the calendar's first month and making Wei the heir of Yu—may that not be a case where intention exceeded what was fitting!
translations.idiomatic: Yet his zeal to change the calendar and cast Wei as Yu's heir may have overshot good sense."
